White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt is stepping down from her role at the end of August, a surprise announcement after her return to the White House less than a month ago following maternity leave.

Leavitt “will be departing her role at the end of the month so she can spend more time with her beautiful young children and family, a decision I totally understand and respect,” President Donald Trump wrote Wednesday on Truth Social.

Trump’s combative spokesperson will be one of the president’s “top outside advisors,” he added, “and an influential voice within the Republican Party, as we work to defy History, and conclusively win the Midterm Elections.”

Leavitt, 28, called her time in the role — which has been marked by fierce loyalty to the president and explosive briefings — the “honor and adventure of a lifetime.”

In a lengthy statement on X, Leavitt claimed the U.S. is facing an “existential threat from an increasingly extremist Democrat Party that seeks to destroy everything great about America” as she embraced her upcoming role as a “top advisor” to the president “on the outside” as well as a “vocal advocate for MAGA and the Republican Party.

open image in gallery Donald Trump’s surprise announcement of the departure of White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt comes just weeks after she returned to the briefing room after maternity leave ( Getty )

Her departure was announced one day after the Department of Justice’s Office of Legal Counsel issued a stunning memo arguing that the president could claim executive privilege over communication between him and his “private advisers” if those conversations were considered confidential and related to his presidential “decisionmaking.”

Leavitt has held only one press briefing since returning to the White House from maternity leave last month, approximately eight weeks after the birth of her second child. She also has a two-year-old son.

“Being a mother and welcoming a new baby while working in one of the most demanding jobs in the world has been the most rewarding yet challenging season of my life, to say the least,” Leavitt wrote Wednesday.

“The truth is since returning to the White House after the birth of my daughter, I have felt in my heart that I cannot be the best mom my two young children deserve while devoting the constant time, energy, and attention required of the White House Press Secretary — and that is why I have ultimately made the bittersweet decision to depart the White House and embark on a new chapter in my life,” she said.

open image in gallery Leavitt, the youngest person to serve as White House press secretary, will transition to one of the president’s outside advisors, a role that the Department of Justice now says is shielded by executive privilege ( AP )

The New Hampshire native entered the White House as Trump’s top spokesperson after serving as a national press secretary on his 2024 presidential campaign.

She also served as a press assistant during the last year of his first term and later as communications director for New York Rep. Elise Stefanik before embarking on an ill-fated campaign for House seat in the Granite State.

Her tenure as White House press secretary has encompassed nearly two full years of Trump’s second term, making her his longest-serving press secretary across his two non-consecutive terms. She is also the youngest person to ever serve in the role.

It remains unclear who will step into the role.

The announcement of Leavitt’s exit from the administration also follows explosive reporting that the president covertly boarded a separate plane after leaving a NATO summit in Turkey last month, leaving several top administration officials and the press traveling with him inside Air Force One while he traveled with Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth and a handful of close aides on a smaller plane.

Leavitt did not travel with the president on that trip, but a traveling press pool joined State Secretary Marco Rubio, among others, onboard an older Air Force One to avoid potential threats from Iran.

U.S. intelligence officials reportedly identified threats from Iranian surface-to-air missiles and a potential shoulder-fired missile before Trump secretly swapped planes, which was not known to government officials, the press or public until this week.

That intelligence appeared to be deemed credible enough for the Secret Service to launch a covert operation to sneak Trump and senior members of his team into a smaller plane, while leaving other officials, and reporters, in the decoy jet.

Leavitt’s departure also comes after several other shifts inside White House communications. Former Homeland Security spokeswoman Lauren Bis is now senior White House deputy press secretary, and White House deputy press secretary Abigail Jackson left the administration last month to work for OnMessage Public Strategies.

News.content:

Millions of Britons took a once-in-a-generation opportunity to view the best solar eclipse in decades as the moon obscured more than 90 per cent of the sun.

Crowds of skywatchers descended on viewing spots, including the Royal Observatory in Greenwich, London, and Calton Hill, Edinburgh, to witness the rare phenomenon that will not be seen again until the end of this century.

People uttered gasps of “wow”, “oh my god” and “this is so cool” as they saw the moon blot out much of the sun and the world grew darker.

open image in gallery More than 90 per cent of the sun was covered ( Getty )

One couple even scheduled their wedding a year in advance to coincide with the event.

An eclipse happens when the moon passes in front of the sun, obscuring its light and producing a stunning ring of what looks like fire around the lunar surface.

Wednesday evening’s event was the most the sun had been blocked over the UK since the total eclipse in 1999.

People used eclipse glasses, colanders or viewers made from cereal boxes to avoid eye damage from looking directly at the sun.

Shops, national parks and the Royal Greenwich Observatory all sold out of the special glasses.

open image in gallery Parts of Spain were plunged into total darkness ( Getty )

The Royal Greenwich Observatory sold 15,000 pairs of eclipse glasses a month.

John Lewis said colander sales had risen nearly 40 per cent in a year. Nasa recommended colanders as a way to watch the eclipse by viewing the shadows it casts on the ground.

After the 1999 total solar eclipse, the Royal College of Ophthalmologists reported around 70 cases of people having sight problems after looking at the sun as the moon moved.

Veronica Orozco, who popped a champagne cork as she watched with her neighbours in Greenwich Park, said it was a magical moment. “I am sitting here with my neighbours and we have been telling each other ‘Happy Eclipse Day’,” she said.

open image in gallery The eclipse was refracted from binoculars and seen on paper ( AFP/Getty )

Britain’s electricity grid operator cancelled its call to the industry to generate more power during Wednesday evening’s solar eclipse.

The National Energy System Operator (Neso) had feared a massive surge in demand as people across the UK returned indoors, switching on lights and appliances, after being outside to view the eclipse.

The 1999 eclipse caused the largest sudden increase in demand on record.

A Neso spokesman said the notice had been issued “as a precautionary measure to the market due to the solar eclipse”.

Jerry and Jamie Bone had planned their wedding at Alpheton in Suffolk for over a year so they could get married on eclipse day.

The couple provided special glasses and filters for guests to view the event.

People in Cornwall saw the highest proportion of the sun covered.

open image in gallery Greenwich Park, London, was full of people wearing special glasses to look up ( Getty )

While the eclipse was only partial in the UK, it was total in other parts of the world, such as Valencia in Spain, which were plunged into darkness.

Dhara Patel, a space expert at the National Space Centre, said it was incredible to witness the event. “What’s really nice is it’s a way for lots of people to come together and connect with nature – looking up at the sky at objects that we typically tend to take for granted,” she said.

“For a lot of people, it can be a little bit of an emotional event. I’ve seen previously people being drawn to tears or just have a really good moment within themselves where they realise they’re seeing or witnessing something… you’ve never seen before in your life.”

The next major eclipse is due in 2081, when 99 per cent of the sun will be obscured by the moon.

open image in gallery Sun thing special: The eclipse seen beside Big Ben, London ( AFP/Getty )

In an added bonus for stargazers, the annual Perseid meteor shower reaches its peak on Wednesday night.

The shower is produced as Earth ploughs through a stream of dust left behind by Comet Swift–Tuttle.

Each tiny grain strikes Earth’s atmosphere at about 60km per second, burning up in a brief flash that takes the appearance of a shooting star.

News.title: Everton dispatch Newcastle to give Matthias Jaissle a reality check

Newcastle 1 Everton 3

Everton appear well ahead of Newcastle United in their preparation for the new Premier League season after a comfortable 3-1 victory at Murrayfield.

On a sobering evening for new Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle, who changed all 10 outfield players at half-time, Everton’s one and two-touch attacking play proved difficult to contain.

Everton took the lead through Thierno Barry after a defensive error from Sven Botman, before Iliman Ndiaye scored a penalty that was won cheaply by summer signing Hayden Hackney.

News.title: Ebola outbreak ‘doubling every 20 days’, warns UN chief
News.content:
Congo’s runaway Ebola outbreak is doubling in size every 20 days, according to the United Nations humanitarian chief, putting it on track to soon be the largest ever seen.

Three months after the outbreak was officially declared, the case load is expanding exponentially and many believe the true toll is far higher than recorded.

If cases continue to double at the same rate, the flare-up in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) will surpass the record West African outbreak sometime around the end of September.

Modelling by one health analytics firm already predicts there is a more than 90 per cent chance that the DRC will become the largest on record.

The two-year West African outbreak grew to more than 28,600 cases and 11,325 deaths across Sierra Leone, Liberia and Guinea from late 2013 to 2016.

This year’s outbreak centred on the DRC province of Ituri has already seen 4,449 cases and 2,061 deaths in only a few months.

News.title: Madagascar forced to divide and share mpox vaccine as epidemic takes off
News.content:
Authorities in Madagascar are being forced to split single vaccines into fifths to try to protect as many people as possible during an ongoing mpox outbreak.

The method, known as “fractional dosing”, is authorised by the World Health Organization (WHO) in emergencies when there are critical vaccine shortages, but is not routinely recommended and carries a level of risk.

Madagascar, the African island with a population of roughly 33 million people, is currently battling its largest-ever outbreak of the virus formerly known as monkeypox, with at least 4,000 cases recorded so far.

Another one million people are thought to be at risk of contracting clade 1b mpox, a fast-spreading strain of the virus that emerged from the Democratic Republic of the Congo in late 2023.

High risk groups include sex workers, young children, and people living with HIV/Aids. Medical workers are also at risk.

“Public health authorities in Madagascar have been given too few doses to protect the at-risk population; they were initially given 30,000 doses in May, and a subsequent 30,000 have just arrived at the end of July,” said Akhil Bansal, a doctor of internal medicine working on the mpox response in Madagascar and a policy fellow at the Centre for Global Development.

“However, we need to vaccinate more than one million people, so we have been “fractionally dosing”, or splitting vaccines, into fifths, to stretch the supply as far as we can.

“This is a somewhat established approach for vaccines, but even then, the number of doses we have is insufficient,” said Dr Bansal.

News.title: Sudan exodus threatens humanitarian catastrophe in Chad
News.content:
Trapped in a desert encampment in Chad, Abakar Adam, 70, dreams of returning to his small farm in neighbouring Sudan, nearby to the village where he was born.

But Mr Adam can’t go home.

Hidden from sight, he watched soldiers set fire to his farmhouse and slaughter his livestock three years ago. One month later, after resettling in the city of El Geneina in West Darfur he heard 40mm grenades rain down on hospitals while patients fought for their lives inside and witnessed civilians executed in the street.

Shortly after, a bullet from the rifle of a Rapid Support Force (RSF) soldier ripped through his gut, and he recalls how he struggled to pull his daughter from the blood-soaked sand after her eye was gouged out by a militiaman during their escape from Sudan.

Now, sitting outside his rotting, wooden shelter in eastern Chad, just 20 miles from the border with Sudan, he tells The Telegraph that he can’t forget the faces of the blind and disabled who he witnessed being thrown onto piles of hay and burnt alive.

Adam’s story is not unique and the refugee camp where he finds himself with tens of thousands of others is on the brink of collapse.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football 2026/27: Everything you need to know and FAQs
News.content:
What’s new for 2026/27?





You’ll need to re-register

When signing up to Telegraph Fantasy Football this season you will notice your old logins do not work.

New for this season you will need to register, or login to an existing, telegraph.co.uk account to play.

NOTE: you do not need to subscribe in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football - it is free to play.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



We’ve had a makeover and Leagues have moved

Over the summer we changed game provider meaning the site was built again from scratch. We hope you like the new look and feel.

We know nobody likes change, but take your time to get to know the new layout as some aspects of the site may have moved slightly.

The most notable change is that Leagues are now created and joined below your team selection.



Back to basics

With such a short space of time to get the TFF live for this season, the game has been stripped back to basics.

You’ll notice there are no Public Leagues and no prizes for Weekly and Monthly Leaderboard winners. Assistant Manager has also not been integrated for launch.



The Fixture Tracker

Whilst the game has been stripped back to basics, you’ll notice a new fixture tracker above your team selection. This is there to help you make transfer decisions and we hope you like it.

When you see a + in the tracker it indicates how many other games start at that time.



No rule changes.

Whilst some things may have changed, the rules remain unchanged.

Telegraph Fantasy Football is fantasy football at its purest. No gimmicks, no boosts, no captains. Simply pick the best XI players you can.



Assists

However, one exception is this season assists will no longer follow Opta’s “Fantasy Assist” definition and revert back to standard assists.



Did you miss it? League Cup fixtures and five more transfers

In case you missed it last year, this season will also feature League Cup fixtures meaning all competitive domestic football containing Premier League fixtures will count towards your Telegraph Fantasy Football points tally.

Why the change? Well for years the general advice early in the season is to hold onto your transfers and we thought that was getting a bit stale. With League Cup fixtures starting as early as Game Week 3 some seasons, you’d be a fool not to take advantage of some fixture gains against lower-league opposition.

To help with the additional fixtures we have also added five more transfers to your season total.



Paid leagues are no more

Unfortunately Plucky Paid Leagues are not integrated this season.



Three new teams

Ipswich are no strangers to Telegraph Fantasy Football as they both return from relegations in 2025. They bring with them a host of talent including two big names you might recognise, including Jaden Philogene (£2.9m) and Leif Davis (£2.6m).

It has been a fair few years since Hull City (2016/17) and Coventry City (2000/01) last featured in Telegraph Fantasy Football - memories may even flood back of posting in your transfers for the Sky Blues’ players. Both clubs are favourites to go down, but with some exciting signings like Tzolakis (£2.5m) and Thomas-Asante (£2.7m) they will certainly put up a fight.

Start creating your team >



FAQs





When does Telegraph Fantasy Football start?

The 2026/27 edition of Telegraph Fantasy Football will launch in the two weeks leading up to the start of the Premier League. The scoring will commence on Friday August 21, 2026 at 8pm when the Premier League champions Arsenal host Coventry.



How do I register for Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You will need to create a new, or use your existing telegraph.co.uk account in order to play Telegraph Fantasy Football. Simply click “SIGN UP”, then “Continue with Telegraph” and you will be temporarily taken to telegraph.co.uk to login with your existing Telegraph account or create a new account, before automatically returning back to the Telegraph Fantasy Football site.

Note: this account is not the same as your account from previous Telegraph Fantasy Football seasons.

Having trouble making a new account or logging in to an existing telegraph.co.uk account? Click here and look at our troubleshooting guide that can guide you through the process.



How much does it cost to play Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Telegraph Fantasy Football is completely free to play. All managers compete for the £5,000 prize pool as well the chance to challenge friends, family, colleagues and fellow managers in private mini-leagues.



How many players can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You only have to pick a squad of XI players in Telegraph Fantasy Football. With no bench to rely on, finding players who get minutes on the pitch is key and we help you out there by allowing transfers right up until every kick-off.



How many teams can I pick in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can create up to five teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football with a budget of £50m for each, meaning you have a better chance of being in contention for the prizes come the end of the season if some of your selections prove to be unsuccessful.



How many transfers can I make in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Up until the first game on Friday August 21, 2025, there is a transfer amnesty, meaning you can make as many changes as you like. After the season has started you have 45 transfers for the whole campaign with a maximum of five per Game Week (00:00 Tuesday to 23:59 Monday).





How do I join a private league in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Leagues have now moved below your team selection.

This should make it easier for managers to see which league the team is in that they are making changes to.

To join a league click “Join a league” and then add the 6 digit code that the League Chairman will have access to.

To create a league click “Create a league”, name the league and then copy the league code generated to share with your fellow managers.

League Chairmen will have the ability to lock and unlock a league to new joiners.



Do ALL Cup games count in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

Yes. All League Cup fixtures plus all FA Cup games involving Premier League sides count towards your TFF points tally. This adds a great dimension to the game as you will want to load your teams with players who make the latter stages for an advantage over your competitors. However, one thing to note is that penalty shoot-outs do not count towards your score.



How many players are in Telegraph Fantasy Football?

You can expect to compete against more than 100,000 other teams in Telegraph Fantasy Football – a vast but tight-knit community of players where you have every chance of winning one of our many prizes on offer throughout the year.

We aim to include every player in a squad who has a chance of getting some game time. From time to time we may miss a youngster on debut, but rest assured they will soon be added to the player list and feel free to let us know on Facebook or Twitter if you feel someone is missing.

Having technical issues with TFF? Check our Troubleshooting page for help.



What else do I need to know?



Get your strategy right. Getting the balance of your team right can be a tricky business, especially with limited funds, but there are a few tried and trusted methods that will stand you in good stead:



Pick regular starters

Okay, so this isn’t always straightforward in the world of squad rotation where world-class players routinely find themselves sitting on the bench. That said, there are certain players who, if fit, are almost always the first name on the team sheet. Think Bruno Fernandes at Manchester United, Jordan Pickford for Everton and Liverpool’s Virgil van Dijk.



Find a couple of budget ‘gems’

Igor Thiago, Nico O’Reilly and James Garner were among a crop of players who began last term in the ‘unfancied’ category and were must-have ‘enablers’ by the time the season was over. If you’re able to identify one or two of this type of player early in the season, you could be on to a winner.



Be transfer savvy

We’ve all been there – you spend hours selecting your team for the big kick-off then half of them don’t start, the other half have stinkers and your star striker gets a season-ending injury. If you do get off to a slow start, don’t panic. Lurching from one strategy to another could do more harm than good, wasting precious transfers in the process. Trust your instincts, tweak where necessary and the points will come.



Read our weekly Selection Guide

The best advice comes from experts at the Fantasy Football Hub who make our weekly selection guide a prolific source of Telegraph Fantasy Football tips and Telegraph Fantasy Football match facts.

If you subscribe to the weekly newsletter this will hit your inbox on Friday around lunchtime; alternatively it can be found on our social channels or Telegraph Fantasy Football content hub.



Telegraph Fantasy Football Player List

We aim to keep our player list up to date with all comings and goings in the transfer window and the first place to look is our trusted Stats Centre. However, if you fancy yourself as a bit of a Telegraph Fantasy Football expert like the team at Fantasy Football Hub, you can find a player list below in a spreadsheet format so you can do your own analysis.

On the document simply click “file”, then “make a copy” and you will have your own version of the player list at that time to edit as you please.



Download the Telegraph Fantasy Football App

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football: transfers explained and top transfer tips
News.content:
As the new Telegraph Fantasy Football season approaches, the fantasy football experts at Fantasy Football Hub will continue to bring you the very best in fantasy football knowledge, tips and tools to help you rise up the ranks and win your mini-leagues.

To join the Hub and get access to all their great resources and expert tips you can take advantage of its 50% pre-season discount here.



Transfers explained



A good place to start is by explaining the Telegraph Fantasy Football rules on transfers. First thing to note is the pre-season transfer amnesty, so you can make unlimited changes to your teams right up until the first scheduled kick-off on Friday 21 August, 20:00.

45 is the magic number of transfers you receive during the season, five more than last season to help negotiate the new League Cup fixtures. This equates to a little more than one a week. You can use a maximum of five transfers in any Game Week which run from 00:00 on Tuesdays to 23:59 on Mondays.

Four seasons ago we scrapped the two-hour rule, meaning you can make transfers right up until a game kicks off. However, we don’t suggest you leave it that late as if a transfer is not completed in time you will not gain any points for the game from the player transferred in. Starting XIs are released an hour before kick-off so you have an ample window to implement any changes.

Scrapping the two-hour rule also means that this year you can be more flexible with your transfers each week. Once a player’s game has started you will amass their points for the entire game and are free to transfer them out for another player who may be kicking off while the previous game is being played, thus benefiting from two players’ points.



Top transfer strategy tips



1) Utilise fixture gains



Telegraph Fantasy Football is unique amongst other fantasy games in that you can transfer a player out as soon as they’ve played for a player yet to play that day or match week. So if Haaland (£8.3m) played in the 12.30pm Saturday kick-off, managers can transfer him out for Saka (£6.0m) who plays in the 3pm kick-off, and score points for both. Picking up extra fixtures each time a transfer is made is key to TFF success.



2) Find enablers early and stick



To fit in a combination of Erling Haaland (£8.3m), Bruno Fernandes (£6.5m) and Cole Palmer (£6.2m) or similar, requires TFF managers to find cheaper players to balance teams. Finding those players early into the season, and sticking with them to utilise transfers on the other strategy tips, can ensure avoiding wasting transfers on constant restructuring of squads.



3) FA Cup and League Cup (new for 2025/26)

Players in TFF gain points for the League Cup and FA Cup as well as the Premier League, so often players topping points charts at the season end have progressed far in the competition. When seeing lineups for early League Cup and FA Cup Rounds, if big hitting players who are regulars in the league start against lowly opposition, it’s a prime opportunity to stock up on those assets.

New for this season League Cup fixtures have been included which will make the early stages of the season even more exciting when Premier League teams who are not competing in Europe will gain a fixture against the rest.



4) Favourable fixture runs

Picking players who are playing against weaker opposition often score more points, therefore keeping an eye on the fixtures for teams is important.



5) Balance transfers out over the season

There are ~37 gameweeks in the season, so averaging around one transfer a week is a rule of thumb that keeps managers from running out early. The start of the season is the only time your team is reset, so it’s important to set a structure that works for you so that you don’t need to use too many moves at the start to identify those players who are likely to shine. It’s a marathon, not a sprint, so keeping pace early isn’t a necessity, and often keeping a few extra back until the end run sees TFF managers get a late boost.

News.title: Telegraph Fantasy Football points: a complete guide to scoring
News.content:
How many points for a Goal?

A regular source of goals is often the first thing a manager looks for in a fantasy football team. The highly-priced Erling Haaland is a go-to signing for many, but last season saw the continuation of mid-priced forwards getting in on the action too with the likes of Igor Thiago racking up 22 goals in Telegraph Fantasy Football.

Players get five points per goal scored which, added to starting appearance points (two), mean a regularly starting goal scorer can be a huge asset.



How many points for an Assist?

It won’t take a master tactician to work out that players who rank highly in the goalscoring charts often also feature in the upper echelons of the Assists table.

Bruno Fernandes was head and shoulders above the rest with regard to assist points last season with 21 in total (nine clear of his closest rival).

An assist will earn three points.





What counts as an Assist?

An Assist is the final touch (pass, pass-cum-shot or any other touch) leading to the recipient of the ball scoring a goal.

Outside of fantasy football, if the final touch is deflected by an opposition player, the initiator is only given a goal assist if the receiving player was likely to receive the ball without the deflection having taken place. Own goals, directly taken free kicks, direct corner goals and penalties do not get an assist awarded.

In a change to previous years, Fantasy Assists are not being used.



How many points for a Tackle?

A slightly more nuanced aspect of scoring is the points a player earns for a successful tackle. Managers will need to cast their nets wide to capitalise on tackling points as the highest scorers tend to come from mid-table and even lower-table teams.

Everton’s James Garner was a key beneficiary of tackle bonus points last season with 120 tackles in total. His closest rivals have been very popular this summer with Wolves’ Joao Gomes, now at Aston Villa, and Nottingham Forest’s Elliot Anderson, now at Manchester City. It’s clear from this that deeper lying midfielders are more likely to amass points here.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made during a match and only midfielders are eligible.



What counts as a Tackle?

A tackle is defined as a player connecting with the ball in a ground challenge and successfully taking the ball away from the player in possession. The tackled player must have clearly been in possession of the ball before the tackle was made.

The final destination of the ball (to the tackler, to a teammate, to an opposition player or out of play) is not considered. A tackle will only be deemed unsuccessful if the player tackled retains possession of the ball.

A player cutting out a pass does not count as a tackle.

Players earn a point for every two tackles made.



How many points for a Clean Sheet?

Attainable by goalkeepers and defenders, the top-scorers in the clean sheet category last season mostly came from Arsenal.

There are five clean sheet points on offer for a player who has played at least 60 minutes of a match and two points if the player has played less than an hour where the game has finished with their team conceding zero goals.



How many points for a Save?

In addition to clean sheet points, goalkeepers can earn one point for every two saves made in a match. Much like points for tackling, save points introduce a new angle to team selection with keepers from teams further down the table likely to face more shots than those who generally dominate games.



What counts as a Save?

A save is a goalkeeper preventing the ball from entering the goal with any part of his body when facing an intentional attempt to score by an opposition player.

Saves have the following attributes:

Body part: Hands/Feet/Body

Save type: Caught/Collected/Parried Safe/Parried Danger area/Fingertip

Goalkeeper position: Diving/Standing/Reaching/Stooping

Sports.title: Xavi makes shock return to football as manager of former World Cup finalists
Sports.content:
XAVI HERNANDEZ has agreed a shock return to management as the new boss of the Netherlands.

The Barcelona legend, 46, is set to take charge of the Oranje on a four-year deal, marking his return to management.



Xavi has been out of work since leaving Barcelona at the end of the 2023-24 season.

The official Netherlands X account posted: “We proudly present our new head coach. Welcome, Xavi Hernández!”



And according to football journalist Fabrizio Romano, Xavi signed an agreement to become the new Dutch manager today

The World Cup winner is now poised to make his comeback in international management with the three-time World Cup finalists.

The Dutch FA have been searching for a new boss since Ronald Koeman stepped down following their World Cup exit to Morocco.

Roberto Martinez had emerged as a leading contender for the vacancy after leaving Portugal following their own disappointing World Cup campaign.

The former Everton boss was interviewed for the position but talkSPORT claim he has been overlooked, with Xavi instead landing the job.

He will be tasked with guiding the Netherlands towards Euro 2028, with the Nations League providing his first competitive challenge next month.



BEST ONLINE CASINOS – TOP SITES IN THE UK

Xavi famously helped Spain beat the Netherlands 1-0 in the 2010 World Cup final in Johannesburg during his glittering playing career.

He later moved into management with Qatari side Al-Sadd before taking charge of Barcelona in 2021, where he won LaLiga and the Spanish Super Cup.

And his appointment will make him the first foreign manager to take charge of the Netherlands men’s team in 48 years, following Austrian Ernst Happel’s spell in the late 1970s.

Sports.title: Southampton manager Tonda Eckert ‘already preparing for ban’ as likely verdict date is revealed after Spygate
Sports.content:

His Southampton side were booted out of the Championship play-offs in May and will start this season on minus four points after he admitted to spying on opponents’ training sessions last campaign.



And the FA are still deliberating on whether to compound his punishment with a touchline suspension.

Eckert, 33, is facing a ban of up to six months, and he has admitted that the saga is still “in the back of his mind”.



The German is set to stew on it for a while longer yet.

According to the Daily Mail, a verdict before Southampton’s league opener at Watford this weekend is ‘highly unlikely’.



And senior figures at the club fear it could be as far off as next month, which is just under three weeks away.

Eckert has seemingly used part of pre-season to prepare for a touchline ban.

He voluntarily watched the friendly against Preussen-Munster from the stands and practiced sending instructions from there to the bench, and onto the players.

Though Eckert is leaving no stone unturned, he is in an awkward spot where a stiff punishment could spell the end of his time at St Mary’s.

Sports.content:
The latest Arsenal, Liverpool, Man Utd transfer news and updates from around the Premier League as the window enters its final stretch ahead of the new season

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog for Wednesday, August 12. With around three weeks remaining, the window is entering its final stretch for Manchester United, Liverpool and more to get deals over the line.

Arsenal have been busy so far this summer, adding Bruno Guimaraes and Christos Tzolis but failing to land Vinicius Junior from Real Madrid. The Gunners remain linked to Aston Villa defender Ezri Konsa, and versatile youngster Myles Lewis-Skelly is said to have been offered to Chelsea and Manchester United.

The Red Devils completed some fast deals to bring midfielders Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos to the club, but could still add another. They remain linked to Lewis Hall as Michael Carrick wants to strengthen his full-back options, and could also sign a striker if the opportunity arises.

Liverpool have confirmed the signing of Ronald Araujo to bolster Andoni Iraola's defence, having signed Spain star Victor Munoz earlier in the month. All eyes are on whether they can get a deal done for Paris Saint-Germain star Bradley Barcola before the deadline, however.

Sports.title: Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli
Sports.content:
Arsenal set to finally break record for transfer sale as bid submitted for Gabriel Martinelli

Arsenal are reportedly weighing up an opening £38.4m offer from Galatasaray for Gabriel Martinelli

View 2 Images Arsenal have reportedly received an offer for Gabriel Martinelli that would be a new club-record sale. (Image: PA Wire)

Arsenal could be on the brink of a new club-record saleafter Turkish Super Lig giants Galatasaray lodged a £38.4m bid for Gabriel Martinelli. Sky Germany claim the Istanbul outfit have tabled an opening offer for the Brazilian winger, with the Gunners contemplating the offer.

‌



Mikel Arteta's men have already offloaded Leandro Trossard to Turkish club Besiktas and could be set for a complete new look left flank next season.

‌



The Gunners have already brought in Christos Tzolis as a replacement for the Belgian international, the club are keen to further strengthen that area of the pitch — a move which could open the door for Martinelli's departure.

‌



The Gunners boss has made no secret of his ambition to bolster his ranks this summer, with Morgan Rogers, Bradley Barcola and Vinicius Junior all being linked with a move to the Emirates, reports Football London.

Arsenal set to receive millions back from Newcastle days after Bruno Guimaraes transfer READ MORE :

Arsenal get significant Julian Alvarez transfer update after Atletico Madrid meeting READ MORE :

FOLLOW OUR ARSENAL FB PAGE! Latest Gunners news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

As it stands, a headline signing has yet to materialise, though numerous transfer targets remain firmly in their sights.

‌



Whether Arsenal will sanction Martinelli's exit before securing a replacement remains to be seen, but should the 25-year-old depart, it appears destined to be for a club-record fee.

View 2 Images Gabriel Martinelli could leave Arsenal this summer (Image: Getty Images)

The reported bid would surpass the current record sale, when Alex Oxlade-Chamberlain joined Liverpool for £35m in 2019.

‌



According to Florian Plettenberg, Martinelli is Galatasaray's 'top priority' this summer, despite being linked with other big-name targets.

The Turkish heavyweights have also been connected with a swoop for AC Milan forward Rafael Leao, who appears poised to depart the San Siro this summer.

Article continues below

The Portuguese winger had been loosely linked with a switch to the Premier League, with Arsenal and Manchester United amongst the clubs mentioned as potential suitors.

However, as it stands, the Gunners have their sights set on alternative targets.

Sports.title: Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'
Sports.content:
Man Utd chief gets blunt response to transfer approach - 'I'd tell him to go away'

Manchester United have been linked with Leicester City's Louis Page but Russell Martin has made it clear the teenager is not for sale

View 2 Images Man Utd are eyeing up a move for Leicester's Louis Page (Image: Catherine Ivill/Getty Images)

Leicester boss Russell Martin admits he'd tell Manchester United chief Jason Wilcox "to go away" if he made attempts to sign teenager Louis Page.

‌



The 18-year-old was named the EFL Apprentice of the Year last season and is seen as one of the most exciting talents in the Football League - attracting attention from the Red Devils.

‌



Page would reportedly be keen on moving to Old Trafford if the opportunity arose, but Leicester are determined to keep hold of their academy graduate. The England U20 international has already made 21 senior appearances for the Foxes - including five starts last season. He played in their Carabao Cup win over Northampton on Saturday.

‌



Martin has been appointed as the Foxes new boss following their relegation to League One and he previously worked at Southampton with Wilcox, who is now the director of football at United. He admits, despite their history, he'd tell him to look elsewhere if they came looking for Page.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion READ MORE :

He jokingly told Sky Sports: "Louis is a really fantastic young player. Obviously, I know the director of football at Manchester United very well after spending some time with Southampton. So we haven't actually spoken with Louis because he probably knows what I'd say to him and tell him to go away.

"But no, until something comes in that is really brilliant for the club, the player, and everyone is happy, then Louis stays, and he's in the squad. I'm really enjoying working with him. He's a fantastic young player."

‌



View 2 Images Leicester's teenage star recently signed a professional deal

Arsenal and Aston Villa have also shown an interest in Page. Leicester have already lost one of their leading young prospects this summer after seeing forward Jeremy Monga, 17, join Manchester City, and they will be loathed to see another leave the King Power Stadium.

Page signed professional terms with the Foxes in September last year, which means United would need to agree a transfer fee if they wanted to secure his services.

Article continues below

Leicester said after he penned his deal: "After joining us at Under-9s, Louis has progressed through our Academy ranks and developed within the LCFC pathway into one of the brightest talents in our system".

Sports.title: Kyle Walker lined up for immediate Premier League return after Burnley relegation
Sports.content:
Kyle Walker lined up for immediate Premier League return after Burnley relegation

Kyle Walker suffered relegation with Burnley last season but has remained with them in the Championship, however he could received an offer to make a Premier League return

View 2 Images Kyle Walker could make a Premier League return before the transfer window closes

Kyle Walker could be handed a route back into the Premier League with Everton keen on signing the veteran right-back.

‌



The ex-Manchester City star suffered relegation with the Clarets in his first season at Turf Moor and is now tasked with getting them out of the Championship, but the Toffees could finally land the Englishman.

‌



Twice in the past they've missed out on Walker. They were in for him before he moved to Burnley 12 months ago and back when Walker was a teenager they also tried to sign him, but he made the move to Tottenham.

‌



Everton could be successful with their third try, according to The Sun, as David Moyes looks to add more experience and quality to his squad on Merseyside.

Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message READ MORE :

Everton player charged with 61 breaches of FA betting rules as statement released READ MORE :

The Toffees have already signed the likes Brennan Johnson, Christian Norgaard and Tyrique George this summer. Johnson became their latest addition this week as he was involved in a swap deal that saw Dwight McNeil head to Crystal Palace.

Walker, now 36, made 35 starts for Burnley in the Premier League last season, highlighting his durability despite his age. He's chosen to remain with the club and scored the winning penalty in their spot-kick Carabao Cup victory over Notts County on Saturday.

‌



The ex-international can boast a CV that includes six Premier League titles and the Champions League but maintained that he's relishing the challenge of the Championship once again. He's previously played in the second tier with Sheffield United and QPR.

View 2 Images David Moyes is eyeing a move for the veteran right-back (Image: Getty Images)

Whilst at Loftus Road he was part of a team that would claim the title and believes that Burnley have all the tools to make an immediate return to the top flight.

‌



"Things aren’t always going to go as planned," he said. "This season might not go as planned. It might not be as plain sailing as we all want it to be. But I feel with the quality, what we have in the dressing room, that’s what we should be doing: getting promoted and going back to the Premier League."

Since 2013 Burnley have won promotion from the Championship on four occasions - but been relegated as many times. This is their sixth straight year playing in a different tier following a period of ups and downs.

Sports.title: Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message
Sports.content:
Michael Carrick told he must sign seven more players in urgent Man Utd transfer message

Manchester United have been sent a stark message following a slowdown in transfer activity

View 3 Images Michael Carrick has been told he needs fresh blood, and soon (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

Manchester United have been told they need to sign as many as seven new players to cope with the demands of the Champions League this season. The Red Devils are back in the world's premier club competition after Michael Carrick inspired an impressive revival over the second half of last season.

‌



But while the third-placed finish was impressive and helped Carrick land the job on a permanent basis, it's been clear for some time that the squad required an overhaul. Midfielders Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans are among the players to have arrived so far, but there is still more work to be done as United aim to compete across four fronts.

‌



Another middleman could arrive while the defence also requires attention. Former Premier League goalkeeper Shay Given reckons that at least seven more signings are required and has been surprised that United have not done more business so far.

‌



Speaking to BOYLE Sports, who offer the latest football odds, Shay Given said: "Maybe it comes down to the financial situation at Manchester United. They have to be careful after not being in the Champions League for a few years.

FOLLOW OUR MAN UTD FB PAGE! Latest United news and more on our dedicated Facebook page

"They're back in the competition this season and if they continue to qualify, maybe they'll go heavy again in the transfer market, and United do need to do more business. I've been surprised there hasn't already been more movement from them in this transfer window.

‌



Youri Tielemans sends clear Marcus Rashford message to Michael Carrick after Man Utd reunion READ MORE :

"Their squad wasn't strong enough last season, and they've already lost a couple of players. I think they need to sign another seven players at least."

Meanwhile, Lisandro Martinez has joined United's pre-season training camp in Ireland as the last of the players to be afforded an extended break following the World Cup.

View 3 Images Shay Given has given United some urgent advice (Image: NurPhoto via Getty Images)

‌



The return of Martinez, who played in Argentina's loss to Spain in the World Cup final in New Jersey on July 19, means Carrick has an almost-full complement of players in camp ahead of Wednesday's friendly against Leeds at Dublin's Croke Park.

On Sunday, England internationals Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo were among nine players to return amid continuing speculation over the former's future.

View 3 Images Lisandro Martinez is back with United (Image: Manchester United via Getty Images)

‌



After Wednesday's match, United will head to Wroclaw, Poland for their final pre-season assignment against AC Milan and former boss Ruben Amorim.

United are hoping to add to their ranks before their Premier League opener at Hull City on August 22, while more new faces should follow before the transfer window slams shut on September 3.

Sports.title: Lionel Messi hints at retirement in emotional letter following his father's death
Sports.content:
Lionel Messi hints at retirement in emotional letter following his father's death

Lionel Messi has paid an emotional tribute to his father, Jorge, following his death at the weekend as he hinted at potentially retiring from football

View 3 Images Lionel Messi has written an emotional message following his father's death (Image: (Photo by Peter Joneleit/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images))

Lionel Messi has hinted that retirement could soon be on the horizon in an emotional message following his father's death. His father, Jorge, passed away in Argentina following a battle with ill health.

‌



The Messi family were forced to release a statement during the recent World Cup, following speculation about Jorge's health, claiming he'd passed away during the tournament. The family made it clear he had not died, but was in the midst of a health battle.

‌



Just a few weeks after the tournament, Jorge died aged 68 and tributes have flooded in from around the world of football, with Messi breaking his silence following the sad news, opening up on the strong relationship he had with his father.

‌



Admitting he is unsure how much longer he will continue playing football Messi wrote on Instagram: "I don't know what I'm going to do without you, I don't know how to go on. I just played football, and now I have serious doubts that I'll be able to keep doing it for much longer. You were by my side from the beginning; the end was so close. Why couldn't you hold on that little bit longer and we could have finished together?

Lionel Messi breaks silence on death of father Jorge as Cristiano Ronaldo shows class READ MORE :

JOIN US ON FACEBOOK! Latest news, analysis and much more on Mirror Football's Facebook page

"I know your happiness came from seeing your family well, your wife, your children, and, above all, without the others finding out, seeing me play... It was always like that from the time I was little. You took me to every training session as soon as you got home from work. My mom took me to many of them because you were working.

‌



"Obviously, you never missed a match. How you suffered watching me and how you enjoyed it, even though you never gave me much praise. You were a father, a friend, and an agent. You were always the person you needed to be in every moment, and you were never wrong about anything. Beyond some reproaches or arguments, you were always right. In the end, things always turned out the way you said.

View 3 Images Lionel Messi with his late father Jorge (Image: X)

"I'm going to miss you so much, but you'll always be present, especially in my children's upbringing, because I teach and raise them the way you did me. Rest in peace and watch over us from above like you did here. Thank you for everything. I love you, Dad."

‌



There has been plenty of speculation about Messi's future in the game, with one of the world's greatest ever players now aged 39. The Argentina legend has racked up almost 1,200 senior appearances and scored nearly 1000 goals.

He added: "Dad, I still can't believe you're gone. It hasn't sunk in, or rather, I don't want to. It's so hard for me to imagine that I won't see you anymore, that we won't talk anymore. I know you were suffering and that it's for the best, but you left too soon. We still had so much to enjoy together.

"You kept asking me to play in the last World Cup, and days before it started, you were at your worst. It was the first time you weren't going to be in a tournament, but Mom told me you were going to get better and that you'd be well enough to travel. I told you we were going to make it to the final so you could go.

‌



View 3 Images Messi posted an emotion tribute to his late father (Image: Jean Catuffe/Getty Images)

"Every time a match ended, I waited for and missed your message. That's when I realized the situation was truly bad. Even so, I kept thinking about going as far as possible, to give you time to see a match.

"We reached the final, and you couldn't be there. I wanted to win it so I could bring it to you and show you a new one. I couldn't; my legs just wouldn't take it anymore. This time, I tried to push myself against my body, but I couldn't. I could never feel good.

‌



"When I arrived, you thought we had lost the final on penalties. We couldn't talk about anything that had happened. You couldn't enjoy anything. We weren't champions, but you have no idea how much we enjoyed every match. Once again, you were right: I had to be there and play.

"I'm telling you this because it was the only thing we couldn't talk about, because you already know everything else. We talked every day and saw each other whenever my commitments allowed."

Sports.title: Birmingham Phoenix win battle to avoid Hundred wooden spoon vs MI London
Sports.content:
Birmingham Phoenix prevailed in the battle to avoid the wooden spoon in The Hundred women's competition as Ellyse Perry's composed half-century condemned MI London to a sixth defeat of a chastening campaign.

Both teams had managed a solitary victory heading into this fixture but a fifth-wicket stand of 66 between Perry (62no from 39) and Pakistan skipper Fatima Sana (36 from 32) ensured Phoenix halted a three-match losing streak to end with a consolation win and finish seventh in the table.

Set a modest target of 122, the hosts were wobbling at 48-4 after Jemima Spence and Davina Perrin fell in the powerplay and England duo Alice Capsey and Emma Lamb were dismissed cheaply, with Kirstie Gordon (2-20) making early inroads with her left-arm spin.

But Perry found a willing partner in Sana, who eventually fell to Nicola Carey when just seven runs were required, and the Aussie superstar secured the win with six balls to spare.

Sports.title: Sports fans watch on as Britain experiences fullest solar eclipse since 1999
Sports.content:
Cricket fans at Edgbaston were among sporting spectators given a stunning view of Wednesday evening's partial solar eclipse.

The sky took on an eerie darkness as the Moon obscured more than 90 per cent of the Sun, leaving only a slim crescent of light visible.

Spectators watching Birmingham Phoenix face MI London in The Hundred were able to take in the spectacle from the stands, with many wearing special glasses.

The eclipse was the fullest above British skies since the total eclipse in 1999.

Image: Many fans watched on at Edgbaston through special glasses

Other sporting events also took place against the unusual backdrop.

Floodlights were turned on in anticipation at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham.

Small groups, including Swedish athletes Erika Warff and Tilde Bjerager, gathered outside Alexander Stadium to observe the phenomenon, congregating on both sides of the terrace below the west stand.

Image: Floodlights at the European Athletics Championships in Birmingham were also on in anticipation of the eclipse

Some were prepared with protective paper glasses while others watched through their phone cameras, although the rare occurrence was already obscured by clouds when it peaked at around 7.15pm.

In Salzburg, football fans attending the UEFA Super Cup between Aston Villa and European champions Paris St Germain also gazed skywards.

Image: Football fans watched on at the UEFA Super Cup match between PSG and Aston Villa in Salzburg

Sports.title: Everton breeze past lacklustre Newcastle in Murrayfield friendly
Sports.content:
Matthias Jaissle was given a hint of the task in hand as Newcastle boss as Premier League rivals Everton strolled to a comfortable 3-1 win in a pre-season friendly at Murrayfield.

In his second friendly game in charge, Jaissle witnessed how ruthless and unforgiving Premier League teams can be as goals from Thierno Barry, Iliman Ndiaye and Tyrique George resulted in a commanding win for the Toffees.

Harvey Barnes scored a late consolation for the Toon, who made 10 changes at half-time with Jaissle seemingly happy to use this fixture as a chance to assess his squad.

Image: Ndiaye scores for Everton against Newcastle

It was a typical David Moyes performance from Everton: disciplined, organised and efficient without the ball, with the Toffees happy to frustrate Newcastle and punish them when opportunities came their way before taking control in the second half.

Barry, new signing Hayden Hackney and George all impressed and looked in excellent nick as Everton produced a performance that would have pleased Moyes, particularly given the intensity of their work out of possession ahead of their Premier League opener with Crystal Palace on Saturday August 22.

Newcastle XI's First Half: Hornicek, Shahar, Thiaw, Botman, Hall, Bamba, Joelinton, Elanga, Wissa, Toure, Osula

Second Half: Hornicek, Charlton, Pivas, Johnson, Miley, Steur, Ramsey, Willock, Murphy, Barnes, Woltemade

Newcastle, by contrast, looked a side still searching for their identity. There were encouraging moments, but the game became increasingly difficult to judge after Jaissle made wholesale changes in the second half, weakening his side and disrupting their rhythm.

Everton were sharper and more cohesive, and ultimately deserved their victory.

Pre-season results can be misleading and there is clearly time for Newcastle to improve, but with only 11 days until the start of their Premier League season, they remain a big work in progress.

And their challenge on the opening weekend could hardly be bigger: Liverpool are the visitors to St James' Park, live on Sky Sports.

Newcastle United

Liverpool Sunday 23rd August 4:00pm Kick off 4:30pm

On this evidence, Newcastle have plenty of work ahead of them before that encounter.

The key moments from Murrayfield…

27: GOAL! Following a slow start by Everton, Barry gets them up the pitch and provides a cool finish into the far corner.

Following a slow start by Everton, Barry gets them up the pitch and provides a cool finish into the far corner. 34: GOAL! Joelinton makes a lazy challenge on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall inside the box right in front of the referee. Ndiaye slots home the penalty.

Joelinton makes a lazy challenge on Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall inside the box right in front of the referee. Ndiaye slots home the penalty. 46: SUBS! Jaissle brings on 10 players at the break and fields a very inexperienced back four of Miley, Johnson, Pivas and Charlton.

Jaissle brings on 10 players at the break and fields a very inexperienced back four of Miley, Johnson, Pivas and Charlton. 73: GOAL! George finishes off a flowing move with a crisp finish, capping a fine performance.

George finishes off a flowing move with a crisp finish, capping a fine performance. 85: GOAL! Barnes is on hand at the back post following a wonderful cross from Jacob Murphy.

'Newcastle fans will be concerned about the season ahead'

Sky Sports News' Keith Downie at Murrayfield:

"That performance showed me that Newcastle desperately need some experience in that team. They have lost Kieran Trippier, Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon and replaced them with youngsters. When things went wrong in this game, some of the players had no leaders to look to.

"It was clear that they need reinforcements.

"Everton looked more streetwise and organised. There's a real concern ahead of the season that Newcastle could be gobbled up by top-half teams if they don't add some experience.

"Of the new signings only Lukas Hornicek and Bazoumana Toure look ready to start. It's a big week and a half until the window closes.

"Newcastle fans will be concerned about the season ahead and the direction of the club."

Sports.title: Chelsea stars for sale: The players who could leave - and what they'll cost
Sports.content:
Chelsea are the Premier League's top spenders this summer with the bulk of their business done and attention is now turning to sales.

They have already made £160m from player sales in this window. Only Newcastle (£244m) and Aston Villa (£202m) have generated more from outgoings.

But do not be surprised if Chelsea end the summer window as the league's top sellers once again after recouping a record £314m one year ago.

Chelsea have a squad of more than 40, according to the club website, and there are expected to be a number of exits in the final three weeks of the window.

Which defenders could leave?

Xabi Alonso wants to cut his number of centre-back options down to five, and he currently has nine.

Trevoh Chalobah has already left to join Como in a deal worth up to £30.8m. Benoit Badiashile and Axel Disasi are likely to join him through the exit door.

Napoli have so far indicated they are willing to pay around £20m all in for Badiashile in a deal that would see him move on an initial loan with an option to buy.

However, the Blues value Badiashile at £30m. He has four years left on his contract.

Meanwhile, Chelsea will be seeking at least £25m for Disasi, who spent the second half of last season on loan at West Ham.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Speaking on the Transfer Show, Sky Sports' Mark McAdam and Michael Bridge provide the latest transfer update on Myles Lewis-Skelly, amid rumours the versatile midfielder might depart The Emirates

Reports have emerged this week of interest in Tosin. As things stand, Chelsea's valuation of the former Fulham defender is unknown.

Mamadou Sarr, who joined Chelsea last summer from partner club Strasbourg, is being lined up for a loan move.

There has been plenty of speculation around the future of full-back Malo Gusto. Chelsea are not trying to sell the France international and value him at £75m.

Chelsea player valuations we know Nicolas Jackson - £65m

Malo Gusto - £75m

Axel Disasi - £25m plus add-ons

Benoit Badiashile - £30m

Enzo Fernandez - £120m

Liam Delap - £50m

Marc Guiu - £25m

Which strikers could leave?

Chelsea have a surplus of strikers following the signing of veteran forward Danny Welbeck from Brighton.

Nicolas Jackson, Liam Delap and Marc Guiu are the players who could move on as a result.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Sky Sports' Dharmesh Sheth explains why Aston Villa may avoid signing Nicolas Jackson from Chelsea

Jackson spent last season on loan at Bayern Munich and has interest from Aston Villa among a number of clubs. Chelsea want £65m for Jackson.

Any deal between Villa and Chelsea is complicated by UEFA's rules around player swaps and both clubs being in a settlement agreement with European football's governing body.

As Morgan Rogers joined Chelsea from Villa within 45 days of the window closing, it means any subsequent deal between the clubs will go down as a player exchange, which is not ideal on the accounting books.

Image: Chelsea's Liam Delap scored two penalties in a pre-season friendly against Malaysian champions Johor Darul Ta'zim

Delap struggled in his first season at Chelsea after being signed from Ipswich for £30m. Nonetheless, he is valued at around £50m by Chelsea after scoring twice last season.

Everton have previously held an interest, as one of the many clubs that tried to sign Delap from Ipswich last summer.

Guiu, who had his loan at Sunderland cut short last season, reportedly has interest from Spain and Italy, with Chelsea looking for around £25m to let him go this summer.

What about Enzo Fernandez?

Image: Enzo Fernandez has been linked with a move to Man City

Barcelona's pursuit of Rodri has raised the prospect of Manchester City making a late move for Enzo Fernandez before the window closes.

City have targets in mind for any player who departs and Fernandez is one of the players they are interested in. He also had a strong working relationship with City's new boss Enzo Maresca when they were at Chelsea together.

But Chelsea are not trying to sell Fernandez, who has six years left on his contract, and value him at £120m. Remember they signed him for around £107m from Benfica in the 2023 winter window.

Fernandez was dropped for two games in April after he admitted he would welcome living in Madrid. The player and his agent also apologised for his comments. They had been seeking improved terms at Chelsea.
