Sports.title: Featured Comment: Has F1 failed to promote quality racing? | Brief
Sports.content:
Those in charge of Formula 1 have allowed its new rules to turn racing into a ‘battle of the bots’, says @RedPill:

I felt there was going to be some trust and proper direction within FIA and Liberty Media who owns the rights to F1 to make sure the quality of (human) racing was going to remain high quality. Boy, we were wrong. The whole debacle and agreed verbiage in contacts allowed the power unit manufacturers and investors to pretty much be the ones to dictate what was going to be allowed in F1, while retaining huge powers in the wording to prevent changes.

Fans, drivers, teams, FIA and Liberty Media are now stuck with it. I hate how the drivers are more passengers in their own cars while racing. Yes, there’s too much going in the cars, that the drivers can’t possibly manage everything and race in full anger, but this is no secret or anything new. The powers that be needed to craft specifications that used the latest tech, but still retain the drivers’ ability to fully race the car, the way a race car driver is suppose to race. That is why we watch the races.

We come and watch these F1 races because there’s humans in control of brilliant machinery, racing them to the ninth degree, but there’s a limit. If I wanted to watch automated machinery duke it out and see battle of bots I would instead go to robot contests, not F1.

Red Pill (@RedPill)

Sports.title: Top Rank’s Thin DAZN Schedule Tells Half The Story
Sports.content:
Darshan Desai of Uncrowned highlighted the unusual arrangement Wednesday while examining DAZN’s schedule. Raymond Muratalla fought Robson Conceição on a Golden Boy card earlier this month, Top Rank fighters Albert Gonzalez and Samuel Contreras competed on a Matchroom show in July, and Giovani Santillan takes another route when he faces Abass Baraou on September 11 in a ProBoxTV headliner.

Building a full show requires considerably more than placing a fighter on an existing lineup. Opponents require negotiation, purses need settling, and organizers must assemble a complete event around the roster. How costs are divided under Top Rank’s agreement with DAZN has not been made public.

Working alongside Golden Boy or Matchroom gives Top Rank flexible alternatives. Both outfits work extensively with DAZN, reducing the traditional network barriers that historically complicated cross-promotional deals.

Top Rank still has plenty of incentive to stage its own events when a leading fighter can anchor a marquee card. The proposed welterweight title bout between Devin Haney and Keyshawn Davis would have provided another major date before Davis declined the WBO process.

Whatever the reason for Top Rank’s limited number of DAZN dates so far, its fighters are finding work without waiting for the promoter to build an entire show around them.

Sports.title: WBC Threatens Noel Mikaelian’s Title Over Jai Opetaia Fight
Sports.content:
King and Benavidez promoter Sampson Lewkowicz reached an agreement for Mikaelian to defend his WBC cruiserweight title against Benavidez in December in Glendale, Arizona. Zuffa Boxing subsequently announced Mikaelian against Opetaia for September 12 in Las Vegas on the Ryan Garcia-Conor Benn card.

Mikaelian is already training for Opetaia, Pugmire reports, giving the WBC reason to seek an answer in the coming weeks on which fight he intends to take.

Benavidez may already have an alternate route. He teased an announcement Tuesday, and Pugmire reports his next bout will likely be against WBC interim cruiserweight champion Michal Cieslak for the title.

The promotional situation remains unusual. King and Lewkowicz had already struck their agreement when Zuffa announced Mikaelian as Opetaia’s opponent. Mikaelian then began preparing for the September fight despite remaining WBC champion, with Benavidez positioned as his mandatory challenger.

If Mikaelian proceeds with Opetaia, the WBC can remove him and leave Benavidez and Cieslak to fight for the championship. That would give Mikaelian the Zuffa fight he is training for, but without the WBC belt.

Sports.title: Hearn Targets Brandon Moore Next For Teremoana
Sports.content:
“I think we might fight him next, Brandon Moore,” Hearn said after the fight. “We have really got to find someone. It’s so frustrating in Australia because no one wants to fight him.”

A fight with Moore (19-1, 10 KOs) would provide an obvious measuring stick. He defeated Savage by a 10-round unanimous decision last September, dropping him in the seventh. His lone defeat came against Richard Torrez Jr., who knocked him out in five rounds in 2024.

Hearn felt Savage became frightened once he experienced Teremoana’s power.

“I was disappointed Savage didn’t get [further]. I don’t blame him, but it was just the fear. His eyes were popping out of his head as soon as he felt the power.”

Teremoana hardly pressed the accelerator in the opening round, throwing only a handful of punches before hurting Savage with a right hand late. Hearn liked the patience he showed rather than immediately going for the finish.

“I saw a guy that was a little bit more experienced tonight. Sort of took his time. I mean, he could have really done it in 30 seconds.”

Getting meaningful rounds has become increasingly difficult. Hearn conceded that fans will question the quality of Teremoana’s opposition and said Matchroom has reached the point where the competition must increase.

“There’ll be a lot of the public that will say, ‘Well, who’s he fighting?’ And I get that as well. We’ve got to step up,” Hearn said. “We do really, really need rounds.”

Hearn wants Teremoana to fight twice more this year and believes another four or five bouts are needed before he challenges for a world heavyweight title. His target is the back end of 2027, when Teremoana will be 29.

“He needs someone that can take him five or six rounds,” Hearn said. “Sooner or later there’s going to be a 10-round, 12-round war in there, and he’ll be ready.”

Anthony Joshua has also taken notice of Teremoana.

“AJ said to me a few times, ‘What’s this Teremoana?’ I’m like, ‘He’s a fucking monster.’”

Hearn expects a different type of fight once Teremoana encounters heavyweights willing and capable of attacking him rather than simply trying to survive.

Sports.title: Teremoana Teremoana Crushes DeAndre Savage in Two
Sports.content:
Teremoana dictated the opening round, forcing Savage onto the defensive while patiently looking for an opening.

In the co-main event, Michael “Pretty Boy” Zerafa stopped Alejandro “El Venado” Ortiz after nine rounds of their scheduled 10-round middleweight bout.

Zerafa established his jab over the opening two rounds before Ortiz found more success in the third, landing several left hooks to the chin. Zerafa countered effectively and produced a strong fourth round.

Ortiz landed a hard right hand midway through the fifth, but Zerafa regained control in the sixth by increasing his output. The Australian broke through in the ninth, hurting Ortiz and overwhelming him with punches. Ortiz struggled back to his corner after the bell, and his team stopped the fight before the 10th round.

Jasmine Parr defeated Jemma Peart by unanimous decision over eight two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout.

Parr controlled much of the opening three rounds by outlanding Peart, who had greater success with her jab in the fourth. Parr occasionally switched to southpaw in the fifth and sixth while maintaining the higher work rate.

The seventh was the most competitive round before Parr closed strongly in the eighth. All three judges scored the bout 80-72.

At super middleweight, Jack Bowen stopped Dalielibieke at 2:15 of the seventh round.

Bowen used an effective jab early and rocked Dalielibieke with an uppercut in the second. Both connected with hard right hands late in the third before the exchanges became heavier in the fourth.

Another right uppercut from Bowen hurt Dalielibieke midway through the fifth. Dalielibieke responded with one of his better rounds in the sixth, but Bowen regained control in the seventh. A sustained combination prompted referee Paul Tapley to stop the contest.

Lekaysha Woodbridge defeated Sothia Sitthichai over five two-minute rounds in their flyweight bout. Referee Paul Tapley scored the fight 50-45 for Woodbridge.

Light heavyweight Omar El-Abdallah stopped Jordan Towns after three rounds of their scheduled five-round bout. The two were competitive through the opening three rounds, but Towns was unable to answer the bell for the fourth.

In welterweight action, Reube Thornberry stopped Lachlan Harrington at 1:40 of the second round of their scheduled four-round bout.

Sports.title: Jake Paul’s MVP Signs IBF Champion Elif Turhan
Sports.content:
Turhan gives Jake Paul’s promotion another major piece at 135 pounds. Caroline Dubois holds the WBC and WBO championships, while Stephanie Han owns the WBA belt.

That leaves MVP working with fighters who control all four major lightweight titles.

Turhan punched her way into that company last December in Monte Carlo. She broke down Brazilian Olympic gold medalist Beatriz Ferreira and forced a fifth-round stoppage to seize the IBF crown, registering the defining victory of her professional career.

She has since strengthened her position with wins over Taylah Gentzen in January and Gabriella Tellez in June.

Turhan brings pressure and finishing instinct to a division loaded with potential championship fights. She likes to close the distance, force exchanges and punish opponents once her combinations begin finding the target.

The Istanbul fighter becomes the first Turkish boxer to join MVP and follows Nicolson as the second addition produced by the promotion’s agreement with Matchroom.

Turhan believes the partnership can push her toward more championship opportunities.

“I am incredibly excited to be part of this powerful collaboration. This marks a major signal of the exciting initiatives we will undertake for women’s boxing globally, and I am deeply honored to be involved in this journey with all my strength and energy.”

Her next opponent has yet to be confirmed, but her ambitions reach beyond defending the IBF belt.

“I am excited for the opportunities that will come my way as I look to win more major World Titles.”

That pursuit creates an obvious pressure point at lightweight. Dubois controls two belts, Han holds another and Turhan carries the IBF championship.

If MVP eventually matches its lightweight champions, Turhan will have to establish her pressure against fighters capable of controlling distance, countering her entries and punishing her on the way inside.

Sports.title: Teremoana vs. DeAndre Savage Live Results and Fight Updates
Sports.content:
Teremoana Teremoana improved to 12-0 with a second-round knockout of DeAndre Savage after another destructive heavyweight finish. Savage survived the opening round despite absorbing several heavy shots as Teremoana began finding his distance and opening up. That resistance ended quickly in the second. Teremoana cracked Savage with a big punch that buckled the American’s legs but left him standing. The Australian kept hunting the finish, dropped Savage moments later, and watched as he failed to beat the referee’s count. Savage became only the third opponent to take Teremoana beyond the opening round, but the extra three minutes merely delayed another knockout for the Australian heavyweight.

Michael Zerafa broke down Alejandro Ortiz for a stoppage victory on the Gold Coast after taking command in the later rounds. Zerafa began forcing Ortiz onto the back foot, then cracked him with a heavy shot in the seventh as the pressure increased. His corner demanded he keep letting his hands go while staying smart, telling him Ortiz was hurt whenever he opened up. Zerafa responded by pressing harder and keeping Ortiz under fire. The breakthrough came when Zerafa dropped Ortiz and immediately looked to close the show. Ortiz climbed off the canvas but remained hurt, and the fight was stopped soon afterward when he had taken enough. The victory gave Zerafa the result he needed after entering the fight under pressure and facing questions over his recent form.

Sports.title: Jack Dempsey’s Harry Wills Problem Never Went Away
Sports.content:
Following Jack Johnson’s 1910 victory over Jim Jeffries, racial violence erupted across the United States. The possibility of another Black heavyweight challenging a white champion encountered resistance from promoters, regulators, and others concerned about another interracial title fight.

Wills paid heavily for that environment.

A Dempsey-Wills fight nearly materialized in 1922 when promoter Tex Rickard selected a date and had tickets printed for a proposed bout in New Jersey. The promotion collapsed when the financing needed to meet Dempsey’s guarantee failed.

Another attempt ran into opposition in New York, where athletic commission chairman William Muldoon resisted an interracial heavyweight championship fight over concerns about racial unrest.

Dempsey also gave his critics ammunition. He drew the color line early in his championship reign before later changing his public position. His long stretches of inactivity intensified criticism that Wills was being denied an opportunity he had earned. Yet Wills himself resisted blaming Dempsey.

“My only regret in life is that I never got a shot at Dempsey, [and] I’m sure I could have beaten him,” Wills later said. “It wasn’t Jack’s fault. He wasn’t scared of anyone. He was a great fighter.”

Dempsey lost the heavyweight championship to Gene Tunney in 1926. Wills never fought for the world title.

The missing fight should count when Dempsey’s championship reign is evaluated. Wills was precisely the type of challenger a champion needed to defeat to remove questions about his dominance.

Placing the entire responsibility on Dempsey, however, ignores the racial barriers, regulators, promoters and failed financing that repeatedly interfered with the fight.

More than a century later, nobody knows what would have happened if Jack Dempsey and Harry Wills had finally met. That unanswered question is why Wills remains an unavoidable part of Dempsey’s legacy.

Sports.title: Teofimo Sr. Dismisses Shakur Stevenson’s Vacant-Belt Championships
Sports.content:
“This fight is about Teofimo Lopez trying to get the world title again, become a real three-division world champion. No vacant belts,” Lopez Sr. said to Fighthype. “Shakur got like two vacant belts, right? So, to me, he’s not a real three-division world champion. My son is going to do it the right way. We’re going to go straight to the champion. No vacant belt.”

Stevenson has actually won world titles across four divisions. His first came against Joet Gonzalez for the vacant WBO featherweight belt in 2019. He then stopped reigning WBO junior lightweight champion Jamel Herring in 2021 before defeating Edwin De Los Santos for the vacant WBC lightweight title in November 2023.

The fourth belt is difficult for Lopez Sr. to dismiss under his own standard. Shakur took the WBO light welterweight title from Teofimo in January, giving him two divisional championships won by defeating reigning titleholders.

Lopez Sr. also criticized Shakur’s fighting style and questioned how much further Stevenson can climb through the weight classes.

“I would love to fight him again. Let’s hope that we can get him before we move up too high,” Lopez Sr. said. “I don’t think Shakur can go up in the weight divisions. He’s too chinny. He doesn’t like to get hit. He’s a boring fighter.”

He believes Teofimo fought the wrong fight against Shakur. In his view, Teofimo should have boxed from the back foot instead of following the southpaw to his right all night.

Ghana News.title: Poor Internet connectivity keeps disrupting teaching and learning at UEW
Ghana News.content:
For students at the University of Education, Winneba (UEW), attending an online class, downloading lecture materials or submitting an assignment has become a struggle that often depends on the strength of an internet connection.



Unstable networks and slow internet speeds are disrupting academic activities for some students, making it difficult for them to participate fully in online classes, conduct research, communicate with lecturers and submit assignments on time.



At a time when digital technology has become an important part of university education, students say unreliable internet connectivity is creating an additional academic burden.



Students struggle to attend online classes



Some students say poor connectivity frequently interrupts online lectures, forcing them to reconnect repeatedly or miss portions of lessons.



Ernestina, a student at UEW, described the experience as stressful.



“Joining online classes here at UEW is very stressful because whenever I try joining an online class, I experience breaks in the connection. It makes online learning very difficult.”



For students who depend on virtual classes to keep up with their courses, such interruptions can mean missing explanations, discussions and important information provided by lecturers.



The problem becomes even more serious when classes are conducted entirely online.



Poor network affects assignment submissions



The connectivity challenge also extends beyond virtual lectures.



John, a student from the Business Department, said he once lost marks on an online assignment because of network problems.



“I once lost five marks for submitting my online assignment before the deadline. It was not because I forgot or did not have a data bundle, but because of the poor network.”



His experience highlights a concern among students that internet connectivity can directly affect academic performance.



For students who submit assignments through online platforms, a weak connection can turn a simple academic task into a race against time.



Lecturers face the same challenge



The problem is not limited to students.



Lecturers who depend on digital platforms to teach, communicate with students and distribute academic materials are also affected.



Dr. Elizabeth, a lecturer at UEW, said the difficulties students face in joining online classes could influence how she conducts lessons in the future.



“From next semester, we will not meet online for classes again because students find it difficult to join my class because of the poor network.”



The situation raises concerns about the effectiveness of online learning when students and lecturers cannot depend on stable connectivity.



Students spend more to stay connected



For some students, poor campus connectivity means spending additional money on mobile data.

Others move to different locations in search of stronger network signals just to attend classes, download materials or submit assignments.



For students already managing tuition-related expenses, accommodation, transportation and other academic costs, the additional financial burden of purchasing data or travelling to areas with better connectivity can be significant.



Digital education requires reliable infrastructure



The growing reliance on online platforms means internet connectivity is no longer simply a convenience for university students.



It has become part of the infrastructure required for effective teaching and learning.



Lecture materials, research resources, online assessments, virtual meetings and communication between students and lecturers increasingly depend on digital access.



When that access is unreliable, the consequences can extend beyond inconvenience.



Students may miss classes, delay assignments, struggle to conduct research or lose marks through no fault of their own.



For UEW students, the hope is that the university will take stronger measures to improve connectivity across campus.



As higher education continues to embrace digital learning, ensuring reliable internet access should be treated as an essential part of creating an effective academic environment.



For students at UEW, a stronger internet connection would mean more than faster browsing.



It could mean fewer missed classes, fewer delayed assignments and a fairer opportunity to learn.

Ghana News.title: Volta Regional House of Chiefs congratulates Ablakwa, pledges stronger ties with Foreign Affairs Ministry
Ghana News.content:
The Volta Regional House of Chiefs has paid a courtesy call on the Minister for Foreign Affairs, Samuel Okudzeto Ablakwa, to congratulate him on his appointment and birthday and strengthen ties between the traditional leadership of the region and the Ministry.

The delegation, led by the President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs and Paramount Chief of the Anfoega Traditional Area, Togbe Tepre Hodo IV, visited the Minister at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Accra on Wednesday, August 12, 2026.

Togbe Tepre Hodo IV said the visit was also an opportunity to deepen the relationship between the House and the Ministry as they work towards the development of the Volta Region and Ghana.

Mr Ablakwa expressed appreciation to the chiefs for the visit and their congratulatory messages.

He said he was particularly grateful that the traditional leaders had travelled to Accra to meet him, noting that he had initially intended to visit the House of Chiefs himself, but the offer was respectfully declined.

The Minister described the visit as a privilege and welcomed the opportunity to host the traditional leaders at his official workplace.

Togbe Tepre Hodo IV commended Mr Ablakwa for what he described as his dedicated service to Ghana and his efforts to promote development in his constituency and the Volta Region.

He noted that the region had, over the years, faced challenges in accessing its fair share of national resources and development opportunities.

According to him, there have been significant changes in recent times, which he attributed partly to the Minister’s efforts to ensure that the interests of the Volta Region receive greater attention.

The President of the Volta Regional House of Chiefs also praised Mr Ablakwa for maintaining a strong connection with the region despite his national responsibilities.

He encouraged the Minister to continue championing the interests of the Volta Region while advancing Ghana’s broader national interests.

Ghana News.title: Baba Yara stadium will be ready for 2026/27 football season – NSA boss
Ghana News.content:
Director General of the National Sports Authority (NSA), Yaw Ampofo Ankrah says the Baba Yara Stadium will be ready for the first game of the 2026/27 Ghana football season.

The NSA boss toured the stadium together with the board chairman of NSA, Dr Fred Awaah and NSA estate boss Mr. Ebo.

The 2026/27 Ghana Premier League season will officially get underway over the weekend of September 4–7, 2026.

After inspecting the stadium, he commended the Ashanti Regional Directorate for its effort in restoring the stadium to its functionality.

The Director General assessed the progress of pitch condition and also inspected the stability of the scoreboard and floodlights.

Speaking to the media, Yaw Ampofo expressed confidence the facility will be ready in time for next football season.

“The pitch is responding to treatment and the rehabilitation is on course. I believe in a few weeks it should be in good, stead, strong enough, robust to host football matches including the Ghana Premier League and any other international match in the need arises,” he said.

The NSA was criticized heavily after video of groundkeepers using hoes on the pitch instead of modern turf maintenance equipment went viral.

Yaw Ampofo backs the move of the regional directorate: “We don’t have the tools that are common, we will acquire them soon but I commend them [Ashanti Regional Directorate] for tackling the weeds from its source.

"In the past when the sprinklers were not working, they resorted to the Fire Service and other means to ensure the grass doesn’t die. Perhaps people didn’t understand the images but now they do”.

With Ghana’s 2027 AFCON qualifiers set to start in September, there are speculation about hosting home games at the Baba Yara Stadium in Kumasi.

But Yaw Ampofo believes the decision to host Black Stars lies with the sports ministry and GFA after consulting the engineers in charge of the facility.

Despite the improvement in work done at the stadium, there are more than three thousand seats to be repaired after violence during school sports competitions in January destroyed some of the seats.

The NSA boss reiterated that the Ghana Education Service has agreed to fund the restoration project.

Ghana News.title: Speak law, not emotions – Amaliba fires back at Mercer on Sedina Tamakloe’s release
Ghana News.content:
Former Director of Legal Affairs of the governing National Democratic Congress (NDC), Abraham Amaliba, has rejected claims by a member of the New Patriotic Party (NPP), Andrews Agyapa Mercer, that the release of former Microfinance and Small Loans Centre (MASLOC) Chief Executive Officer, Sedina Christine Tamakloe-Attionu, vindicates the opposition party’s concerns about selective justice.

Mr Amaliba said Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release was the logical consequence of her acquittal and discharge by the Court of Appeal.

Speaking on Joy FM’s Top Story on Wednesday, August 12, he argued that the government could not have prevented her release after an independent court had delivered its judgment.

“How can a decision of a court of competent jurisdiction become a matter of ‘we told you so’? It cannot ... I think that we should speak law and stop speaking with emotions,” he said.

Mr Amaliba stressed that the judiciary is an independent arm of government and that its decisions must be respected.

He said even if the NDC government had wanted Ms Tamakloe-Attionu to remain in custody, it could not have simply overturned or ignored the court’s decision.

“Even if we as a party wanted to do it, how could we have done it? Another arm of government, independent as it is, and respectable as it is, gave that ruling,” he added.

His comments followed remarks by lawyer and NPP member Andrews Agyapa Mercer, who said he was not surprised by Ms Tamakloe-Attionu’s release.

Mr Mercer argued that the development reinforced concerns that the government was selectively pursuing cases involving political opponents.

“I really am not surprised. The script that was formulated when the NDC came into office commenced with the nolle prosequi that they entered for all persons affiliated with the NDC who were standing trial in the courts,” he said.

Mr Mercer further questioned the circumstances surrounding the Attorney-General’s decision to withdraw the application for a stay of execution after the Court of Appeal acquitted and discharged Ms Tamakloe-Attionu.

He suggested that the development vindicated earlier concerns raised by the NPP about the government’s handling of cases involving individuals associated with political parties.

Mr Amaliba, however, maintained that such claims failed to account for the role of the judiciary in the matter.

He said the appropriate approach was to examine the legal basis for the court’s decision rather than interpret the outcome through a political lens.

Ghana News.title: NSA releases 121,754 PIN codes for 2026/2027 National Service Year
Ghana News.content:
The National Service Authority (NSA) has released PIN codes for 121,754 prospective national service personnel for the 2026/2027 National Service Year.

The release marks the opening of the registration process for eligible graduates required to undertake national service under the National Service Authority Act, 2024 (Act 1119).

Online registration began on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, and will close on Wednesday, August 26.

The Authority has urged all eligible prospective personnel to complete their registration within the stipulated period to avoid delays in deployment.

The NSA said tertiary institutions submitted a total of 144,023 prospective personnel for consideration.

Of that number, 122,712 were approved, with records created for 121,754 unique persons.

However, 958 approved submissions have not been promoted pending further verification, while another 21,311 submissions were rejected pending further identity verification.

The Authority said the 121,754 PIN codes released represent applicants whose submissions successfully passed the requisite validation and verification processes.

The remaining 22,269 submissions have been withheld pending the outcome of further checks.

Prospective personnel with PIN codes are required to access the NSA's registration portal, activate their PIN codes and complete the online enrolment process.

A registration fee is also required to activate the PIN code before applicants can access the enrolment platform. Payment is to be made via Mobile Money across all networks.

The NSA said it has introduced enhanced security measures to strengthen the integrity of the registration process and prevent fraudulent enrolments.

These include facial biometric verification against Ghana Card records held by the National Identification Authority (NIA).

Applicants must also provide a valid GhanaPost GPS address, which the Authority says will support accurate deployment and proximity-based postings.

Real-time verification mechanisms have also been integrated into the registration platform to improve data accuracy.

The NSA has further reminded tertiary institutions whose accreditation status remains unresolved to engage the Ghana Tertiary Education Commission (GTEC) to regularise their status.

The Authority said it would continue processing eligible graduates from such institutions once GTEC confirms their accreditation.

Prospective personnel requiring assistance have been directed to use the support channels provided on the NSA registration portal.

Ghana News.title: Eyipe’s sanitation crisis raises concerns over public health and coastal pollution
Ghana News.content:
Residents of Eyipe, a community in Winneba in the Central Region, are raising concerns over persistent sanitation challenges, including improper waste disposal, open defecation and the poor management of wastewater.

The situation has become particularly worrying because of the community’s proximity to the sea. Rubbish can be found in parts of the community, especially around the shoreline, while wastewater from households is sometimes discharged into open areas where waste has already accumulated.

For residents, the problem goes beyond the appearance of their surroundings. They are concerned about the possible effects on public health and the coastal environment.

Waste disposal remains a challenge

Some residents say the cost of waste collection contributes to improper waste disposal in the community.

According to them, some households struggle to pay the waste levy regularly and resort to disposing of rubbish in open spaces, sometimes early in the morning.

Residents also expressed concerns about wastewater from washing and other household activities being discharged into open areas. In some locations, the wastewater mixes with accumulated rubbish, creating unhygienic conditions.

The situation is more concerning around the shoreline, where some residents say rubbish is dumped close to the sea.

With the community located near the coast, residents fear that continued dumping could contribute to marine pollution and affect the environment and people who depend on the sea.

Residents express frustration

Some residents said they had reported the sanitation problem several times but had seen limited improvement.

Others declined to speak about the issue, explaining that they had raised similar concerns in the past without seeing enough action.

For these residents, the problem has therefore become more than the presence of rubbish. It has also created a sense of frustration over whether their concerns are receiving adequate attention.

Assembly acknowledges sanitation problem

The Assembly Member for the area, Hon. Kofi Kumi, acknowledged that sanitation remains a challenge in Eyipe.

He said the community does not have enough dustbins to provide residents with adequate facilities for proper waste disposal.

He also identified the absence of Zoomlion waste collection services as another challenge, saying the lack of regular collection makes it difficult to manage waste generated by households.

Despite these challenges, he said community clean-up exercises are organised regularly and residents are encouraged to participate.

However, residents say the clean-up exercises provide only temporary relief because the community continues to face difficulties with regular waste collection and disposal.

Public health concerns

The sanitation situation has also raised concerns about the health of residents.

A sanitation officer who spoke about the situation presented records of cholera and diarrhoea cases and explained the health risks associated with poor sanitation.

Improper waste disposal and open defecation can create conditions that increase the spread of disease. For residents living near areas where rubbish accumulates, sanitation is therefore a public health issue as much as an environmental one.

Concerns over coastal pollution

Eyipe’s proximity to the sea adds another dimension to the sanitation challenge.

Waste dumped near the shoreline and wastewater discharged carelessly can eventually enter the marine environment, raising concerns about coastal pollution and its potential impact on marine life.

The situation also threatens the cleanliness of an environment that supports the livelihoods and daily activities of people in the community.

Calls for a lasting solution

The sanitation challenges in Eyipe are linked to several factors, including improper waste disposal, the cost of waste collection, inadequate disposal facilities and limited regular waste collection services.

Addressing the situation will therefore require more than periodic clean-up exercises.

Residents need access to adequate waste bins, reliable waste collection services and affordable disposal options. Continuous public education could also encourage households to adopt safer waste disposal practices.

The concerns about open defecation further highlight the need for access to suitable toilet facilities and sustained sanitation education.

For residents, the ultimate goal is not simply to have a clean community immediately after a clean-up exercise. They want a system that keeps the community clean throughout the year.

As Eyipe continues to confront its sanitation challenges, the issue has become a reminder that public health and environmental protection are closely connected.

For a community located beside the sea, addressing poor sanitation is not only about improving the appearance of the community. It is about protecting residents, preserving the coastline and ensuring a healthier environment for future generations.

By Daniella Adoma Sarpong

Ghana News.title: My studio caught fire after I ignored God’s warning to ditch secular music – Perez Musik
Ghana News.content:
Gospel musician Perez Musik

Gospel musician Perez Musik has recounted how a fire that destroyed his recording studio became a turning point in his decision to leave secular music and focus on his Christian faith.

Speaking on The Career Trail on Joy Learning TV and Joy News, Perez Musik said he had received what he described as several prophetic warnings to turn away from secular music, but continued recording artistes at his studio.

“I had been getting prophecies that you need to start doing the work of God and I've been stubborn. Because I was enjoying the secular, recording the boys in the area. Article Wan and all. They used to come to my studio to record,” he recalled.

He said the studio was later destroyed by fire after he had invested money in new equipment.

Perez Musik recalled receiving money for his work as a sound engineer on Anita Erskine's Fashion 101. He decided to use part of the money to upgrade his studio.

According to him, he had an uneasy feeling before purchasing the equipment but proceeded with the purchase.

“Just when I stepped into the shop, I heard a voice. ‘So these equipment that you're going to buy, if it catches fire and everything gets burned, what will you do?’ But I still went ahead and bought the equipment,” he said.

He said the studio caught fire on 24 December.

“I woke up in the morning, everything was fine. I was just going to pick something. I came back, the studio was on fire,” he recalled.

Although the incident was painful, Perez Musik said he came to regard it as a turning point in his life.

“It realigned my thinking. It changed my perspective on life. That, you know, material things are not things that you can hold on to. There's something higher. There's something greater. There's something more, which is Christ,” he said.

He subsequently became more involved in church activities, prayer and Bible study. He also said he quit drinking and smoking as he took his Christian faith more seriously.

Perez Musik said he had long believed he possessed a prophetic gift but had resisted the responsibility he associated with it.

“I knew the gift was there. It's just that I was shying away from the responsibility and the requirement that comes with the gift,” he said.

His spiritual transformation eventually influenced his music.

“Then I started doing the urban gospel. My first album, Tenacity, was an urban gospel. So that was when everything started. From there it's been one song after the other,” he said.

He also explained how he adopted the name Perez, drawing inspiration from the biblical account of Tamar and Judah in Genesis.

Perez said the name represented breakthrough and reflected what he regarded as his transition from his previous lifestyle into a new one centred on his faith.

World.title: Trump pleads not guilty to 34 felony counts
World.content:
News outlets will not be allowed to broadcast former President Donald Trump’s arraignment on Tuesday in a New York state court, a judge said Monday night, but he will allow some photographers to take pictures in the courtroom before the proceedings formally begin.

Acting New York Supreme Court Judge Juan Merchan rejected the request by several media organizations, including CNN, for permission to broadcast the historic proceedings. Trump’s arraignment — like most arraignments in the Manhattan courthouse — is a public proceeding, but news cameras are not usually allowed to broadcast from inside the courtroom.

However, the judge is allowing five pool photographers to take still photos at the beginning of the proceedings “until such time as they are directed to vacate the jury box by court personnel.”

Earlier on Monday, Trump’s lawyers urged the judge to reject the media’s request for live cameras in the courtroom. The Manhattan District Attorney’s office told the judge they didn’t have a position.

The media outlets that tried to get cameras into the courtroom argued that “the gravity of this proceeding … and, consequently, the need for the broadest possible public access, cannot be overstated.”

Trump is now in Manhattan ahead of the arraignment. A grand jury indicted the former president last week.

The arraignment is also expected to bring the unsealing of the criminal charges against Trump, which have not yet been seen by his lawyers or the public.

The indictment stems from Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg’s investigation into hush-money payments, made during the 2016 presidential campaign, to women who claimed they had extramarital affairs with Trump, which he denies.

Trump denies all wrongdoing and his lawyers said last week that they’ll fight to get the charges dropped.

World.content:
A Ukrainian tank is seen near the frontline area amid the Russia-Ukraine war, in Bakhmut, Ukraine, on April 02. (Muhammed Enes Yildirim/Anadolu Agency/Getty Images)

The Ukrainian military has reported little change to the front lines but heavy fire from Russian forces at various parts of the front line in the Donetsk region.

The General Staff said that more than 45 enemy attacks had been repelled over the past day, with the focus on Lyman, Bakhmut, Avdiivka and Mariinka.

It said there were 17 air strikes and more than 20 strikes by multiple launch rocket systems.

“In the Bakhmut direction, the enemy is trying to take full control over the city of Bakhmut and continues to storm it,” the General Staff said.

West of the city, Ukrainian defense forces repelled about 20 enemy attacks, according to the General Staff.

Oleksandr Syrskyi, commander of Ukrainian Land Forces, posted on Telegram that in Bakhmut he had met with “soldiers and commanders who destroyed the myth of invincibility of the Wagner fighters and Russian paratroopers.”

“The enemy is weakening and trying to cover up its failures with new fakes about the capture of Bakhmut,” Syrskyi said.

Syrskyi referenced the possibility of a future counter-offensive, saying that “the forward movement of our entire army depends on what every soldier is doing right now on their section of the front.”

Some of the most intense fighting is to the northwest and west of the city of Donetsk – as the Russians continue months-long efforts to dislodge Ukrainian defenses in Avdiivka and Mariinka. The General Staff said that some 20 assaults had been repelled.

“There are also some operational successes of our military in the Donetsk area. Our military have taken some positions. They have taken a more strategic and favourable position,” said Oleksii Dmytrashkivskyi, spokesperson for the military in that zone.

He also noted that Russian special forces had been introduced in the area.

“The enemy is trying to attack our positions between Avdiivka and Marinka. These attempts do not stop. It should be noted that the enemy has suffered quite significant losses,” Dmytrashkivskyi said.

He also claimed that the Russians “don’t have the same amount of equipment and, as they themselves say, they are on a ‘diet’ of ammunition for assaults.”

Social media video showed both sides engaged in heavy fire in the Avdiivka area, which the Russians have surrounded on three sides.

Denis Pushilin, the leader of the self-declared Donetsk People’s Republic, claimed that Russian forces were still advancing in the Avdiivka direction.

“It is still premature to speak of encirclement, but the situation is being created, if not critical, then extremely difficult for the enemy… After clearing Kamianka, our units are moving further. There are difficulties both with the terrain, which must also be overcome, and there are also similarities with weather conditions. But these difficulties are mutual — both for the enemy and for us,” Pushilin said.

World.title: Suspected Chinese spy balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing
World.content:
Washington —

The Chinese spy balloon that transited the US earlier this year was able to capture imagery and collect some signals intelligence from US military sites, a source familiar with the matter tells CNN.

The balloon was able to transmit information back to Beijing in real time, the source said, and the US government still does not know for sure whether the Chinese government could wipe the balloon’s data as it received it. That raises questions about whether there is intelligence the balloon was able to gather that the US still doesn’t know about.

Still, the intelligence community has not been overly concerned about the information the balloon was able to gather, the person said, because it is not much more sophisticated than what Chinese satellites are able to glean as they orbit over similar locations.

A US intelligence official told CNN on Monday that “although analysis of the wreckage of the High Altitude Balloon remains ongoing, thus far, its flight over the United States does not appear to have provided critical new insights to the People’s Republic of China.”

The US also knew what the balloon’s path would be and was able to protect sensitive sites and censor some signals before the balloon was able to pick them up, officials have said.

As CNN has reported, the US intelligence community last year developed a method of tracking what it says is a fleet of these Chinese balloons operating across the globe, controlled by the Chinese military.

The FBI is still examining the balloon, but so far officials have been able to glean additional information about how the device worked, including the algorithms used for the balloon’s software and how it is powered and designed.

CNN has reached out to the National Security Council at the White House and the Pentagon for comment. NBC was first to report on the new intelligence.

Video Ad Feedback Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33 • Source: CNN Justin Trudeau on what the world needs to do to handle China's threats 1:33

The balloon first crossed into US airspace over Alaska in late January before passing through Canada and down into Montana, where it hovered for a few days, leading the US to believe it was trying to surveil sensitive military sites, like Malmstrom Air Force Base in Montana. It was eventually shot down by the US off the East Coast on February 4, and the incident further escalated tensions between Washington and Beijing, including the postponement of a diplomatic visit by US Secretary of State Antony Blinken to China.

A senior State Department official said in February that, as the balloon floated across the US, it “was capable of conducting signals intelligence collection operations.”

Gen. Glen VanHerck, the commander of US Northern Command and NORAD, said at the time that the US “did not assess” that the balloon “presented a significant collection hazard beyond what already exists in actionable technical means from the Chinese.”

The surveillance program, which includes a number of similar balloons, is in part run out of the small Chinese province of Hainan, officials told CNN. The US does not know the precise size of the fleet of Chinese surveillance balloons, but sources tell CNN that the program has conducted at least two dozen missions over at least five continents in recent years.

Roughly half a dozen of those flights have been within US airspace, although not necessarily over US territory, according to one official familiar with the intelligence.

China has maintained that the balloon was actually just a weather balloon thrown off course, and the US has been assessing the possibility that it was not deliberately maneuvered into the continental US by the Chinese government, CNN has reported.

Still, China did maintain some ability to maneuver the balloon, officials believe. And once the balloon was over Montana, China appeared to take advantage of its position to loiter over sensitive sites and try to collect intelligence.

This story has been updated with additional reporting.

World.title: Beijing promised to 'fight back' over Taiwan leader's US visit. But this time it has more to lose
World.content:
Hong Kong —

An anticipated meeting between Taiwan’s President Tsai Ing-wen and US House Speaker Kevin McCarthy in California this week has sparked concerns of a repeat of the pressure campaign China launched last year when then-Speaker Nancy Pelosi visited Taipei.

At that time, Beijing encircled the island democracy with unprecedented military drills – firing multiple missiles into its surrounding waters and sending dozens of warplanes speeding across a sensitive median line dividing the Taiwan Strait.

It also cut off contact with the United States over a number of issues from military matters to combating climate change, in retaliation for what it viewed as a violation of its sovereignty.

This time, Beijing has already threatened to “resolutely fight back” if a Tsai-McCarthy meeting goes ahead.

Video Ad Feedback See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32 • Source: CNN See why tensions are rising between US and China over Taiwan 2:32

It also slammed Washington for allowing Tsai to stopover in the US while en route to and from official visits in Central America, warning it could lead to “serious” confrontation between the two powers.

A defiant Tsai staked out her own ground, pledging as she took off on her 10-day trip not to let “external pressure” stop Taiwan from connecting with the world and like-minded democracies.

But the optics of the meeting, taking place in California and not Taiwan, and its timing – at a particularly thorny moment in China’s foreign relations and ahead of a presidential election in Taiwan that could reset the tone of its relationship with Beijing – may see Beijing tread more carefully this time, or at least not escalate further, analysts say.

“This puts the burden on China not to overreact, because any overreaction is only going to push China further away from the world,” said Yun Sun, director of the China Program at the Stimson Center think tank in Washington.

That doesn’t mean, however, that Beijing won’t be closely watching Tsai’s movements as it calibrates its response – and decides how much military might to flex over her meeting with an American lawmaker on American soil.

The opacity of China’s system – and the potential for competing interests within its vast bureaucracy – also make it difficult to accurately predict its response.

“Every time Taiwan does anything that China doesn’t like, the Chinese react with their own military coercion,” Sun said. But in the current situation, “they have to consider the consequences of overreaction,” she added.

House Speaker Kevin McCarthy talks to reporters at the Capitol in Washington on March 24, 2023. J. Scott Applewhite/AP

Rising pressure

The expected meeting, which McCarthy’s office announced earlier this week would take place on Wednesday, also comes at a precarious moment in US-China relations.

Washington and Beijing are struggling to stabilize their communication amid flaring tensions over issues from a downed suspected Chinese surveillance balloon to semiconductor supply chains – raising the stakes of potential damage to that relationship if Beijing lashes out as it did when Tsai met Pelosi.

Taiwan is still feeling the fallout of that response last August, with Chinese military forces now regularly making incursions over what had previously been an informal but largely respected border of control between Beijing and Taipei in the Taiwan Strait. Taiwan’s official Central News Agency also reported Monday that Tsai would meet with McCarthy, citing Tsai’s presidential office.

Video Ad Feedback See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05 • Source: CNN See image of a Chinese balloon hovering over Taiwan 3:05

But a meeting between Tsai and the leader of the Republican majority in the US House of Representatives, who ranks second in line to the Presidency, would mark another symbolic moment for Taiwan and the US, which only maintain unofficial ties.

For Tsai, who is entering the final year of her two-term presidency, “it’s clearly a capstone event,” according to Wen-Ti Sung, a political scientist at the Australian National University’s Taiwan Studies Program. “She has this image as the Taiwanese president who has taken US-Taiwan relations to new heights, and who … has been able to give Taiwan almost unprecedented international visibility,” he said.

That increased visibility – and enhanced cooperation with the US – has followed China’s mounting pressure on the island, which sits fewer than 110 miles (177 kilometers) from the mainland coast.

China’s Communist Party claims the self-governing island democracy as its own despite never having controlled it, and has vowed to take the island, by force if necessary.

The party has undertaken a sweeping expansion of its military capabilities over the past decade under leader Xi Jinping – and ramped up its pervasive economic, diplomatic and military pressure on Taiwan.

That’s driven concerns, among some in Washington, that Beijing is preparing for an invasion, though China’s official language still suggests that scenario is not its preferred option for achieving the claimed goal of “reunification.”

It is those pressures – and how to support Taiwan against unilateral actions by Beijing – that are likely to be on the table when Tsai, McCarthy and a bipartisan group of US lawmakers sit down on Wednesday.

Congress has been a pillar of increasing American support for Taiwan in recent years. Lawmakers regularly visit the island and drive bipartisan legislation enhancing support and cooperation.

While the US switched its diplomatic relations to Beijing decades ago, it maintains unofficial ties with Taiwan and is bound by law to provide the democratic island with the means to defend itself.

Under Washington’s longstanding “One China” policy, the US acknowledges China’s position that Taiwan is part of China, but has never officially recognized Beijing’s claim to the island of 23 million.

Though McCarthy does not have Pelosi’s decades-long record of advocacy regarding China, the California Republican is now a leading voice pushing for closer scrutiny of Beijing, and meeting Tsai could help him to burnish that image.

Last month, McCarthy told reporters that meeting Tsai in the US would not impact whether he travels to Taiwan in the future – something he had earlier said he wanted to do.

Fighter jets of the Chinese People's Liberation Army Eastern Theater Command conduct joint combat training exercises around Taiwan on August 7, 2022 in this photo released by Xinhua News Agency. Gong Yulong/Xinhua/AP

Beijing watching

A meeting in California, on US soil, is widely seen as less likely to provoke Beijing than a McCarthy visit to Taiwan.

Pelosi’s trip – the first from a lawmaker of that rank to the island in 25 years – generated a fever pitch of nationalist and anti-US rhetoric in mainland China.

This time, so far, domestic conversation in China’s heavily controlled media sphere has been significantly muted.

But the stakes remain high – including for Beijing itself – over how it responds, analysts say.

As Taiwan prepares for a presidential election in January, a fierce response could push voters away from Taiwan’s main opposition party Kuomintang (KMT), widely seen as more friendly toward Beijing.

It could also jar with another high profile trip happening now: a tour of mainland China from former Taiwan president and senior KMT member Ma Ying-jeou, the first visit from a current or former Taiwan leader since the end of the Chinese Civil War in 1949.

Ma’s tour is a “once in a half a century opportunity to send a conciliatory message between the two sides, Beijing shouldn’t want to tank that,” said Sung, the political scientist.

China is also acutely aware that its actions toward Taiwan are under a significantly brighter global spotlight following the invasion of Ukraine by Russian President Vladimir Putin, a close diplomatic partner of Xi. Putin’s rhetoric over Ukraine has echoes of how Xi speaks of Taiwan.

Beijing has recently sought to position itself as an agent of peace in that conflict – especially as it aims to repair frayed ties with Europe.

This week, as Tsai is expected to meet with McCarthy, French President Emmanuel Macron and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen will head to China – an important opportunity that Xi may not want to overshadow with military posturing.

An aggressive response also risks stoking confrontation with the US, not yet six months after Xi and US President Joe Biden called to enhance communication during a face-to-face meeting in Bali.

“(A less overtly aggressive response) would imply that Beijing does not wish to escalate tension with the US to a level that can risk getting out of hand,” said Steve Tsang, director of the SOAS China Institute in London.

“A reset in US-China ties is not on the agenda, but an easing of tension is not beyond the realm of possibility.”

World.title: Trump reveals Karoline Leavitt to step down as White House press secretary
World.content:
Leavitt is departing her role to spend more time with family after giving birth to her second child, according to Trump.

White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt will be departing her role at the end of the month to prioritise her family, United States President Donald Trump announced on Truth Social.

“Karoline has been a real leader in the White House, and has done a phenomenal job fighting for Justice, Liberty, and Freedom, since 2018,” Trump wrote in a post on Wednesday, revealing the staffing shake-up.

He noted that Leavitt would remain one of his “top outside advisors” and an “influential voice within the Republican Party”.

Leavitt is the latest in a series of senior Trump officials to step down from his second administration.

Since the start of this year, high-level figures like former Attorney General Pam Bondi and ex-Secretary of Homeland Security Kristi Noem have been fired.

Other officials — including former Secretary of Labour Lori Michelle Chavez-DeRemer and Todd Lyon, acting head of Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) — have resigned amid scrutiny over their leadership.

Leavitt’s departure, however, comes on the heels of her maternity leave. She and her spouse Nicholas Riccio gave birth to their second child, a baby girl named Viviana, in early May.

The 27-year-old stepped away from her duties as White House press secretary in late April. She returned to the White House podium for her first formal press briefing in mid-July.

“Karoline has been one of the best White House Press Secretaries in the History of the Office”, Trump said in his post.

He added that Leavitt would continue to serve his administration as the Republican Party seeks to “conclusively win the Midterm Elections” in November.



Leavitt has been a presence in Trump’s inner circle since his first term in office. She started as an intern, serving in the White House Office of Presidential Correspondence, and from there, her career quickly advanced.

By the end of Trump’s first term in January 2021, Leavitt was a spokesperson for the White House, serving as an assistant press secretary.

Her relationship with Trump continued even after he was voted out of office in the 2020 presidential election. She worked in communications for MAGA Inc, a super PAC named after Trump’s “Make America Great Again” movement, and in 2021, she launched a bid to serve New Hampshire in the US House of Representatives.

While she won the state’s Republican primary for New Hampshire’s first congressional district, she was ultimately defeated in the 2022 midterm election by incumbent Democrat Chris Pappas.

When Trump launched his 2024 bid for a second term as president, Leavitt supported his campaign as its primary spokesperson. Upon his inauguration in 2025, she became the youngest person ever to act as White House press secretary, assuming the role at age 27.

Her style at the White House podium has been described as “combative”, and she developed a reputation for clashing reporters during her frequent news briefings.

“I think it’s insulting that you’re trying to test my knowledge of economics and the decisions that this president has made,” she told one reporter from The Associated Press early in her tenure.

This is a developing story. More details to come.

World.title: Josh Kushner, Bob Iger, buying Los Angeles Lakers for record $12.5bn
World.content:
Billionaire Mark Walter’s sale of the NBA’s Lakers is a record-breaking valuation for a North American sports franchise.

Venture capitalist Josh Kushner and former Disney CEO Bob Iger are set to buy the Los Angeles Lakers, with the ⁠deal valued at a record $12.5bn, according to sources familiar with the matter, on Wednesday.

Billionaire Mark Walter purchased a majority stake in the NBA team last year in a deal that valued the club at $10bn, with the deal only having been approved by the board of governors in October.

Walter’s ⁠financial empire faces a federal probe, according to reports last month, examining links between investments held by his insurers and affiliates. Walter is also the owner of Major League Baseball’s Los Angeles Dodgers.

“As lifelong NBA fans, we are deeply honored for the opportunity to become stewards of the Los Angeles Lakers, one of the most iconic sports franchises in the world,” Iger and Kushner said in a statement.

“We have immense respect for the leadership and vision of [former Lakers owners] Jerry ‌and Jeanie Buss. Our long-term commitment is to build on that foundation, compete at the highest level, and serve this extraordinary team, its fans, and the city of Los Angeles.”

The two businessmen had previously been tied to a potential NBA expansion team in Las Vegas, but Wednesday’s news, which stunned fans and industry experts, seemingly ended that effort.

The deal requires sign-off from the board of governors. It is also pending due diligence by Kushner’s Thrive Eternal, a new investment strategy launched by his venture capital firm Thrive Capital, a source said.

Magic praises Iger

“I want to congratulate my good friend Bob Iger and Josh Kushner on their purchase of the Los Angeles Lakers!” Lakers great Earvin “Magic” Johnson posted on ⁠social media.



“Laker fans, you couldn’t have two better owners. I’ve known Bob personally for over 40 years – he ⁠has always loved the Lakers and basketball and he will bring championships back to LA.”

As CEO of Disney, Iger oversaw sports network ESPN and built relationships with the NBA while the company entered into multibillion-dollar broadcast deals for games. He retired from Disney in March.

Iger and his wife, Willow Bay, previously acquired a controlling stake in National Women’s Soccer League side Angel City FC.

On the court, the ⁠Lakers are in a period of transition after the league’s all-time leading scorer LeBron James left the team in the offseason to join the Philadelphia 76ers.

FIFA Fallout

The deal comes just weeks after Kushner emerged as a central ⁠figure in a controversial private equity plan involving global football governing body FIFA.

FIFA said in July ⁠it planned to create a new commercial subsidiary, valued at about $20bn, to hold the organisation’s World Cup and other event-related businesses and sell minority stakes to outside investors.

Thrive Eternal was expected to lead a group of investors. The proposed transaction could have raised more than $4bn for FIFA, with the proceeds intended in part to fund football development programmes around the ‌world.

The proposal triggered an immediate backlash from European football officials and others who objected to private investors taking an ownership stake in the commercial operations of the world’s most popular sport and threatened to become a test of FIFA President Gianni Infantino’s leadership.

FIFA later backed away from the plan after ‌the ‌criticism, though it said it would continue consulting on the proposed structure. Kushner’s brother, Jared, is US President Donald Trump’s son-in-law. Jared Kushner was not involved in the proposed deal.

World.title: Brazil orders Discord to suspend livestreams after teen’s death
World.content:
Brazil has ordered social media app Discord to suspend its livestreaming feature across the country, accusing the platform of failing to protect children and teenagers after a 13-year-old girl died by suicide following a livestream in which authorities say she was encouraged to harm herself.

Brazil’s National Data Protection Authority (ANPD) on Wednesday gave Discord three business days to suspend its “Go Live” feature and other similar video-sharing tools. Discord itself will not be blocked, but those features won’t be available to users until the company can show it has put adequate safeguards in place for minors, said the agency in a statement.

The regulator said it had found “robust evidence” that Discord failed to take reasonable steps to prevent minors from being exposed to content promoting violence, self-harm and suicide.

The order follows the death of a 13-year-old girl in central-western Brazil last month. Authorities say that during a 45-minute Discord livestream, she was encouraged to harm herself and ultimately take her own life.

Five teenagers have been arrested in connection with her death. Police said the investigation also led them to another girl “who was about to commit suicide live on the internet”, but that the police operation saved her.

Alessandro Barreto, coordinator of the Brazilian Justice Ministry’s Ciberlab intelligence unit, described the case as a “terrible failure in moderation” by Discord.

“We witnessed truly outrageous acts being broadcast online,” Barreto said.



He said the 13-year-old had first been encouraged to kill an animal and, when she could not do it, was then encouraged to kill herself, “all of it broadcast live”.

“We used to see adults grooming minors. Now, what do we see? Minors grooming other minors to commit barbaric acts,” Barreto said. “Girls are being enslaved online and coerced into committing truly barbaric acts.”

Calls for Discord to be removed

Barreto said a 14-year-old boy arrested in connection with the case was “smiling as if he had just beaten a level in a game.” He added that the parents of most of the teenagers detained had been taken completely by surprise.

Following the girl’s death, Rosangela da Silva, the wife of President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, called for Discord to be shut down and urged the judiciary to “remove this horrible network from the Internet”. Discord says it has more than 90 million daily active users worldwide.

But the ANPD said its concerns go beyond this case. The agency said Discord’s livestreams have repeatedly been used in connection with serious crimes and have put the physical and mental safety of minors at risk.

It also pointed to the way Discord’s livestreaming system works. According to the regulator, Discord cannot access the content of video streams while they are happening, meaning it cannot automatically analyse the video and detect violations in real time. Instead, the ANPD said, the platform relies on automated systems the agency described as flawed, as well as reports from users themselves.

Discord said in a statement to AFP before Wednesday’s decision that it was “cooperating with authorities in the investigation into this serious case”.

Brazil’s move against Discord is the latest example of the country taking a tougher approach to tech giants, particularly over their responsibility for what happens on their platforms.

In 2024, Brazil blocked X for 40 days, until the company complied with Supreme Court orders to remove accounts accused of spreading disinformation. The crackdown has angered United States President Donald Trump, who has accused Brazil of targeting American social media companies and cited that as one of the reasons for imposing tariffs on Brazilian goods.

World.title: Iraq says September 30 withdrawal deadline for US-led coalition ‘final’
World.content:
A US official confirmed that the United States expects to complete its pullout by September 30, AP reported.

Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi has said that the September 30 deadline for ending the US-led international coalition’s military mission in Iraq and completing the withdrawal of its forces is “fixed and final”.

The remarks on Wednesday came after al-Zaidi’s meeting with US Central Command Commander General Brad Cooper, the Iraqi prime minister’s office said in a post on X.

The withdrawal would mark the end of a presence that started with the 2003 US-led invasion against Saddam Hussein. In 2024, Washington and Baghdad agreed to wind down the much smaller US-led operations against the ISIL (ISIS) armed group.

“September 30 will be the fixed and final date for ending the military mission of the Global Coalition to Defeat ISIS in Iraq and completing the departure of its forces,” said the statement from the prime minister’s office.

“October 1 will mark a new day in the trajectory of the Iraqi state, as Iraq will be free of any foreign military presence,” it added.

Placing all weapons under exclusive state control “represents an essential prerequisite for moving Iraq into a new phase of development and prosperity”, the statement read.

The office added that both sides agreed to the deadline of the mission, as discussed during al-Zaidi’s visit to Washington, DC, in mid-July.

Al-Zaidi and Cooper stressed that Iraqi-US ties would shift toward economic and security cooperation based on mutual respect for sovereignty and shared interests, it added.

A US official told The Associated Press news agency that the US expects to complete its pullout by September 30, but declined to say how many troops remain in Iraq or where they would be redeployed.



“The United States, Iraq and coalition partners have achieved tremendous success in defeating ISIS and now the Iraqi security forces, including the Peshmerga and other Iraqi Kurdistan Region security forces, will lead the fight against terrorists in Iraq,” the official said, The AP reported.

US troops pulled out of bases in most areas of Iraq last year but maintained a presence in the semi-autonomous northern Kurdish region.

Bases there have regularly come under attack since the US and Israel launched the war on Iran on February 28.

The US presence in Iraq grew to more than 170,000 troops at the peak of counterinsurgency operations in 2007.

In December 2011, the final combat troops departed. But in 2014, the rise of the ISIL group and its capture of a wide swath across Iraq and Syria brought US forces back at the Iraqi government’s invitation.

After ISIL lost its hold on territory it once claimed, coalition military operations ended in 2021.
