World.title: Derick Hougaard starts new hustle after GoFundMe backlash
World.content:
Derick Hougaard has launched a new side hustle. Images via Facebook

Former Springbok Derick Hougaard has revealed a new business venture in the wake of backlash against a GoFundMe campaign, that appealed for public donations.

The retired rugby player has made headlines in recent weeks after claiming to be in “big trouble”

Derick – once known as the “Liefling van Loftus” – hung up his boots in 2015 amid a series of health concerns. Since then, he has made headlines over his personal life.



DERICK HOUGAARD LAUNCHES NEW BUSINESS VENTURE

On his Facebook account Derick Hougaard shared a post about his new side hustle, endorsing a new business directory app, called Wha2do.

The start-up app was created by Limpopo businessman, Lesley Bernard, who encouraged South Africans to support the rugby player’s new gig.

“Today, there is a new way for Derick to live out his love for South Africa,” an excerpt on the business read.

In recent months, Derick Hougaard has also shared his expertise as a coach on several rugby coaching programmes.

FINDING HIS FEET ATFTER RUGBY

Derick Hougaard has previously spoken about hos his rugby career was “cut short” following a series of injuries, particularly concussions

The flyhalf transitioned into rugby coaching and sports commentary as many former players do.

However, his gig as a SuperSport commentator was terminated over his controversial comments about trasnformation in rugby.

In 2020, Derick Hougaard shared his plan to get into the NFL league in the US.

He stated that would attend the World Wide Scholarships (WWS) talent scouting camp in South Africa in the hopes of transitioning from converting from rugby flyhalf to an American-football kicker/punter.

“All athletes dream of a second chance and this is mine”, he said at the time.

He added: “I still have five years left in me.”

A year later, his dream appeared to have fizzled out.

Over the next few years, Derick confused to battling an addiction to booze and prescription pills.

After a 2023 health scare, Derick’s medical and rehabilitation bills likely started accumulating, possibly in addition to his inability to work.

His life’s story, including his struggles with mental and physical health, financial setbacks, susbtance abuse, and failed relationships, weres told via a kykNET documentary and biography that both came out in 2023.

World.title: Mamelodi Sundowns sell Bafana Bafana star for R28 million
World.content:
Mamelodi Sundowns have reportedly agreed to sell Thapelo Maseko to Danish giants FC Copenhagen.

The 22-year-old winger has fallen out of favour at Masandawana but revived his career during a loan spell at AEL Limassol last season.

His impressive form in Cyprus also saw him earn a recall to the Bafana Bafana squad, where he featured in several matches during the FIFA World Cup.



One of his most memorable moments came when he scored against South Korea in Bafana’s 1-0 victory, helping the team reach the knockout stages for the first time.

Following the tournament, Maseko was linked with several clubs, including teams in Europe and North Africa. However, it was reported that Sundowns were reluctant to sell the Bafana Bafana international to any of their domestic rivals.

On Wednesday, iDiski Times reported that Sundowns had agreed to sell Maseko to Copenhagen for a fee of R28 million.

Maseko would become the latest South African to join the Danish club. Sibusiso Zuma previously played for Copenhagen in the early 2000s and went on to become a club legend.

Maseko joined Sundowns from SuperSport United but struggled for regular game time at Chloorkop and was eventually loaned out last season. Injuries also played a role in limiting the speedy winger’s opportunities with the Brazilians.

Now, after reviving his career at AEL Limassol, Maseko appears set for a new chapter in Europe with Copenhagen after a €1.5 million agreement with the Premier League Giants.



Will Maseko make it in Denmark or should have stayed in Chloorkop?

World.title: Prison warden busted with condoms, libido pills and drugs worth R65K
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - A 47-year-old prison warden has been arrested in the Western Cape after he was allegedly busted with 60 libido tablets, drugs vaulted at approximately R65, 000 and other items in his vehicle.

The arrest happened on Wednesday during a targeted roadblock at Goodwood Prison.

It was conducted by members of the SAPS Anti-Gang Unit and the Department of Correctional Services Emergency Support Team.

READ | R1m drug bust in Phoenix: Mandrax, cocaine and heroin seized

According to Western Cape spokesperson Frederick van Wyk, the operation took place at about 6.40am when the warden’s vehicle was stopped and searched.

"The members found 600 mandrax tablets, 100 grams of tik, 300 grams of dagga, 23 cellular telephones, three earpod pairs, five USB memory sticks, 10 condoms and 60 libido tablets in the warden’s vehicle," Van Wyk said.

He said the prison warden has been detained at Goodwood SAPS and will appear before court once charged.

World.title: NSFAS faces R15bn student-funding gap
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - NSFAS does not have enough money to fund all qualifying students, as it faces a student funding shortfall.

This is according to the Minister of Higher Education, Buti Manamela, who warned that the financial aid scheme is facing an estimated R15 billion student-funding gap across universities and TVET colleges.

He said universities account for the overwhelming majority of the requirement.

READ | NSFAS praises staff for exposing alleged laptop theft

Manamela was briefing the Parliament's Portfolio Committee on Higher Education on Wednesday on the progress in stabilising NSFAS, which still remains under administration.

According to Manamela, the problem runs deeper than money being overspent.

He said a report has indicated that there is what he described as a ‘structural mismatch’ between the number of qualifying students requiring support, the baseline allocation and the disappearance of once-off funding sources supported in previous years.

READ | NSFAS opens theft case against former board member

This, he said, does not “absolve NSFAS of the obligation to control expenditure, verify liabilities and operate within the law.”

“The immediate second-semester funding requirement must therefore be dealt with separately from the broader structural shortfall. "Qualifying students cannot simply be abandoned because a long-term funding problem remains unresolved; but neither can government resolve a structural problem through repeated emergency interventions,” he said.

Manamela confirmed that he had received the Administrator's Initial Stabilisation Plan.

He said the plan outlines correct systemic problems including weakness in governance, financial controls, accommodations well as appeals and provides a useful strategic framework.

READ | Not the first time| How Nsfas ended up under administration again

Despite the submission of the Plan, Manamela cautioned that it does not mean that stabilisation at NSFAS has been achieved

World.title: Madlanga Commission turns spotlight on taxi boss Joe ‘Ferrari’ Sibanyoni
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Notorious Mpumalanga taxi boss Joe 'Ferrari' Sibanyoni needs to provide answers to the Madlanga Commission.



Sibanyoni needs to answer queries about alleged criminal syndicates and his association with Jothan "King Mswazi" Msibi and Steven Motsumi.



Sibanyoni received a Rule 10.6 notice from the commion last week.



“The Commission does not comment publicly on the preparations it may or may not be making with regard to the testimony or appearance of witnesses, unless a particular matter is ventilated in an open hearing," said commission spokesperson Jeremy Michaels.



“Similarly, the Commission does not provide details of whether a specific witness may or may not be appearing before it.”

World.title: Power outages disrupt these Gauteng healthcare facilities
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - Power outages have disrupted healthcare services across Gauteng.

The provincial health department blamed severe weather and pressure on the grid for the outages, with Johannesburg the hardest hit.

Affected clinics include Eyethu Yarona, Diepsloot South, Tshepisong, and Moroka Clinic in Soweto.

Winnie Mandela Clinic in Ekurhuleni is also without power tonight.

According to Gauteng department of health spokesperson Steve Mabona, backup generators are helping keep essential services running.

READ | Cold, wet weather delays power restoration in parts of Joburg

According to the first four health facilities in Johannesburg District have resorted to using backup generators to ensure that health services continue.

At Winnie Mandela Clinic, technical teams have been deployed and are attending to the facility's generator to ensure that the backup power system is restored, Mabona added.

Mabona said the department continues to monitor the readiness of backup power systems across health facilities, including generator functionality and fuel availability.

World.title: Rand shows resilience amid Middle East conflict
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The rand is showing remarkable resilience amid conflict in the Middle East.

It traded below R16.20 to the dollar, its strongest level since early July.

The currency has been supported by easing expectations of further US interest rate hikes and improving investor sentiment.

The rand has also shrugged off uncertainty surrounding the conflict in the Middle East and developments around the Strait of Hormuz.

READ | Calls grow for tighter oversight as Treasury releases R7.1bn

The currency came under pressure last month after the Reserve Bank unexpectedly kept interest rates unchanged while warning about inflation risks.

Higher oil prices linked to the Iran conflict also weighed on sentiment, given South Africa's reliance on imported fuel.

However, analysts say stronger gold prices, relatively healthy public finances and confidence in the Reserve Bank's inflation-targeting framework continue to support the rand.

World.title: 'His allegations are far-fetched' - Parliament on Adams' claims of writing to speaker
World.content:
CAPE TOWN - Parliament has disputed National Coloured Congress leader Fadiel Adams' claims that he wrote to the National Assembly Speaker about the Political Killings Task Team (PKTT).

Speaking to eNCA on Wednesday, Adams said had written to the speaker months ago on questioning why the PKTT had allegedly broken the authority of Parliament?

But he said he never got a response.

He said that this was not the first time he had written to Parliament, this as he claims he cited concerns over an increase in salary of secretary of Parliament.

But Parliament spokesperson Moloto Mothapo said there is no record of any communication from Adams to the Speaker’s office.

He further described Adams' allegations as 'far-fetched'

According to Mothapo office bearers, do not determine their own salaries, neither does the Speaker nor any member of Parliament, a magistrate or a member of the judiciary.

"There is an independent commission that is established exactly for that. Whether it's a determination of a salary or an annual increase, there is an independent commission that does that" "On the alleged salary increase or the PKTT matter there is no evidence of such correspondence," he said.

Parliament's comment comes amid other claims Adams made at the Madlanga Commission.

Adams told the commission that his faulty device had caused him to miss critical emails.

He further added that he had to rely on phone calls and colleagues for updates about his work.

This he said contributed to the delay in his response to the commission.

But Parliament disputed the claim saying Information and Communications Technology (ICT) records showed no evidence of persistent malfunction or repeated repairs.

It said the logged issues were mainly password, login and Wi-Fi problems and that Adams had access to other devices to maintain his work.

World.title: R1m drug bust in Phoenix: Mandrax, cocaine and heroin seized
World.content:
DURBAN - More than R1 million worth of drugs has been seized in Phoenix, north of Durban.

A 39-year-old man has been arrested at a property on Rinkford Road.

The Durban Metro Police Tactical Support Unit carried out the operation.

Police said the unit gathered intelligence from drug buyers in the area.

A search warrant was obtained after weeks of investigation.

Mandrax tablets, cocaine and heroin were seized during the operation.

World.title: Alleged cop killer faces bail battle after Reiger Park murders
World.content:
JOHANNESBURG - The state intends to oppose bail for Regan Collis, the 23-year-old suspected of killing four people, including two police officers, in Reiger Park.



Collis made his first appearance in the Boksburg Magistrate's Court.

READ: 'Policemen are on the payroll of the gangsters' - Reiger Park community leader



He faces nine charges, including four counts of murder.



The case has been postponed to 25 August for a bail application.

World.title: Court dismisses bid to strike out duty-free rice import case
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

National Treasury CS John Mbadi issued a gazette notice allowing the importation of 500,000 metric tons of duty-free milled white rice. [Courtesy]

The High Court has declined to strike out a case challenging the government’s decision to allow duty-free rice into the country.

Justice Edward Muriithi, in his ruling, said that the case by Kirinyaga Senator Kamau Murango was weighty as it questions the legitimacy of the government’s interest to ensure food security in the country as measured against the legitimate expectation that they would sell their products without losses owing to flooding of exported commodities.

“It would appear that this apparent intersection (or conflict) of rights caused by the Cabinet Secretary for Treasury in repeatedly publishing the Gazette Notices subject of the constitutional challenge herein and in other suits gives rise to questions in terms of Article 165(4) whether it was a valid exercise of authority within the meaning of the Constitution and whether the Gazette authority to import rice duty-free infringes upon the farmers’ right to property through resultant price drops affecting the marketability and profitability returns of the local farmers’ rice growing activity,” ruled Justice Muriithi.

This comes as two separate cases were filed questioning the government’s fresh green light to importers to bring into the country 4,900 tons of rice. Rice farmers say the country has more than enough rice to feed Kenyans. They complained that the move was to flood the market.

In the case before Justice Muriithi, the government claimed that the court had no powers to entertain the claims as this was an administrative issue. It also argued that several cases had been filed in different courts, hence, an abuse of court process.

On July 28, 2025, the National Treasury Cabinet Secretary John Mbadi issued a gazette notice allowing the importation of 500,000 metric tons of duty-free milled white rice.

The notice has created a circus, with the judiciary as the playing field.

The cases that were filed in different courts tell of a food crop that has turned out to be hotter than a potato.

Kenya produces 244,000 metric tons of rice, against a consumption demand of at least 1 billion. This creates a window for businesses to import rice worth Sh55 billion.

Mbadi allowed duty-free rice because the government needed to close the market gap. However, those opposed to it claim that there is enough rice, and the importation window was made to create a glut in the country, which would harm rice farmers.

So far, the rice import has attracted six cases. The drama, which is now full-blown, has seen Farmers Party opt to drop the case, only for Kirinyaga Senator Kamau Murango and MCA David Mathenge to fight in a bid to salvage it.

The political party claimed the price of grade one rice has been retailing at approximately Sh 355 and Sh 385 per Kg for imported brands and between Sh 166 and Sh 277 for locally produced rice, depending on the variety (pishori, basmati, long grain, biryani) as well as the blend.

It also claimed that the price is fully determined by market forces, as there have not been any duty-free waivers to any importers of Grade 1 rice since November of last year, with the rains being predictable.

In response, Mbadi argued that there was a need to address the rise in the cost of living. He said that the Cabinet approved a framework to position the Kenya National Trading Corporation (KNTC) as the anchor of State initiatives to create a price stabilizer for essential household food items.

According to him, rice is the third most important cereal after maize and wheat. He was of the view that about 1 million metric tons of rice in the country is imported mainly from India, Pakistan and Tanzania.

He asserted that the current retail market price ranges between Sh 190 and Sh 220 per kilogram for Grade 1 milled white rice, representing a significant increase from last year's average of Sh 150 per kilogram during the duty-free period.

He argued that Kenya needs 1.5 million tons of rice to seal the current rice deficit, adding that 95 per cent of the imported rice is basmati, which would allegedly not affect the market for local pishori rice.

Mbadi also cited food security risk in Turkana, Marsabit, North Eastern and Parts of the Coastal area.

Kerugoya High Court Judge Edward Mureithi froze clearance of the consignment.

Nevertheless, he was not the only one who had issued the orders involving the same issue. Miles away from his court, Milimani High Court Judge Chacha Mwita (now a Court of Appeal Judge)had also barred the government from bringing in the rice, in a case filed by Japheth Kirui. This was on October 14 last year.

Following the orders, the Attorney General, the Kenya Bureau of Standards, and the Agriculture Cabinet Secretary lawyers raised concern that there were five other cases filed in Mombasa, Kisumu, Milimani Commercial Court and Kerugoya by different parties, over the same issue.

This prompted Justice Mwita to order that Kirui appear before him in person on October 30, 2025.

When he took the witness box, he told the court that he was born in Kuresoi, but he sells household items at a kiosk in Embakasi.

Asked by the Judge what he knew about the case, he went mute.

AG’s lawyer, Henry Kaumba, told the Judge that Kirui was allegedly being used as a proxy.

“It is doubtful whether the petitioner knows about the case and what transpired and even the development in the proceedings that have taken place. It is unfortunate,” said Kaumba.

In his filed reply, he said 250,000 tonnes had already been shipped into the country, with others on the way in the high seas.

World.title: You have failed Kenyans, Gachagua tells Ruto
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Democracy for Citizen Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua when he read out President Ruto’s four-year score card during a media briefing at the party’s offices in Nairobi on August 11, 2026. [Kanyiri Wahito, Standard]

Democracy for Citizens Party (DCP) leader Rigathi Gachagua has accused President William Ruto of failing Kenyans and abandoning his campaign promises.

Gachagua who was speaking at the DCP headquarters accused the president of eroding democratic gains of multipartyism and swallowing opposition parties.

“Four years later, Mr. William Ruto has betrayed the trust bestowed on him by the people of Kenya, betrayed the fruits and foundation of our Nation that have been built by previous administrations under the various development blue prints such as Vision 2030,” he said.

Gachagua was addressing the press on the score card of the Kenya Kwanza administration for the four years it has been in leadership.

According to the opposition figure, President Ruto had promised to uphold the rule of law, build a secure, just and democratic Kenyan founded on the constitution but he had abandoned all of the promises.

He added that there were promises of professionalising the National Police Service, safeguarding human rights, protecting Kenyans and strengthening the administration of justice while ensuring security agencies are accountable to the constitution.

Gachagua alleged that the Kenya Kwanza administration had allowed goonism and drug abuse to thrive adding that the country had also become a bedrock of extrajudicial killings and an abductors playground.

He said that during campaigns they had promised to amend and operationalise the National Coroners Service Act of 2017 to establish the Coroner General’s office to remove the burden of probing deaths from the regular police channels and Directorate of Criminal Investigations (DCI).

Gachagua said that proposed amendments were aimed at removing potential conflict of interest and ensuring transparency in handling unexplained deaths, enforced disappearances or fatalities caused by the police.

“Four years later, this promise has not been fulfilled.”

He accused the government of overseeing the arrest and rendition of government critics from Turkey, Uganda, Tanzania and South Sudan adding that officials attached to a construction company from China were deported when they protested the awarding of a contract to rivals.

“Kenyans are not safe, our children are not safe, investors are not safe and foreigners are not safe. Foreigners are not safe, Investors are not safe, no one in Kenya is safe.”

He accused the President of limiting the freedom of the press through sponsored disinformation campaigns and also citing the attempted abduction of Standard Group’s Associated Editor Alex Kiprotich in Nakuru on June 26, 2026.

According to Gachagua the government had failed to fight corruption despite promising to do so adding that it had entrenched graft as a way of life in Kenya.

World.title: Wamboka: Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang'i should back Sifuna
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kabuchai Mp Majimbo kalasinga and his counterpart Jack Wamboka during a press briefing on Monday. [Juliet Omelo, Standard]

The political battle for the 2027 presidency has intensified, with leaders allied to the Linda Mwananchi movement urging opposition figures Kalonzo Musyoka, Rigathi Gachagua and Fred Matiang’i to abandon their presidential ambitions and back Nairobi Senator Edwin Sifuna.

Bumula MP Jack Wamboka made the call after a three-day political tour of Western Kenya by the Linda mwananchi brigade, saying the region had demonstrated growing grassroots support for Sifuna.

Wamboka said the tour was a major success, with close to 22 rallies held in three days. He added that the crowds reflected growing enthusiasm for Sifuna, particularly among young people, women, political aspirants and ordinary voters.

“We respect you, Kalonzo, Gachagua and Matiang’i. We know you have what it takes but in 2027, we ask you to stand with Sifuna,” Wamboka said.

He said the reception in Western Kenya showed that Sifuna’s campaign was gaining national attention.

The first time MP said Sifuna had focused on issues affecting Western Kenya, particularly the collapse of industries and the struggling sugar sector. He pointed to Mumias and Nzoia sugar factories, saying their decline had left farmers and workers suffering.

Wamboka accused National Assembly Speaker Moses Wetang’ula of failing to deliver development promises made to Bungoma residents citing unfinished roads and the stalled Bungoma stadium, saying several projects lacked adequate funding despite repeated commitments to voters during the campaigns.

He also questioned Wetang’ula’s political record, citing past controversies and accusing the Speaker of failing to live up to his promises adding that voters should judge leaders by what they deliver, not by speeches alone.

Kabuchai MP Majimbo Kalasinga said the tour had proved that Sifuna’s bid was gaining grassroots support.

“Edwin Sifuna is going for president, nothing else,” he said.

He said supporters contributed small amounts to the campaign, arguing that the movement was being funded by ordinary Kenyans rather than wealthy political backers. He said crowds turned up voluntarily.

Kalasinga also announced that Linda Mwananchi would hold a rally in Homa Bay on August 16 despite local warnings. He said Sifuna had a right to campaign anywhere in Kenya.

He called for peaceful competition and warned against attempts to block the rally or restrict political activity in the region emphasising that Kenya is for everyone, constitutionally, peacefully and equally.

They two vowed to fight for the Linda Mwananchi name.

The Wamboka-Kalasinga push adds momentum to Sifuna’s campaign and pressures opposition leaders to unite before the 2027 election.

World.title: Kindiki defends government's development agenda in Mt Kenya
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki and Lands Cabinet Secretary Alice Wahome at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on August 10, 2026. [Boniface Gikandi, Standard]

Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has reiterated the government’s commitment to ensure equitable development.

Prof Kindiki said that President William Ruto’s government has initiated many development projects in Mt Kenya to transform livelihoods.

“Am advising the people against being deceived to leave the government to join the opposition where nothing is being provided,” he said.

The Deputy President said the road projects which had stalled have since been revived after the government released Sh176 billion owed to contractors to ensure completion of 6,000km.

He spoke at Gaichanjiru Catholic Church in Kandara, Murang’a, on Sunday, where he was the chief guest during celebrations to mark 100 years since the establishment of Gaichanjiru Mission Hospital managed by the Catholic Diocese of Murang'a.

Kindiki, who was accompanied by Cabinet Secretaries Alice Wahome (Lands) and Rebecca Miano (Tourism), said that the government has impacted the region with affordable houses estimated at 180,000 units, modern markets and student hostels that have created employment for hundreds of skilled and unskilled persons.

He said the church has a history of partnering with the government in matters concerning development and empowerment of the less fortunate in the community.

“In Murang’a the government has ensured all the projects that KeRRA under Eng Antony Mwaura was working on are completed to give the locals value for money,” said the DP.

During the event, the President gave Sh10 million for procurement of equipment for the health facility, where more than Sh20 million was raised.

Ruto also gave Sh 50 million and directed the Housing Department to facilitate construction of the hospital's ICU, HDU, theatre and laboratory

Kindiki lauded efforts by Wahome that have seen Murang’a County benefit from Sh27 billion programmes from her ministry.

“Murang’a through her efforts has 27 modern markets, Affordable Housing Programme units, and student hostels, programmes that have engaged hundreds of persons,” he said.

World.title: Charlene Ruto's Koito lights up Kilgoris
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Ruto, is engaged to Tanzanian entrepreneur Isaiah Yunge.

The drums rolled, traditional songs filled the air and dancers swayed in colourful rhythm as Kilgoris was transformed into a spectacular theatre of love, culture, wealth and political power.

At the expansive Intonna Heritage Farm in Naserian Village, President William Ruto’s daughter, Charlene Chelagat Ruto, took a major traditional step towards marriage as the First Family hosted her Koito ak Chaik—a colourful Kalenjin engagement and farewell ceremony.

For hours, the skies above Kilgoris were punctuated by helicopters ferrying distinguished guests to the President’s family property, while luxury vehicles streamed through the gates carrying politicians, government officials, business personalities, relatives and friends.

On the ground, the mood was unmistakably festive. Traditional songs echoed across the expansive farm as dancers moved to the rhythm, colourful attire transformed the venue into a sea of elegance and culture, and guests embraced the joy of a ceremony that combined an ancient African tradition with the unmistakable grandeur of Kenya’s First Family.

It was romance wrapped in tradition—and tradition presented on a spectacular scale.

The guest list read almost like a roll call of Kenya’s political establishment. Leaving the Narok delegation was Governor Patrick Ole Ntutu, who joined Kilgoris MP Julius Sunkuli and former Narok Governor Samuel Tunai in celebrating the First Family on the special occasion.

The ceremony also brought together elected leaders from across Narok County, creating an impressive gathering of the county’s political establishment at the heart of Trans Mara.

From governors and Senators to MPs, the event brought together leaders from across the country. Top government officials and senior executives too came dressed for the ceremony

The fashion became part of the spectacle. Brown, maroon and other earthy tones dominated the scene, blending effortlessly with the traditional African setting. It was a celebration in which political leaders seemed determined to make an entrance as memorable as the occasion itself.

But beyond the political faces and the luxury was the heartbeat of the ceremony—culture. Traditional songs rang across the farm. Dancers moved with energy and precision, their performances adding colour and rhythm to a celebration centred on family and love.

The atmosphere shifted between moments of emotion and bursts of exuberance as relatives, friends and guests celebrated Charlene’s transition into a new stage of life.

The contrast was striking. Modern wealth arrived by helicopter, while ancient traditions were celebrated through song and dance. Luxury vehicles lined up outside as cultural performers entertained guests inside. Political heavyweights mingled with family elders.

Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

And amid the glamour, the central message remained simple: Charlene and her fiancé, Isaiah Yunge, had brought together not just two families but two countries.

Yunge is a Tanzanian technology entrepreneur and digital innovation enthusiast associated with Goodsam Technologies and is a co-founder of Smart Kaya LLC, a smart-home technology venture.

He has been recognised among Forbes Africa’s 30 Under 30 and received the Queen’s Young Leaders Award in 2018. His interest in technology reportedly began at an early age. At 17, he was selected as a UNICEF Africa Youth Ambassador and participated in international advocacy around children's rights.

He later pursued training in sustainable business models through the Swedish Institute, studied Leading Change at Cambridge University and became an alumnus of the Harvard Ministerial Leadership Program.

For all its glamour, the heart of the celebration remained the centuries-old tradition of Koito. Among the Kalenjin, it is a significant engagement ceremony through which the families of the bride and groom formally meet, bless the relationship, exchange gifts and discuss dowry arrangements.

It is a moment when families begin the process of becoming one. The Chaik aspect gives the occasion an emotional dimension, symbolising the farewell of a daughter as she prepares to leave her parental home and begin a new chapter with her husband. Politicians arrive for Charlene Ruto's Koito in Kilgoris. [UGC]

For Charlene, the symbolism was profound. Surrounded by her parents, family, friends and some of the country’s most powerful political figures, she was celebrated not simply as the President’s daughter, but as a daughter taking a traditional step towards marriage.

The songs, dances and blessings gave the occasion an emotional warmth that stood in contrast to the scale of the event.

Yet there was no escaping the extraordinary display of wealth surrounding the celebration. Helicopters arriving overhead. Luxury vehicles streaming through the gates. High-ranking government officials and elected leaders arriving in motorcades. Elegant outfits and carefully coordinated colours.

It was a spectacle that demonstrated the resources, networks and influence available to one of Kenya’s most powerful families. The ceremony was therefore more than a social event.

For Charlene, however, beyond the helicopters, politicians, fashion and cameras was the quiet meaning of the day.

A daughter was being prepared to leave one home and begin another. Two families were being brought together.

Love was at the centre. Culture provided the rhythm. Wealth supplied the grandeur. And political power provided the spectacle.

For one unforgettable Saturday, Charlene Ruto’s Koito turned Kilgoris into a glittering stage where romance, tradition, influence and prosperity met under the Narok sky.

World.title: Police join protest victims' Sh25.75m reparations payout
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Prof. Makau Mutua, Chairperson of the Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations. [File,Standard]

A protest reparations panel has approved compensation for 49 police officers, awarding them Sh25.75 million alongside payments to civilians who suffered human rights violations.

The Panel of Experts on Compensation of Victims of Human Rights Violations approved seven claims involving severe injuries, 37 for moderate injuries and five for minor injuries, according to an update issued Friday, August 7.

"In acknowledgement of the dedication by our uniformed officers to protecting the public, the Panel has resolved to grant appropriate compensation for the human rights violations they sustained during the period in question," the panel said.

The inclusion of police officers adds a new dimension to a compensation programme created against the backdrop of protests in which police conduct has faced scrutiny.

During protests between June 17 and July 7, 2025, the Independent Policing Oversight Authority (IPOA) recorded 65 deaths, 342 civilian injuries and 171 injuries to police officers.

IPOA said most of the deaths were linked mainly to police actions during crowd-control operations.

The compensation programme grew out of the National Dialogue Committee (NADCO) process, which sought to address political and governance tensions in Kenya.

The government later set aside Sh2 billion for victims of human rights violations linked to protests and other demonstrations between 2017 and 2025.

The panel reported that it has processed 680 claims and disbursed Sh896.1 million in compensation.

The panel listed three phases of payments as Sh448.7 million in the initial phase, Sh225.4 million in the second phase and Sh247.95 million in the third phase.

The latest phase covered 175 civilian victims and included 50 fatalities, 46 severe injuries, 49 moderate injuries, 21 minor injuries and nine economic-loss claims.

The panel reported total payments of Sh222 million for the phase.

However, 472 claims submitted through IPOA and KNCHR remain outstanding because applicants have not provided enough supporting documents.

The panel is working with IPOA regional offices to locate affected victims and their beneficiaries and obtain the documents required to process the claims.

The backlog includes 594 of the 600 economic-loss claims received by the panel. Only four have been processed and compensated.

The panel has also received nine claims under the sexual offences category. Eight have been processed and compensated while one remains pending.

Claims involving enforced disappearances remain under review because the panel says the cases require investigation and verification before they can be approved, referred for further investigation or declared ineligible.

The panel has also reclassified three claims from minor to severe after reviewing medical reports and additional submissions.

It approved above-scale compensation for five victims whose injuries it described as permanent and life-altering and said it would recommend that President Ruto include them in a government-funded lifetime medical scheme.

World.title: EACC arrests Kitui County Chief Officer over Sh17.48m procurement fraud
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors arrested by EACC. [Joh Muia, Standard]

The Ethics and Anti-Corruption Commission (EACC) has arrested Kitui County Chief Officer Gladys Mami Kivoto and five company directors over alleged conflict of interest and procurement irregularities involving Sh17.48 million contracts.

In a statement on Thursday, EACC CEO Abdi Mohamud said investigations found that Kivoto, who served in the Departments of Agriculture & Fisheries and Irrigation, allegedly traded with the county through five proxy companies: Shanel Construction Ltd, ECO Stone Ltd, AZ Links Ltd, DTK Construction Ltd, and 4-Walls Ltd.

The companies were paid a total of Sh14.1 million by the county between the 2018/2019 and 2024/2025 financial years.

EACC further established that three of the directors, Josephine Mwikali Wambua of Shanel Construction, Makoma Wambua of AZ Links and Emmanuel Wambua of ECO Stone are relatives of Kivoto. There were also financial transactions between Kivoto and directors of DTK Construction and 4-Walls.

Following investigations, the file was forwarded to the DPP, who approved charges against nine suspects, including conflict of interest, abuse of office, money laundering, and corrupt procurement.

Those arrested are Gladys Mami Kivoto, Josephine Mwikali Wambua Director, Shanel Construction, Roselyne Kyambi Kilonzi Director, Shanel Construction, Mary Mueni Mbiti Director, DTK Construction & 4-Walls, Jonathan Kivondo Kieti Director, DTK Construction and Onesmus Munyao Nzioka Director, ECO Stone.

EACC directed Makoma Wambua of ECO Stone, Emmanuel Wambua of AZ Links, and Stella Nthenya Kioko of AZ Links who are reportedly in hiding to present themselves at the EACC Lower Eastern Regional Office in Machakos or the nearest EACC office for processing.

The suspects are expected to be arraigned at the Kitui Law Courts.

World.title: High Court orders striking nurses back to work
World.content:
Audio By Vocalize

Uasin Gishu County nurses strike over delayed payments and unfulfilled Collective Bargaining Agreement [Wycliff Kipsang, Standard]

Nurses across the 47 counties have been ordered to report back to work immediately or face legal action from the counties.

Justice Monica Mbaru of the Employment and Labour Court in Mombasa issued orders temporarily stopping the nationwide nurse strike that commenced on July 29, 2026, and ordered the Kenya National Union of Nurses and Midwives (KNUNM) to direct its members back to work.

Justice Mbaru said on Wednesday that any nurse absent from work without proper and lawful cause shall face disciplinary action.

This is after Mombasa County Government and its Public Service Board successfully enjoined the 46 county governments to make the order national.

“In the interim, the KNUNM (respondent) is hereby restrained from undertaking any industrial action relating to the strike notices dated July 21 and July 29 and shall direct all its members to resume duty forthwith and unconditionally to allow the court to address the claim herein on a priority basis,” said Justice Mbaru.

The judge ordered all county labour officers in the 47 counties to record attendance of nurses who report to work and compile a report in court on September 22, 2026.

“Any member of the KNUNM who will be noted by the County Labour Officer as absent from duty without lawful cause shall allow the counties to issue necessary notice to show cause why disciplinary action should not be taken,” said Justice Mbaru.

In their petition certified urgent, Mombasa County claimed that the nurses strike has crippled services in public hospitals across all the 47 counties, thereby placing patients facing emergency and inpatient care at risk.

In Mombasa County, the nurses strike paralysed medical services at all medical facilities, including Coast General Hospital, Port Reitz Hospital, Likoni District Hospital and Shimo La Tewa GK Prison Hospital.

Mombasa County, through its Counsel Murtaza Tajbhai, said that the strike had turned from a labour disagreement to a matter of immense public interest.

Tajbhai said that the nurses’ union proceeded with the said strike despite the Mombasa Public Service Board inviting the KNUNM officials for talks to avert the said strike.

The union had raised concerns over the 2025-2029 Collective Bargaining Agreement (CBA), implementation of the 2017 Return to Work Formula and pension terms for Universal Health Coverage staff care guidelines for nurses and the reinstatement of 46 nurses dismissed in Kisii County.

However, in their petition, Mombasa County said that the said grievances could not be addressed by each county individually.

Mombasa County Service Board Chief Executive Officer Fadhil Maamum told the court in his affidavit that most of the demands required consultation with national institutions like the Salaries and Remuneration Commission, while others cannot be implemented immediately given their significant financial implications.

He said that nurses under Mombasa County have no salary arrears and had met some of the union’s demands through negotiations.

Maamum said that while the nurses’ grievances can be resolved, the patients do not have the luxury of time.

“Nurses are designated essential service providers under the Labour Relations Act and the industrial action was unlawful because the statutory dispute resolution mechanism had not been exhausted," said Maamum.

He said the court's intervention will allow for negotiations and safeguard the constitutional right to healthcare.

However, the Union said that the strike was after failed action by the counties to meet their agreed grievances despite continued negotiations.

The nurses said they will not be reporting to work unless guided by the union.

World.title: Yemen’s Huthis: More on the group who reportedly struck a vessel in the Red Sea
World.content:
Pakistan’s foreign minister has said three of its nationals were killed in an attack by the Iran-backed Huthi militia on a commercial vessel in the Red Sea.

This marks the first fatalities in the Red Sea since the Yemen-based militant group declared a blockade of the Bab al-Mandeb Strait on July 20.

Here’s a closer look at the Huthis and how they got to where they are:

Who are the Huthis?

Huthi fighters take part in a parade as part of a mobilization campaign, in Sanaa, Yemen, on December 18, 2024. Khaled Abdullah/Reuters

The Huthi movement, also known as Ansar Allah (Supporters of God), is one side of the Yemeni civil war. It emerged in the 1990s, when its leader, Hussein al-Huthi, launched “Believing Youth,” a religious revival movement for a centuries-old subsect of Shia Islam called Zaidism.

The Zaidis ruled Yemen for centuries but were marginalized under the Sunni regime that came to power after the 1962 civil war. Al-Huthi’s movement was founded to represent Zaidis and resist radical Sunnism, particularly Wahhabi ideas from Saudi Arabia. His closest followers became known as Huthis.

Yemen’s civil war began in 2014, when Huthi forces stormed the capital Sanaa and toppled the internationally recognized and Saudi-backed government. The conflict spiraled into a wider war in 2015 when a Saudi-led coalition intervened in an attempt to beat back the Huthis.

Nowadays, Sanaa is still under Huthi control, alongside much of the west of the country.

Who are they allied with?

The Huthis are backed by Iran, which began increasing its aid to the group in 2014 as the civil war escalated and as its rivalry with Saudi Arabia intensified. Iran has provided the group with weapons and technology for, among other things, sea mines, ballistic and cruise missiles, and unmanned aerial vehicles, according to a 2021 report from the Center for Strategic and International Studies.

The Huthis form part of Iran’s so-called “Axis of Resistance” – an anti-Israel and anti-Western alliance of regional militias backed by the Islamic Republic.

CNN’s Sophia Saifi and Rhea Mogul contributed to this reporting.

World.title: Meta just picked a side in a big debate over the future of AI
World.content:
Meta is taking a stance on one of the biggest debates shaping the future of artificial intelligence: Should AI models be open for anyone to tinker with and modify, or should they be tightly controlled by the companies making them?

For Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, the answer is clearly the former. The tech giant on Monday launched a new “open-weight model” — which has parameters that users can customize to adjust how the AI performs or responds — called Glimmer.

Meta says Glimmer is tailored for powering AI models that can run directly on personal computers instead of relying on computing power from data centers. Zuckerberg also published a lengthy manifesto laying out his vision and approach to AI, attempting to assuage wide-ranging concerns about AI as the company combats criticisms about its data center buildout and AI smart glasses.

“Rather than centralizing superintelligence, we should distribute it widely and give every person the ability to direct it,” he wrote.

The open vs. closed debate

Debates over whether AI should be open or closed have permeated both Silicon Valley and Washington. Closed models are generally thought to be more advanced and can be closely tested and monitored by the companies developing them. However, like open-weight models, closed models can still behave in unpredictable ways, as the recent reports of AI models going rogue and breaking into other companies have demonstrated.

Open models give developers the freedom to build their own products and services based on the technology. That creates an opportunity for companies offering open models to potentially become indispensable to businesses by offering technological blueprints for their products. Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is also a supporter of AI models with open weights, and the chip giant says companies like Uber and Zoom are using its open models to build features and analyze data.

Meta at one point had one of the more popular open-weight models, called Llama, but late last year started focusing on developing its own closed-source model called Spark to compete with the most advanced models from OpenAI and Anthropic.

Popular AI models from China, like those made by Moonshot and DeepSeek, are also open weight — raising questions over whether that approach is giving Chinese models an edge.

And there’s another downside: Some experts say open-weight models tend to lag behind the most advanced closed models in performance and capabilities. Yet Zuckerberg and Huang maintain that open-weight models can lead to faster innovation because they allow for broader access.

Zuckerberg’s vision for AI

Zuckerberg’s thesis paints an idyllic picture of the benefits of AI, writing that the technology will give every individual their own custom assistant, tools to build businesses and a tutor with “a PhD in every subject.” Society shouldn’t hand just a select few companies the keys to create, control and distribute these tools, he argued.

“There is no technological solution that can align with everyone’s opposing interests and values at once,” he wrote. “Any singular superintelligence would have to prioritize some values over others and in the process would be incapable of being benevolent to everyone.”

Yet there’s been growing backlash over the technology’s rapid advancement and its influence on everything from jobs to cybersecurity, mental health, the economy and local communities. College students booed mentions of AI during commencement ceremonies this spring. Roughly $130 billion worth of data center projects were blocked or delayed in the first quarter of 2026 alone because of local opposition, according to research firm Data Center Watch.

And Meta has been embroiled in controversy over concerns about its AI smart glasses being used to record others without their consent.

Zuckerberg argues that if everyone has access to “superintelligence,” the playing field will be equal. He also said Meta builds its own energy infrastructure to keep electricity prices low in the areas where it builds data centers.

He also called for more collaboration between frontier AI labs and the government, coming after representatives from Meta, OpenAI, Google and Anthropic met with the White House to discuss a new framework for government review of AI models before they launch.

“To develop the most advanced models and products,” he wrote, “we must recognize that AI is likely the most competitive industry in history.”

World.title: Cristiano Ronaldo and Georgina Rodriguez tie the knot after 10 years
World.content:
They married Tuesday in a civil ceremony described by the public relations team that represents the Portuguese soccer star as “a private and intimate moment attended by their five children.”

The ceremony took place in Cascais, a coastal town in western Portugal near the capital, Lisbon, the Brunswick Group said in the announcement.

The couple posted a picture on their Instagram accounts showing their rings.

They have been together for the past decade after meeting in Madrid.

The 41-year-old Ronaldo, a five-time world player of the year and one of the most high-profile sports stars, is coming off playing in his record-tying sixth World Cup for Portugal.

His Saudi team, Al Nassr, starts its domestic season on Saturday.

World.title: Shoulder-fired missile threat prompted Trump’s plane ruse, source says
World.content:
A specific threat to Air Force One by a shoulder-fired missile emerged on the final day of last month’s NATO summit in Turkey, according to a person familiar with the matter, prompting the scramble among US officials to devise a furtive plan to sneak President Donald Trump out of the country on an alternate jet.

The threat was specific enough that officials feared Trump’s life would be at enormous risk if he flew out of the country on either the legacy Air Force One plane or the Qatar-donated jet that he used to fly to the summit.

The person declined to say where information about the threat originated, but said it was believed to be serious in part because of how specifically the Iranians seemed to know details of Trump’s arrangements in Turkey.

Officials, including from the military and Secret Service, put together the plan to move Trump to another plane to fly out of the country within hours.

Trump, over the course of his final day at the conference, appeared preoccupied with Iranian threats on his life, raising the issue repeatedly with reporters.

CNN reported in the days following the summit that Israel had shared intelligence with the United States that Iran had recently devised a new plan to assassinate Trump.

But some officials at the time cast skepticism on the Israeli intelligence, suggesting the report was viewed — in part — as a piece of a broader Israeli effort to influence Trump’s decision making on Iran.

World.title: PM inspects development and service projects in Gharbiya Governorate
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly began an inspection tour of Gharbiya Governorate on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to inaugurate and inspect a number of development, service, and government projects, accompanied by several ministers and senior officials.

During the tour, Madbouly highlighted Gharbiya’s competitive advantage as one of Egypt’s traditional industrial hubs and a major agricultural governorate. He also reviewed progress on projects implemented under the presidential “Decent Life” initiative, which aims to improve basic services and enhance the quality of life in rural communities.

The tour included healthcare facilities, family medicine centers, drinking water and wastewater projects, as well as the inauguration of a regional branch of the Consumer Protection Agency.

Gharbiya Governor Alaa Abdel Moaty said 221 projects have been completed in Zefta district, covering 55 villages and 92 hamlets and serving around 560,000 people. The projects include government and agricultural service complexes, healthcare facilities, roads, bridges, and irrigation infrastructure.

PM: Egypt Prioritizes Drinking Water Services

During the tour, Madbouly inaugurated the Nahtay water station in Zefta, stressing that the state places particular importance on the drinking water sector as a vital service directly linked to citizens’ daily lives and health.

The station was upgraded and its efficiency enhanced under the presidential “Decent Life” initiative as part of ongoing efforts to improve drinking water services and the quality of life in Egyptian villages.

Madbouly said drinking water projects implemented under the initiative are contributing to a significant improvement in basic services across targeted villages. He added that these projects aim to provide safe, high-quality drinking water and ensure reliable services for citizens.

The upgrades to the Nahtay station are expected to increase water production, improve pumping rates, and enhance the stability of services provided to residents.

Madbouly stressed the importance of accelerating the completion of “Decent Life” projects, addressing any obstacles affecting implementation, and maximizing their impact on the quality of life in targeted communities.

PM Inspects Sandbast Family Medicine Center

Madbouly also inspected the Family Medicine Center in Sandbast village, Zefta district, describing healthcare projects under the “Decent Life” initiative as a key pillar of the state’s efforts to invest in human development.

He said such projects reflect the state’s commitment to providing comprehensive and advanced healthcare services in villages, ensuring that citizens have access to quality medical care close to their homes while contributing to improved quality of life and sustainable development.

Minister of Health and Population Khaled Abdel Ghaffar said the Sandbast Family Medicine Center represents a model for modern primary healthcare facilities designed to bring medical services closer to citizens and support comprehensive health coverage.

Built on an area of 2,050 square meters, the three-story center serves more than 47,000 citizens and includes specialist clinics, family medicine and family planning clinics, a dental clinic, a first-aid unit, a fully equipped pharmacy, a medical laboratory, maternal and child healthcare services, a radiology center, and a state-funded treatment clinic.

The center also provides services under Egypt’s presidential public health initiatives, including screening and treatment for chronic and kidney diseases, early detection and treatment of hearing impairment among newborns, women’s health services, maternal and fetal care, early detection of genetic diseases, healthcare for the elderly, and cancer screening and treatment.

Abdel Ghaffar said the center has spared residents the time, cost, and difficulty of traveling to Zefta General Hospital, around five kilometers away, to receive medical care.

During his inspection, Madbouly toured the center’s clinics and spoke with medical staff about working hours and services. Doctors said healthcare services are available around the clock, while the family planning clinic receives up to 900 visitors per month and provides all services free of charge.

Madbouly also spoke with residents about the quality of services provided at the center. They expressed satisfaction with the healthcare services and said the new facility had significantly reduced the need to travel for treatment, particularly for elderly people, women, and children.

Gharbia Governor Alaa Abdel Moaty said the governorate is witnessing a major transformation in healthcare infrastructure under the “Decent Life” initiative. He added that the Sandbast center represents an important addition to healthcare services in Zefta and supports preparations for the implementation of the Comprehensive Health Insurance System.

The prime minister was accompanied during the tour by the ministers of health and population, local development and environment, agriculture and land reclamation, and housing, as well as lawmakers and senior officials.

World.title: PM: LE450B allocated to “Hayah Karima” projects benefiting 20M citizens
World.content:
Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said the total funding allocated to completed projects under the presidential “Hayah Karima” (Decent Life) initiative nationwide has exceeded LE 450 billion.

Speaking at a press conference following the opening and inspection of a number of service and development projects in Gharbiya Governorate, Madbouly said the completed projects have been implemented in more than 1,450 villages, benefiting around 20 million citizens.

Madbouly said the progress achieved under the presidential “Hayah Karima” initiative represents the outcome of extensive efforts, describing the initiative as, “by all measures, Egypt’s project of the 21st century.”

He explained that Gharbiya Governorate is currently putting the final touches on the completion of all “Hayah Karima” projects, noting that the projects have either already been received or are at the stage of preliminary handover, paving the way for their full operation.

Madbouly said Gharbiya is among the governorates where implementation of the initiative has been fully completed, adding that the completion of Phase One in the remaining governorates will take place successively, with its completion expected to be announced over the coming weeks.

He underscored the substantial scale of funding spent on the completed “Hayah Karima” projects nationwide.

Madbouly said the projects being implemented in Egyptian villages go beyond developing individual villages, forming part of a comprehensive effort to improve services and infrastructure on a large scale.

He explained that comparing the conditions of villages before the implementation of the initiative’s projects with their current status clearly demonstrates the extent of development achieved.

As an example of the scale of development, he noted that the rate of wastewater coverage in villages across Gharbiya Governorate stood at 26 percent in 2014, while it has now risen to 77 percent following the completion of the initiative’s first phase, in addition to other projects to be added to the villages targeted under the second and third phases.

The Prime Minister pointed out that development efforts have not been limited to infrastructure projects, but have also been carried out in parallel to improve the level of services provided to citizens, particularly healthcare services through health units, medical centers and hospitals, alongside the provision of medicines and medical services.

He explained that the water treatment plants constructed under the initiative now cover projected needs through 2050.

The Prime Minister added that development efforts have also extended to bringing modern services to villages, including natural gas networks and fiber-optic telecommunications lines, stressing that the ongoing projects represent genuine development of Egyptian villages.

Madbouly explained that implementing this massive project faced numerous challenges, particularly the lack of comprehensive information at the outset regarding the services already available in villages, the complexity of implementing the projects, and challenges related to allocating land needed for their construction.

He pointed out that overcoming these challenges required tremendous efforts involving millions of Egyptians, including consulting firms, universities and construction companies, stressing that the scale of the work carried out reflects the magnitude of the project and the extensive efforts it has required over the past years.

Prime Minister Mostafa Madbouly said the government is contributing to improving the quality of life for more than 60 million citizens through the three phases of the major “Decent Life” (Haya Karima) initiative.

He said the government had gained considerable experience following the completion of the first phase of the initiative, adding that the new phase is currently focused as a top priority on sanitation projects and improving water quality, as well as healthcare projects, including hospitals and health and medical units, in addition to schools.

Madbouly said the initiative had also created significant employment opportunities, noting that the unemployment rate had fallen below 6 percent. “We are moving in the right direction despite all the unprecedented challenges we are facing,” he said.

The prime minister also highlighted the “Ras El Hekma” medical project in Matrouh, which has been fully developed, as well as expansion plans across the governorate. He pointed to the construction of an entirely new building for Alamein Hospital and the “Alam El Roum” Hospital, the governorate’s main hospital, which has hundreds of beds.

He added that major medical services are being implemented alongside housing and development projects, as well as the Alam El Roum project being developed through an Egyptian-Qatari partnership.

Madbouly stressed that tourism is a genuine source of income for Egypt, saying it is encouraging to see the large presence of foreign tourists on the North Coast. This, he noted, means an inflow of foreign currency into the country, as well as job opportunities for young people living in these areas throughout the year.

He noted that the North Coast has strong tourism potential, pointing to the acceleration in the development of tourism projects. Such projects, he said, will create job opportunities and generate billions of dollars in revenues for the state.

The prime minister also touched on the high-speed railway serving the development process, saying it would help citizens travel from Cairo to Matrouh, as well as along the “Ain Sokhna-Matrouh-Salloum” route, alongside electricity, energy and development projects.

He stressed that the government is safeguarding the state’s rights and that an integrated vision for the development of the North Coast will benefit the people of Matrouh by generating jobs and development opportunities.

Madbouly affirmed that development is at the heart of every part of Egypt, urging people to consider the scale of development achieved over the past 12 years, compared with the situation in Egypt before that period and the country’s current position, despite the unprecedented external challenges.

He added that the government is focusing on improving citizens’ quality of life and has comprehensive plans to address existing challenges. The government is nearing completion of a program aimed at launching an economic transformation over the next three years.

“Our goal is to anticipate all possible scenarios that could unfold globally and their impact on us, including the continuation of the conflicts currently taking place,” he said.

On the energy sector, Madbouly said the government reviews the file on a weekly basis with the officials responsible for it.

He added that, under the visions and strategies set by the political leadership for the sector since 2014, the state has undertaken a large number of projects whose benefits are now being realized and whose returns are being reaped during the current phase.

He affirmed that Egypt is capable of meeting the energy sector’s needs over the coming period.

World.title: Finance Minister: LE 6 bln targeted for cash payment of third tranche of exporters’ dues
World.content:
Finance Minister Ahmed Kouchouk said the government is targeting the allocation of six billion LE to pay in cash the third tranche of overdue dues owed to exporters for shipments made before July 1, 2024.

Kouchouk said applications from exporting companies seeking to benefit from the third tranche of the cash payment initiative will be accepted from Aug. 16 through Oct. 1, with payments scheduled to be disbursed on Oct. 22.

In a statement issued on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, the minister said more than LE 80 billion has been paid to exporters over the past six years, adding that the government aims to clear all outstanding dues within two years.

He noted that LE 48 billion has been allocated in the current budget to accelerate the provision of export support, while export subsidies reached LE 28 billion in fiscal year 2025/2026, marking annual growth of 55%.

Kouchouk said there is ongoing coordination and integration with the Ministry of Investment and Foreign Trade to develop the export system and boost the export sector.

He stressed that the government is working to provide exporters with liquidity to support the growth and competitiveness of Egypt’s goods and services exports, adding that it aims to significantly increase annual allocations for export support and promotion in order to open new markets for Egyptian products.

Meanwhile, Nevine Mansour, the minister’s adviser for economic institutions’ relations, said LE 12.6 billion in cash had been paid to around 2,500 exporting companies during the last fiscal year.

She noted that the amount represented the total value of the first and second tranches of overdue dues paid in cash during fiscal year 2025/2026, instead of being paid over two fiscal years.

World.title: Petroleum Minister: Proactive plans remain in place to secure natural gas market needs
World.content:
Minister of Petroleum and Mineral Resources Karim Badawi has affirmed that the petroleum sector continues to implement comprehensive, proactive plans to secure the local market’s natural gas needs.

He stressed the importance of managing shifts in consumption with high efficiency and flexibility, while maintaining maximum readiness to handle any emergencies or developments.

This came as the minister reviewed the operational status of the national natural gas grid directly from the Egyptian Natural Gas Company (GASCO) control center.

He inspected the steady flow of gas to various domestic sectors and evaluated strategic plans to meet energy demands through the remainder of the summer season.

During his visit, the minister verified uninterrupted gas supplies to power generation plants to ensure grid stability amid soaring temperatures.

He also monitored deliveries to the industrial sector to guarantee that factories operate at full capacity, alongside fulfilling domestic market requirements and export commitments.

Badawi noted that decisive state measures, backed by the political leadership and the government, have successfully met local demand throughout the first half of the summer.

Key actions included procuring regasification vessels and natural gas shipments, boosting domestic production, and implementing forward-looking supply strategies, he said.

Concluding his remarks, the minister underscored the necessity of continuous coordination between the petroleum and electricity sectors, alongside other relevant authorities.

This integrated approach aims to guarantee sustainable energy supplies for all state sectors moving forward, supported by real-time monitoring of the grid, consumption rates, and supply flows.

World.title: Govt. dismisses abduction allegations
World.content:
Government has dismissed allegations circulating on various media platforms suggesting that it has abducted individuals connected to some political parties.

Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security Permanent Secretary Dickson Matembo has clarified that several suspects, among them, three former senior government officials have been apprehended over an alleged plot to interfere with the 2026 general elections.

Speaking during a joint media briefing, Mr Matembo clarified that no abductions have taken place, stressing that all actions undertaken by the state are within the confines of the law.

Mr Matembo emphasised that contrary to speculation, individuals such as former Ambassador Martha Lungu and journalist Hannah Katontoka were not abducted, but lawfully apprehended to assist with investigations and have since been released.

And government has commended members of the public for their cooperation in providing information that aided law enforcement and urged citizens to remain vigilant, reporting any activities that may threaten national security, public safety, or peace.

“The government’s position is clear. The security of the Republic of Zambia is a responsibility of the state and must be protected through lawful, accountable and constitutionally established institutions,” he emphasised.

Mr Matembo also confirmed the arrest of businessman Valden Findlay in connection with investigations into alleged military-related training undertaken by Zambian nationals abroad.

The arrest follows the earlier interception of three Zambian nationals at Kenneth Kaunda International Airport on August 1st, 2026 who have since been arrested and charged with unlawful drilling, unauthorised use of uniform and prohibition of terrorism.

He explained that a joint intelligence-led operation involving defense and security agencies culminated in the apprehension of several suspects linked to attempts to interfere with the electoral process.

He added that the three former senior government officials are currently in lawful custody for allegedly providing technical services aimed at undermining the electoral system.

The Permanent Secretary revealed that Investigators have also extended invitations to Japhen Mwakalombe, Mwila Kakana and Sessho Banda to assist with ongoing inquiries after they were found in possession of over K7.3 million.

He explained that the source and intended purpose of the funds remains unclear, noting that the trio, however, have communicated through their lawyers that they will only be available after August 14th, 2026.

Mr Matembo further disclosed that sensitive military intelligence information was discovered on electronic devices seized from the suspects, raising concerns about unauthorised access to protected data.

In a related development, Mr Matembo also disclosed that a Kenyan national, Michael Juka, aged 56, has been apprehended for allegedly being contracted to carry out cybercrimes targeting the State.

And Ministry of Information and Media Permanent Secretary Thabo Kawana warned that anyone attempting to disrupt elections, peace, or national security will face the wrath of the law.

He noted that some political leaders had admitted to sending people abroad for training and later declared readiness to kill or be killed during elections, warning that such actions would not be tolerated.

Mr Kawana added that foreigners linked to treasonous activities were among those arrested, while others fled.

He reiterated that the government would not allow desperate individuals to endanger peace and security in pursuit of political power.

“We are aware of some individuals that also have finished their so-called training and would want to get back into the country to implement that which they want to come and do on the soil of this country. We want to say we welcome them. The law enforcement agencies are ready”, the Permanent Secretary warned.

World.title: ECZ deploys Poll staff in Chilubi
World.content:
The deployment of poll staff by the Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) in Chilubi District ahead of the August 13 General Election has reached an advanced stage.

The exercise, which began yesterday, is scheduled to be completed today.

Chilubi District Electoral Officer Kenneth Kafumbwe says poll staff that have been deployed to swamp areas are being airlifted using a Zambia Air Force (ZAF) chopper, while those assigned to the mainland are being transported by boats, before continuing their journey on vehicles and motorbikes.

Speaking in an interview with the media today in Chilubi today, Mr Kafumbwe expressed optimism that the deployment exercise will be completed before the close of business today.

Meanwhile, stakeholders observing the electoral process have welcomed the timely deployment of poll staff noting that the Electoral Commission of Zambia has taken into account Chilubi’s unique geographical challenges.

New Buyantanshi Village Headman, David Mwaba said the Commission’s proactive approach has ensured that staff reach their destinations on time.

Mr Mwaba further expressed happiness for the peaceful atmosphere that has characterised the electoral process in the area.

World.title: Zambians urged to be peaceful- Haamaundu
World.content:
Government has called on members of the public to uphold peace during elections, stating that continued peace in the country acts as an asset in promoting investor confidence and economic development.

Ministry of Defence Permanent Secretary, Maambo Haamaundu, says that his ministry is committed to ensuring continued peace that can be exported to other countries in leadership and peace keeping missions.

Mr Haamundu added that despite crowd management falling under the Ministry of Home Affairs and Internal Security, the Ministry of Defence has its services on standby, should they be called upon due to a situation that demands their attention.

“We must continue to maintain the peace of our country, because like I said, it is the foundation for economic and social development,” he said.

Mr Haamaundu has since appealed to members of the public to refrain from the temptation of wanting to cause violence, as they remain as key stakeholders of championing peace in the country.

He said that the government will work with a government approach that will involve key collaborations with stakeholders such as correctional services and immigration, in order to maximize peace.

Mr Haamaundu expressed that he is hopeful of a peaceful environment as the people go about casting their votes and that individuals who want to cause unnecessary trouble will be dealt with accordingly.

World.title: ECZ commissions 2026 National Election Results Centre in Lusaka
World.content:
The Electoral Commission of Zambia (ECZ) has officially opened the 2026 National Election Results Centre in Lusaka situated at the Mulungushi International Conference Centre.

Speaking during the commissioning of the Centre today, ECZ Chairperson, Mwangala Zaloumis, called for transparency, professionalism and respect for the democratic process during the results management period.

Ms Zaloumis said the media has a critical role to play in promoting transparency and providing accurate information to the public during the electoral process.

She implored journalists to report objectively, independently and in accordance with their accreditation, while ensuring that information is verified before publication or broadcast.

Ms Zaloumis said the media should rely on official results issued by the Commission and avoid amplifying speculation and unverified claims.

She said inaccurate figures and misleading information can spread rapidly, particularly through social media and other digital platforms.

Ms Zaloumis also urged the citizens to exercise caution over information circulating online, noting that photographs, documents, figures and other claims may be genuine, incomplete, taken out of context or entirely false.

The Chairperson encouraged the public to rely on official information from the ECZ and remain patient as the established results management processes are completed.

Ms Zaloumis, who was flanked by her Vice Vincent Mukanda, three Commissioners and Chief Electoral Officer, Brown Kasaro, further appealed to political parties, candidates and their supporters to avoid using unofficial or unverified information in ways that could create unnecessary tension, confusion and mistrust.

She said the launch of the National Election Results Centre is more than the opening of a physical facility, as it demonstrates the Commission’s commitment to making the presidential election results announcement process accessible to stakeholders and conducting it with the seriousness it deserves.

Ms Zaloumis said all stakeholders operating from the Centre should comply with established procedures and cooperate with officials responsible for its operations.

Meanwhile, ECZ Director of Information and Communication Technology (ICT), Victor Kachaka, said the Commission has put in place systems to facilitate the management and display of election results from the voting stage through to the announcement of results.

Dr Kachaka said internet connectivity will also be provided to facilitate access to the electoral results system.

He explained that the results display portal will enable users to access results and analyse trends at different levels, including provinces and constituencies.

Dr Kachaka said the portal will initially display presidential candidates in alphabetical order, but the figures will be updated as results are officially announced by the Commission.

He said the system will enable stakeholders to follow the results as they are progressively received and displayed by the Commission.

World.title: TIZ urges Zambians to adhere to the provisions of the law
World.content:
Transparency International Zambia (TIZ) Executive Director, Maurice Nyambe, has called on all stakeholders participating in this year’s General Elections to adhere to the provisions of the law.

Mr Nyambe says stakeholders should comply with the Electoral Process Act, electoral guidelines and the Electoral Code of Conduct to ensure a credible and peaceful election.

He also urged citizens to turn up in large numbers and exercise their constitutional right to vote in tomorrow’s General Elections.

Mr Nyambe noted that voting is an important civic duty through which citizens contribute and strengthen democracy and maintain the integrity of the electoral process.

The TIZ Chief said this in an interview with the media in Lusaka today ahead of tomorrow’s General Elections.

Mr Nyambe has further called on all stakeholders to allow the electoral and results management processes to take their full course.

He revealed that TIZ has deployed long-term monitors across the country since March this year to monitor the electoral process and report issues observed on the ground.

And Mr Nyambe has appealed to candidates who will lose the elections to genuinely accept the outcome.

Mr Nyambe said there can only be one winner in an election, and urged all candidates and their supporters to respect the outcome and use the legal channels provided should they wish to challenge the results.

He noted that even in the event of electoral disputes, all parties should allow the prescribed appeal processes to take their full course.

Mr Nyambe said TIZ wants to see Zambia maintain the peace it has enjoyed over the years by ensuring that all electoral disputes are handled within the confines of the law.
