Susana Vera (REUTERS) A man wears special eclipse glasses, as beachgoers gather before a total solar eclipse set to begin around sunset, at a beach near Valencia, Spain, Wednesday Aug. 12, 2026. Alberto Saiz (AP Photo/Alberto Saiz) The moon partially covers the sun during a solar eclipse as seen from Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. Borja Suarez (REUTERS) The atmosphere leading up to the eclipse at the soccer field on Teide Street in San Sebastián de los Reyes. Álvaro García On this Wednesday, the Port of Tarragona, bathed in sunshine, filled up with families and enthusiasts to secure the best spots to view the eclipse. Alex López (EFE) Cientos de personas esperan el inicio del eclipse solar en la playa de Riazor en Coruña, este miércoles. Lavandeira (EFE) A woman watches the sun from the soccer field on Teide Street in San Sebastián de los Reyes. Álvaro García The scene before the eclipse, near a cliff in Cedeira. ROCÍO CIBES People lie down inside a portable planetarium during an eclipse watch party on the day of a total solar eclipse in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. Susana Vera (REUTERS) Jose Luis Martinez, a member of the "Los Taraos" amateur astrophotography group, sets up his cell phone to shoot a total solar eclipse in Berlanga de Duero, central Spain, Wednesday, Aug. 12, 2026. Bernat Armangue (AP Photo/Bernat Armangue) A person wearing a mask and glasses waits for the solar eclipse in Madrid on Wednesday, August 12, 2026. SERGIO PEREZ (EFE) Un incendio cerca del parque de El Monte de San Pedro, en A Coruña. Está previsto que miles de personas se acerquen al parque para contemplar el eclipse total. Maria Alejandra Cardona (REUTERS) The sun, ahead of a total solar eclipse, as seen from the beach in Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. Borja Suarez (REUTERS) Several people heading to Gurugú Beach to watch the total solar eclipse. Andreu Esteban (EFE) Valerio D'Orazio, from Lisbon, Portugal, uses an app on his mobile phone to find out where the totality will appear during the total solar eclipse, at an eclipse watching party in Buitrago del Lozoya, Spain, August 12, 2026. Susana Vera (REUTERS) A view of the 40-meter telescope at the Yebes Astronomical Observatory in Guadalajara on Wednesday. Ismael Herrero (EFE) Maarten Savelkoel, 76, from the Netherlands, visits a campsite to see the total solar eclipse, in Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. Borja Suárez (REUTERS) Cesar Gadea from Miami, Florida, U.S., looks at the sun through self-made binoculars ahead of a total solar eclipse, at the Galactica Centre, near the Javalambre Astrophysical Observatory in Arcos de las Salinas, near Teruel, Spain, August 12, 2026. Christian Hartmann (REUTERS) Patricia Molera and Enrique Sotomayor test their eclipse glasses during sunset at Arija beach, Spain, August 11, 2026. Borja Suarez (REUTERS) A woman takes photos of the sunset and the Sil River Canyon on Tuesday from the Matacás Lookout in Castro Caldelas (Ourense), one day before the solar eclipse. Brais Lorenzo (EFE) Frenchman Leyssalle Anthony, 39, prepares a telescope to view the total solar eclipse from the beach, in Arija, Spain, August 12, 2026. Borja Suarez (REUTERS)

La meteorología también cumplió esta vez con su parte en buena parte de la franja de totalidad. Al menos 15 millones de personas ubicadas bajo esa sombra de unos 300 kilómetros de ancho, prácticamente libre de nubes para la ocasión, tuvieron la ocasión de mirar directamente el espectáculo natural de un eclipse total perfecto, algo que no puede verse desde ningún otro punto del sistema solar. Solo en la Tierra; y, este 12 de agosto, solo en parte de Islandia y de España, los únicos territorios habitados por los que cruzó la banda de totalidad de este eclipse. En declaraciones a los medios desde el Observatorio de Yebes (Guadalajara), punto oficial de seguimiento del eclipse, el presidente de la Comisión Interministerial para el Trío de Eclipses y secretario de Estado de Ciencia, Innovación y Universidades, Juan Cruz Cigudosa, aseguró que esta cita convertiría a España en “el Mundial de la Astronomía”. “Hoy es la final. España está jugando la final. Está liderando la final”, subrayó. Y desde luego España ganó esa final, para desgracia de los islandeses, que no pudieron ver nada: nubarrones y lluvias opacaron el paso del eclipse por el extremo occidental de la isla, donde Björk había organizado una “rave” solar.

La España vaciada, donde las condiciones eran idóneas para observar el fenómeno, esperaba con la mayor expectación este eclipse. Provincias casi siempre alejadas de la atención, como Soria, Palencia, Teruel o León, concentraron las miradas de todo el mundo y fueron anfitrionas de una celebración única en medio de un verano plagado de romerías. Los festivales masivos de música cedieron el protagonismo a fiestas populares en honor a la alineación perfecta del Sol y la Luna, planeadas con mimo en localidades como Castrillo de la Reina (Burgos), donde la charanga comenzó a recorrer sus estrechas calles a las seis de la tarde, anunciando la doble noche que se avecinaba. Este pueblo, que en invierno solo tiene 121 habitantes, fue el campamento base para más de mil personas llegadas de toda España, que guardaron con celo el secreto de esta ubicación privilegiada ante la posibilidad de una afluencia masiva. A Castrillo de la Reina llegó también una delegación de periodistas del periódico estadounidense The New York Times, que pondría en el centro de atención mundial a esta pequeña localidad de la Sierra de la Demanda. Periodistas internacionales y un festival con aficionados llegados de toda España para ajetrear un pequeño pueblo, perfecta ilustración de lo que supuso este fenómeno astronómico en buena parte de los pequeños municipios que se vieron regados con el premio de la lotería cósmica. “Va a ser como un atardecer sin atardecer”, comentan emocionadas unas adolescentes de Castrillo, ataviadas con las gafas eclipseras en la frente como si fueran gafas de sol fashion.

00:51 Reacciones al eclipse solar total en España 12.08.2026 El eclipse visto desde Riaño (Castilla y León). Foto: Néstor Rodan | Vídeo: EPV

La idea de verse desbordados con concentraciones multitudinarias, en medio de un verano que está surfeando una ola de calor tras otra, era la gran preocupación en esa España que enseñaba con orgullo observatorios astronómicos privilegiados como el de Javalambre (Teruel) o que sentía reconocida la bella oscuridad de sus cielos en provincias como Guadalajara, donde las noches de verano que muestran miles de estrellas invisibles en las ciudades, y revelan la Vía Láctea, han sido un auténtico semillero de vocaciones para docenas de astrónomos de primera fila internacional. Esa España que tiende un puente científico con Marruecos —en tiempos tan complicados con el vecino del sur— para ensayar en la ciudad de Palencia un experimento científico que se completará el 2 de agosto de 2027, cuando otro eclipse total cruce el extremo sur de la Península y el norte de África.

Si lo normal es que pasen casi 400 años para que un eclipse total vuelva a pasar por el mismo lugar, las regiones que han vivido este miércoles el día de las dos noches pueden considerarse especialmente afortunadas. Otro eclipse con un recorrido muy similar pasó por la mayoría de ellas en 1905, dejando huella en la memoria colectiva. En Castrillo de la Reina, los más viejos del lugar recuerdan cómo sus mayores les hablaron de aquella vez que la gran sombra de la Luna les cogió por sorpresa, hace 121 años y también a mediados del siglo XIX. Aunque el país entero llevase meses hablando del fenómeno astronómico, cuyo paso la ciencia había predicho al segundo, cuando de verdad llegó dejó una mezcla de júbilo y estupor que nos hizo empatizar con nuestros antepasados que vivían con miedo esa súbita oscuridad, que siempre llegaba por sorpresa.

La eclipsemanía pasó por España por primera vez desde que toda la población tiene acceso libre a la información sobre los detalles de la ocultación total del Sol —y a los medios de protección adecuados para observar el fenómeno sin riesgos para la vista—, resucitó preocupaciones que conectan con algunos de esos miedos ancestrales. Colegios de oftalmólogos y departamentos ministeriales recomendaron a la población que observase el eclipse total con las gafas de protección puestas todo el tiempo, ante el temor a graves lesiones oculares por su uso incorrecto. Mientras tanto, pequeños pueblos como Frómista (Palencia) prefirieron organizar observaciones públicas con maestros de ceremonias como el astrofotógrafo Ángel de Francisco, que dio precisas indicaciones a sus vecinos sobre cuándo tenían que quitarse las gafas para poder, sin riesgos, lo que siempre está ahí pero nunca habíamos podido ver: la corona solar.

Un reto para el país

Justo cuando la Luna comenzaba a morder la luz del Sol, el ministro del Interior, Fernando Grande-Marlaska, informaba en Yebes de que el comienzo del operativo —que había anunciado el despliegue de casi 35.000 efectivos, entre policías y guardias civiles— se había desarrollado sin demasiados incidentes. A primera hora de la tarde, algunos atascos a la salida de Madrid y Barcelona, que no se habían llevado el premio gordo del eclipse total, mostraban las ganas de la ciudadanía de llegar a un evento único. También en la costa asturiana, castigada por las nubes.

El Gobierno instaló su cuartel general en el Observatorio Astronómico de Yebes, levantado en 1975 en este pueblo de Guadalajara de más de 5.600 habitantes por sus casi 1.000 metros de altitud, pero a pesar de los rumores, desmentidos desde La Moncloa, no apareció por allí Pedro Sánchez, que solo disfrutó de un eclipse parcial en la residencia de La Mareta, en la isla canaria de Lanzarote. Aunque la totalidad del 100% oculto solo ensombreció al 40% del territorio español, todo el país, hasta el archipiélago canario, disfrutó de su trocito de eclipse.

01:43 Seis lugares distintos que han visto el eclipse Varias personas observan el eclipse en Arcos de Salinas (Teruel), este miércoles. Foto: Christian Hartmann (REUTERS) | Vídeo: EPV

El Gobierno preveía entre 400.000 y 1,5 millones de desplazamientos adicionales para acudir a zonas donde el fenómeno se observara en su totalidad, por lo que se había desplegado un dispositivo especial de vigilancia de la Dirección General de Tráfico. También se temía una caída de las comunicaciones por saturación y, sobre todo, había temor por el riesgo de incendios, como señaló la ministra para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico, Sara Aagesen: “Prohibido encender fuego, no aparcar sobre vegetación seca, mantener los accesos libres para emergencias y consultar diariamente el nivel de peligro de incendios. El día del eclipse solar total es un día para disfrutar, pero también una llamada a la prudencia y a la precaución”.

El cálculo de los beneficios para las provincias agraciadas por la lotería astronómica estimaba medio millón de turistas extra gracias al astroturismo y entre 350 y 400 millones de euros de valor añadido. Pero la ciencia tomó la palabra para reivindicarse en tiempos oscuros, y no por la sombra del eclipse. El astronauta, exministro de Ciencia y presidente de Hispasat, Pedro Duque, expresó su deseo de que el eclipse “atraiga a la gente hacia el conocimiento” y de que “quede en la conciencia” de los españoles. En declaraciones a los medios en el Observatorio del Ebro, en Roquetes (Tarragona), insistió en luchar contra la desinformación con el poder de la ciencia: “Hay gente que hace más caso a un audio de WhatsApp que te viene de la vecina del quinto que a las cosas que realmente funcionan, como la ciencia”.

En ese mismo sentido, su sucesora, Diana Morant, defendió en RNE que “es imposible una conversación entre ciencia y un charlatán”. “La humanidad siempre ha mirado al cielo para explicar las cosas y cuando no existía la ciencia se pensaba que eran los dioses los que castigaban”, dijo la ministra. “Se buscaban explicaciones y ahora las explicaciones las tenemos en la ciencia y no hay una ciencia que explique el cambio climático y una ciencia que diga que no hay cambio climático”, insistió. Más allá de la confrontación política, una cita científica, un eclipse total histórico, llenó de asombro a media España, hipnotizada por la belleza de la imagen que grabó en sus retinas.

World.title: Oído durante el eclipse en una playa asturiana: “El del siglo que viene lo vemos en otro sitio”
World.content:
Varios grupos de gente esperan a ver el eclipse solar en Lastres.

Crónica de una jornada marcada por la incertidumbre de si las nubes dejarían ver o no el eclipse desde la costa

A las once de la mañana, la playa de Vega, en el oriente asturiano, está mucho más poblada de lo habitual.

Hay bruma. Lastres, a 21 kilómetros y normalmente visible desde aquí, amanece hoy escondida. Hace calor. En la arena aún resisten los muros construidos el día anterior para frenar la subida de la marea.

—¿Se verá? —pregunta una señora.

—El tiempo en Asturias es una lotería —le responden.

Un grupo de amigos se instala en la arena.

—La semana que me ha dado este con el eclipse. Que si dónde lo vamos a ver, que si las gafas eran buenas, que si había que venir pronto... —dice una chica refiriéndose a su pareja.

—Nosotros vinimos escuchando Total Eclipse of the Heart en el coche... —responde una amiga, subiendo la apuesta.

Un chico lee Morir en la orilla, de Leonardo Padura, sentado en una silla plegable.

—¡Mi círculo en el que nadie puede entrar! Salvo que tengas el código —anuncia una niña desde el centro de un enorme flotador.

El código, por si interesa, es “mamá y papá”. No ha especificado si va junto o separado, ni si distingue mayúsculas y minúsculas.

Desde el prado que linda con la playa llega el mugido de una vaca.

A las 13.05, la playa se ha llenado de sombrillas. En el horizonte vuelve a aparecer la silueta de Lastres.

—Aquí no se va a ver nada —dice un chico.

—Y con esa negatividad, menos —replica su novia.

Empiezan a abrirse los táperes y a aparecer los bocadillos. Mucha tortilla, mucho pollo y mucho lomo empanado.

—Como no abra pronto, verás qué desbandada a última hora —comenta un señor.

A las tres de la tarde, Lastres vuelve a desaparecer tras la bruma.

Las nubes han adquirido un tono más gris.

—Todavía va a llover... —aventura una mujer.

Por la playa pasa una señora hablando por teléfono.

—No, no, murieron ahogados.

No parece especialmente preocupada por el eclipse.

Tres chicas conversan con los pies en el agua.

—Es un día histórico, ¿no? —dice una.

—Lo histórico es que vayamos a pasar un día entero en la playa —responde otra.

—¿Creéis que el eclipse saldrá en los libros de Ciencias? —plantea la tercera.

La mujer del teléfono sigue a lo suyo:

—¡Que yo no le dije eso, hombre!

Un chico pone un audio para sus amigos. Se escuchan instrucciones para observar el eclipse. La voz insiste en que las gafas solo deben quitarse durante unos segundos y remata tres veces:

—No más. No más. ¡No más!

Empieza una encuesta improvisada a pie de playa, formulada por niños.

—¿Por qué se llama eclipse?

—¿Por qué nos dicen que no miremos al Sol si normalmente nadie nos dice nada?

—¿Es todos los años?

—¿Y si la Luna se queda ahí para siempre?

—¿Se puede ver desnudo?

La señora del teléfono continúa:

—Y un día dije yo: Se acabó, hay que hacer la fiesta. Y que venga mi hermana si quiere a decirme que no...

Una socorrista explica a un grupo de niños los peligros de la carabela portuguesa junto a un ejemplar varado en la arena.

La mujer termina la llamada, recoge sus cosas y se marcha.

—Mis hijos están cagados. Dicen que no van a mirarlo por si se quedan ciegos —cuenta un hombre.

—Pues casi mejor. El otro día leí lo de una chica que se quedó ciega por mirar un eclipse cuando tenía siete años y no se enteró hasta mucho después —responde una mujer.

En la orilla se forma una pequeña tertulia.

—Pues a mí todo esto del eclipse me da un poco igual —afirma una madre que lleva en brazos a su hija de once meses.

—Aunque haya nubes, ¿también se hace de noche? —pregunta una joven.

—Yo creo que sí —opina un señor.

—Dicen que baja la temperatura doce grados —añade otro.

—Tenía que haber traído el forro polar —responde una mujer, alarmada.

Una chica lee Hamnet en formato digital.

—¿Te acordaste de las gafas? —pregunta una mujer.

—¡Que síiiii! —contesta su pareja, dando la impresión de responder a una pregunta repetida muchas veces.

A primera hora de la tarde comienza a extenderse la desilusión. Los móviles propagan la noticia: las aplicaciones meteorológicas y las previsiones anuncian que las nubes persistirán en la costa.

—¿Cómo lo ves? —pregunta un chico.

—Chungo.

—¿Qué hora nos ponemos de límite para movernos?

—Yo ya me quedaba aquí...

—Pues yo prefiero irme a casa a verlo.

Le enseña el móvil. La aplicación asegura que allí sí despejará.

Un hombre lee El legado de los espías, de John le Carré, bajo una sombrilla.

—A partir de las siete no se puede mirar al Sol —advierte un joven.

—Pues primero tendremos que saber dónde está, porque no se ve —le contestan.

En una playa donde suele haber muchas tablas, apenas quedan surfistas en el agua.

—¿Está el mar raro? ¿Más calmado? —pregunta una chica.

—Y el ambiente. Hay algo extraño... —responde una amiga.

Las vacas del prado vecino han desaparecido.

—En cuanto empiece el eclipse, se acabó el fútbol —anuncia un padre a sus hijos.

El balón se escapa hacia la orilla. Una pareja pasea junto al agua. Él se adelanta para devolverlo de una patada.

—Te morías por darle, ¿eh? —le dice ella con cariño.

Pasa un corredor.

A las siete empieza a cundir el desánimo.

—La playa, muy bonita. Pero el eclipse no lo vemos.

Una niña contiene mal la decepción.

—Bueno, no verlo en un sitio donde se iba a ver también es especial —la consuela su madre.

Empiezan a aparecer figuras humanas en los montes que rodean la playa. También en las terrazas.

—¿Pero hay que ponerse las gafas o no? —pregunta un camarero.

A las 19.23 empieza a chispear.

—¿Dónde están los niños? Que se pongan las gafas aunque no haya Sol —ordena una madre.

—¿Te imaginas? La generación ciega —bromea otra.

—¿Cuánto queda? Estoy ya un poco hasta el gorro del eclipse —remata una tercera.

Por los altavoces de un restaurante suena, casualmente, Antes que ver el Sol, de Coti. Después llega Cien gaviotas, de Duncan Dhu.

—¡Está saliendo el Sol, está saliendo el Sol! —gritan unos niños.

Es una falsa alarma.

Una niña pasa con la linterna del móvil encendida para que la gente compruebe cómo se vería la luz a través de las gafas.

El pinchadiscos se anima. Ahora suena 19 días y 500 noches, de Joaquín Sabina.

—Yo no voy a ver nada, pero a lo mejor mi mujer sí, que es más alta que yo... —dice un hombre, provocando una carcajada colectiva.

Muchos conectan sus teléfonos y siguen el eclipse a través de retransmisiones en directo.

A las 20.26 se hace de noche.

Suena el Himno de Asturias interpretado con gaita.

A las 20.29 vuelve la luz.

—En el del próximo siglo igual tenemos más suerte —comenta una señora.

—Sí, pero ese lo vemos en otro sitio —responde su marido.

—Eso seguro —cierra ella.

Al fondo, la silueta de Lastres continúa difuminada tras la bruma.

World.title: Cataluña se rinde al eclipse total: “Ya se ve, mamá”
World.content:
Centenares de personas se han concentrado la tarde de este miércoles en el castillo de Montjuïc de Barcelona, pero en vez de mirar hacia la ciudad, todas sus miradas se han dirigido hacia el cielo en sentido oeste para observar cómo la luna se iba sobreponiendo poco a poco, hasta cubrirlo casi totalmente, sobre el Sol. Poco antes de las ocho de la noche, Nina, una niña de siete años que se protegía con unas gafas especiales, decía en voz alta, emocionada: “Ya se ve, mamá”. Tanto en Montjuïc como en otros puntos de la ciudad, como los búnkers del Carmel, se acumulaba la gente para ver el fenómeno astronómico.

A las 20.22 en Barcelona, aunque el sol aún estaba alto y sin ninguna nube que lo tapara, el día ha empezado a parecerse a la noche y a las 20.27 Rosa y Teresa han empezado a decir “¡ahora, ahora!” rendidas a un eclipse que se había hecho realidad, aunque no en su totalidad. Otros puntos de Cataluña, en Lleida y Tarragona sobre todo, dentro de esa franja en la que estaba previsto que se pudiera ver el eclipse total que no se podrá volver a observar en tierras catalanas hasta dentro de más de 100 años, se han convertido en lugares de peregrinaje para miles de personas en búsqueda de la mejor atalaya. Como el puerto de Tarragona, donde el eclipse total ha hecho acto de presencia a las 20.29 ante la atención de miles personas.

“Ha sido más impresionante de lo que pensaba. Hemos hecho dos horas de viaje hasta aquí, pero ha valido la pena”, explicaba Bruna, de ocho años y de Mataró, que con su familia se ha desplazado hasta Móra la Nova (Tarragona) para observar el eclipse. La única espinita es no haber podido disfrutarlo con su padre, que llegaba por la tarde en avión desde Mallorca, pero se ha quedado atrapado en el aeropuerto por los problemas de este miércoles en El Prat. “Hemos hecho una videollamada y le hemos retransmitido el eclipse, algo es algo”, añade la madre, Carol, quien también se muestra emocionada. “Ha sido muy emocionante, se me ha puesto la carne de gallina. Piensas que no será tan espectacular, pero ha superado todas las expectativas”, añade. “Y el cambio de temperatura”, interviene su hijo Leo, de 14 años, quien se muestra seguro de haber vivido una experiencia inolvidable. “Lo recordaré siempre y se lo contaré a mis hijos”. La familia, incluso, se plantea volver a repetir la experiencia el año próximo con el eclipse total que se podrá ver en el sur de Andalucía.

Móra la Nova ha sido el lugar elegido por centenares de personas para seguir el fenómeno astronómico. Se trata de uno de los 23 puntos oficiales habilitados por la Generalitat para seguir este evento, en un día marcado por las altas temperaturas -se ha llegado a los 37 grados- y con una alerta activada por el Servicio Meteorológico de Cataluña. Por ello, los primeros asistentes, que han llegado al mediodía, buscaban el refugio del conjunto de olivos que ofrecían un descanso ante el desangelado solar que esperaba vacío a la gran multitud.

Entre los asistentes había veteranos de estos fenómenos, como Lluís Jardí, de Sant Cugat del Vallès. Para él es el tercer eclipse solar total. El primero lo presenció en 1999 en Hungría y el segundo, en Estados Unidos en 2017. Informático de profesión, confiesa ser gran aficionado a la astronomía. Y esta afición la ha contagiado a su hijo, Bernat, de 23 años, que también vivió el eclipse de 2017. “Era muy pequeño y no me acuerdo de la experiencia, pero no de la corona; recuerdo que había mucho ambiente, como aquí”, explica. Con ellos ha viajado Joan, amigo de Bernat, también aficionado. “Yo no viajaría a Estados Unidos, pero quería verlo y pensé que no había otra forma mejor que hacerlo con Lluís, que es un gran experto”.

Maria Rosa (77 años), por ejemplo, se fue hasta Móra la Nova (Tarragona) con cinco amigos. Contempló su primer eclipse solar cuando tenía 14 años en Turín (Italia) y pensaba que no volvería a conseguirlo. “Fue una experiencia muy bonita y original. Pensaba que no vería otro, pero aquí estoy”, asegura esta mujer que tiene una casa de veraneo en Montroig, así que el eclipse le ha cogido cerca. A sus amigos, no, que han venido expresamente desde Turín para verlo. “Es algo bello, mágico”, apunta Marco. El grupo ha llegado hacia las 15 horas y han extendido un gran pañuelo gris en el suelo bajo el cobijo de unos olivos: su plan para pasar las largas horas de espera a 37 grados: “Comida y bebida, ¡somos italianos!”, aseguraban entre risas.

Eclipse Solar desde el castillo de Montjuic de Barcelona, este miércoles Massimiliano Minocri

Pero también los había novatos, pero no por ello no menos preparados, como la familia de Felip Sarroca y sus amigos. Mesas y sillas de camping, pañuelos y mantas para el suelo y montañas de juguetes para los niños. Las dos familias han venido desde El Prat de Llobregat (a 160 km) esta misma mañana y su idea es volver a casa esta misma noche después de ver las Perseidas. Felip se ha preparado para la ocasión y eligió este emplazamiento usando la IA. “Pregunté a ChatGPT y consulté en otras webs por un sitio no muy lejano, adecuado y no muy masificado y me recomendó este”, explicaba sentado a la mesa, apurando un almuerzo tardío a las 16 horas, lo que explica la previsión. Incluso ha diseñado una aplicación con preguntas sobre el eclipse. “Nos ha puesto a prueba a todos”, bromea su hijo Roger de 12 años.

El punto de observación de Móra la Nova (Tarragona) se ha habilitado en un solar situado justo detrás del centro de atención primaria, una ubicación que puede resultar de utilidad en esta jornada calurosa donde los centenares de visitantes que se esperan deberán esperar varias horas a temperaturas máximas de 37 grados. Sílvia Nicolás, auxiliar administrativa del ambulatorio, explica que para esta jornada no se han habilitados refuerzos, pero sí para mañana por la mañana. “Si hay lesiones oculares se espera que las consultas empiecen mañana a partir del mediodía. Hoy podríamos tener golpes de calor o algún traumatismo”. Pero el centro sanitario también está ejerciendo de refugio climático para aquellas personas que lo necesiten.

El centro de jubilados de Móra la Nova se halla junto al punto de observación del eclipse. Además de refugio climático para los visitantes -que pueden usar sus lavabos, ya que no se han instalado provisionales en el exterior-, sirve de sala de espera para las parroquianas del centro, que este miércoles por la tarde se han dado cita para jugar al bingo. “Estamos aquí al fresquito jugando, esperando a que empiece el eclipse”, asegura María Jesús. El grupo de seis mujeres asegura que quedan tres días a la semana a jugar, como no, con dinero, aunque sea solo con monedas de céntimo.

Problemas en trenes y carreteras

El eclipse ha provocado una punta de movilidad en las horas previas, con miles de personas buscando un lugar donde ver el fenómeno astronómico. Y los coches han saturado las principales carreteras con dirección hacia Tarragona y Lleida, ambas zonas en el corredor donde se ha podido contemplar la sombra completa de la Luna sobre el Sol. La AP-7 y la C-32 han sufrido colas kilómetricas en algunos puntos por la acumulación de vehículos, siempre en sentido sur, y la A-2, en Jorba, en dirección a Lleida, también ha sido el escenario de retenciones. Asimismo, en las horas previas, múltiples usuarios de Renfe denunciaron el colapso de los andenes de la estación de Sants por gente que quería desplazarse hacia Tarragona con un servicio de trenes que acumulaba retrasos a causa de una avería en la estación de Castelldefels. Protecció Civil ha tenido que activar una alerta de Ferrocat por aglomeración de personas en las estaciones de Sants y de Sant Vicenç de Calders. La Generalitat preveía el desplazamiento de 50.000 personas.

En Barcelona, una riada de gente ha ocupado las calles que llevaban hasta Montjuïc, una de las mayores recomendaciones para verlo en la ciudad. Los búnkers del Carmelo, otra atalaya privilegiada de la ciudad, contaba con más personas de las que son habituales para disfrutar del horizonte de la ciudad. Antes de que empezara el fenómeno, cada centímetro alrededor del castillo de Montjuïc fue ocupado por los visitantes, que buscaban cualquier espacio que tuviera visibilidad del sol. Carolina ha acudido con un grupo de amigos y su hija, África. “La verdad es que no tengo mucha expectativa, pero vinimos a pasar un buen rato juntas y a disfrutar”, ha explicado. Su hija ve el fenómeno con más ilusión. “Nunca he visto un eclipse, así que estoy emocionada”, ha comentado. Las dos llegaron preparadas para la espera con sillas de playa, las gafas de protección recomendadas y abanicos para combatir el calor, con temperaturas que superaban los 30 grados centígrados.

En los alrededores del castillo de Montjuïc se ha concentrado medio millar de personas, mientras que en la terraza interior había unas 350, entre invitados de instituciones barcelonesas y personas que habían comprado una entrada. Entre ellas estaban Teresa Plana y Rosa Masques, de 79 y 67 años, que han acudido para celebrar lo que consideraban un momento único. “Ha sido muy complicado subir, había muchísima gente viniendo”, comentaban las dos sobre el gran flujo de personas que accedían a los alrededores del castillo. Era la primera vez que ambas asistían a un eclipse, ante el que estaban muy expectantes: “Es importante participar de la historia”, ha dicho Plana.

En el Observatorio del Ebro, ubicado en Roquetes (Tarragona), ha seguido la evolución del eclipse una comitiva del Govern presidida por el jefe de gobierno Salvador Illa, junto a sus consellers Albert Dalmau (Presidencia), Núria Montserrat (Universidades), Esther Niubó (Educación) y Núria Parlon (Interior). Todos han podido disfrutar el momento pese a las dudas que existían unos días antes por la presencia de nubes que pudieran impedir la observación. La retransmisión en directo a través de Youtube desde el observatorio ha permitido ver cómo la luna iba mordisqueando el plato anaranjado del sol, una retransmisión que apenas han seguido directamente a través de la red social unas 80 personas.

World.title: 16 pueblos españoles que piden manga larga cuando cae la tarde
World.content:
Vielha (Lleida). La gran baza de los pueblos seleccionados radica, sobre todo, en la posibilidad de tener que taparse para descansar, algo que se ha convertido en todo un lujo durante la canícula. Es un requisito que cumple Vielha, a la vera de los ríos Garona y Nere, con su casco histórico construido a la manera aranesa, a golpe de piedra, pizarra y madera. Sus mínimas descenderán hasta los 12ºC la noche del domingo; las máximas alcanzarán picos de 33ºC en las horas centrales del jueves y viernes, pero bajarán a los 24ºC (y con probabilidad de lluvias) el lunes, según la Aemet. La capital del Valle de Arán se presenta como un buen campamento base para conocer este territorio del Pirineo catalán, con sus 33 núcleos de población, sus algo más de 10.000 habitantes y sus iglesias románicas. Es recomendable acercarse a la cascada Saut deth Pish, probablemente la más bonita de la zona. Más información: visitvaldaran.com/descubre-la-val-daran/pueblos/vielha/.

World.title: Xavi Hernández, nuevo seleccionador de Países Bajos
World.content:
El excentrocampista español Xavi Hernández, de 46 años, será el nuevo entrenador de la selección de fútbol de Países Bajos. Ha llegado a un acuerdo con la Federación Neerlandesa de Fútbol (KNVB) que este miércoles ha anunciado la firma de un contrato hasta 2030. Xavi, que sustituye a Ronald Koeman, será presentado en público el 25 de agosto. De momento, ha declarado a través de la KNVB que el nombramiento supone para él “un gran honor”. La Federación lo ha calificado a su vez como un futbolista “que lo ha vivido y ganado todo”.

Koeman anunció su marcha después de un Campeonato Mundial decepcionante en 2026 -celebrado en Canadá, México y Estados Unidos- en el que la selección neerlandesa fue eliminada en octavos de final ante Marruecos. La búsqueda de un reemplazo adecuado llevó a la KNVB a sondear, entre otros, al futbolista neerlandés Arne Slot. Este entrenó al Liverpool entre 2024 y 2026, y prefiere seguir en el circuito de los clubes.

Xavi Hernández ha sido capitán de la selección española de fútbol y 133 veces internacional con esta. Su etapa como entrenador dio comienzo en el equipo Al-Sadd, de Catar -2019 y 2021- aunque antes fue uno de sus jugadores durante cuatro temporadas. Después de la aventura catarí, pasó a ser entrenador del F.C. Barcelona, donde firmó en 2021 y fue destituido en 2024.

En las mismas declaraciones hechas públicas por la KNVB, el futbolista español dice que se formó en la cantera del F.C. Barcelona, “con fuertes influencias de, entre otros, Johan Cruyff y Rinus Michels”. “Siento un vínculo especial con el fútbol neerlandés. Se podría decir que soy, en cierto modo, un hijo del fútbol neerlandés”, añadió. Por su parte, Nigel de Jong, director del fútbol de élite de la KNVB, ha señalado: “Cada nuevo ciclo exige que volvamos a analizar hacia dónde queremos ir, qué necesitamos para ello y qué seleccionador disponible encaja mejor en esos objetivos”. Marianne van Leeuwen, directora del fútbol profesional neerlandés, ha añadido este miércoles que con Xavi incorporan “a alguien que, como jugador y entrenador, conoce la élite absoluta del fútbol internacional”.

Como jugador, Xavi Hérnandez estuvo 17 temporadas en el Barcelona. En total, disputó más de 750 partidos oficiales y ganó con el club ocho ligas, cuatro Champions de la UEFA y dos Mundiales de Clubes de la FIFA. Con la selección española se proclamó campeón de Europa en 2008 y 2012, y campeón del mundo en 2010. En las próximas semanas, se perfilará la composición del cuadro técnico de la selección neerlandesa.

World.title: Ukrainian soldier murdered by Soviets exhumed in Rotterdam
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The remains of a Ukrainian soldier who was murdered in Rotterdam by the Soviet secret services in 1938 are being repatriated for a military burial.

Colonel Yevhen Konovalets, the founder of a Ukrainian nationalist group, was killed by a bomb concealed in a box of chocolates as he walked home from a meeting with an undercover agent.

The Soviet spy had infiltrated the Organisation of Ukrainian Nationalists (OUN) and handed Konovalets the chocolates as a gift during a meeting at a hotel in Rotterdam on May 23, 1938.

Ukrainian president Volodymyr Zelensky announced on his official website that the colonel’s remains had been exhumed at Crooswijk Cemetery in Rotterdam so that they could be sent back to Ukraine.

He will be temporarily reinterred at the National Military Memorial Cemetery, in preparation for a farewell ceremony will be held at the Ukrainan Greek Catholic cathedral in Kyiv.

The OUN was founded in 1929 in Vienna as a right-wing nationalist organisation that aimed to establish an independent, ethnically homogenous Ukrainian state.

It was influenced in its early days by Italian fascism and German Nazism, but as Germany’s defeat in the Second World War drew nearer, the OUN adopted a more democratic ideology.

World.title: ABN Amro profit climbs to €781m as fees, lending grow
World.content:
ABN Amro has booked net profit of €781 million in the second quarter, up 29% on the same period last year and ahead of analyst forecasts, the bank said on Wednesday.

Analysts had expected earnings of around €686 million. The result beat even the highest forecast in that consensus, and shares in the group rose more than 5% to a record high.

The bank, which is now around one-fifth owned by the Dutch state after reducing its stake following the 2008 financial crisis, is in the process of a reorganisation that will cut 5,200 jobs by 2028.

The state is close to recouping the full €21.7 billion cost of the 2008 nationalisation of the bank, following a share price rally that took the bank’s stock above €40 this week.

World.title: Limburg wildfire wiped out rare juniper shrubland
World.content:
Fewer than 100 of the roughly 4,000 juniper bushes that grew in the Boschhuizerbergen nature reserve near Venray have survived this month’s wildfire in northern Limburg, the foundation that manages the site says.

The reserve held the largest juniper shrubland in the southern Netherlands, according to Het Limburgs Landschap, with some bushes more than 130 years old. Junipers grow slowly and thrive in the reserve’s nutrient-poor, drifting-sand soil – conditions that have become rare in the region.

The fire, which broke out on August 3, destroyed around 100 hectares, including 20 to 30 hectares of protected Natura 2000 land where the junipers stood. More than a week on, crews were still pouring water on smouldering hotspots to stop them reigniting.

The shrubland might not be able to be re-established, as the soil has changed over the decades and young plants may struggle to take root. “It is questionable whether we will ever get such a beautiful shrubland here again. I am afraid I will not live to see it,” the foundation’s Loek Hendrikx told broadcaster NOS.

Het Limburgs Landschap, set up in 1931 to stop the reserve being cleared for farmland, has appealed for donations towards a recovery it says will take years.

World.title: Human rights groups sue US government over Hague court sanctions
World.content:

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

Four US human rights organisations have sued the Trump administration over its sanctions against the International Criminal Court in The Hague, arguing the measures are unconstitutional and should be struck down.

The American Friends Service Committee, the Center for Constitutional Rights, Human Rights Watch and the Open Society Institute filed the complaint in New York on Tuesday.

It challenges the executive order signed by US president Donald Trump in February 2025, which authorised sanctions on court officials and on anyone assisting its investigations.

Washington has since used it against the court’s former chief prosecutor and two of his deputies, eight of its judges, a UN human rights expert and three Palestinian rights organisations.

The four organisations say the measures have forced them to drop work such as representing war crimes victims and making legal submissions to the court, in breach of their rights to free speech, association and religion under the US constitution.

They also argue the order exceeds the president’s powers and rests on a declared national emergency that has no basis in fact, describing it as a “blatantly illegal attack on international justice”.

Liz Evenson, international justice director at Human Rights Watch, said governments should step up to protect the court and those seeking justice before it.

The case follows Washington’s announcement in July of a campaign to dismantle the court, which the Netherlands hosts and has a duty as host state to protect.

Federal courts in New York and Maine ruled in 2025 that the order breached free speech protections, blocking enforcement against the claimants in those cases.

World.title: Roberto Martinez front-runner to be next Netherlands head coach
World.content:
The Dutch football association KNVB is reportedly lining up Roberto Martinez to take over from Ronald Koeman as coach of the national men’s team,.

The 53-year-old Spaniard emerged as a surprise contender after candidates such as former Feyenoord and Liverpool manager Arne Slot, former Ajax and Manchester United coach Erik ten Hag and PSV boss Peter Bosz ruled themselves out.

The KNVB held talks at the weekend with under-21 coach Michael Reiziger, but there have been no further discussions since Sunday, the Telegraaf reported on Wednesday.

Louis van Gaal also sent an open application to Zeist last week saying he was ready to step in for a fourth spell in charge, but the KNVB has not followed up with the 75-year-old former Ajax trainer.

Martinez was in charge of Portugal during the recent World Cup in North America, resigning after the team lost 1-0 to eventual winners Spain in the round of 16.

Previously he coached Belgium for six years, reaching the World Cup semi-final in 2018. He would be the first foreign manager to coach Oranje since Ernst Happel in 1978.

World.title: Uncertain future for Dutch bike brands after Accell goes under
World.content:
Add as a favourite source on Google Add DutchNews as a favourite source on Google

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

See more DutchNews articles in your Google search results

The Netherlands’ largest bicycle manufacturer, Accell, has been declared insolvent, leaving an uncertain future for major brands such as Batavus, Sparta and the British-based bike maker Raleigh.

A court appointed curators last week when Accell applied to suspend payments to its creditors, the last step before insolvency in the Netherlands.

In a statement, the curators said they would explore all options, including a relaunch for Accell’s Dutch operations, based in Amsterdam. The company’s other European branches remain in business.

CEO Jonas Nilsson said: “Every realistic option for the future of the business has been tirelessly explored, and none has resulted in a solution to continue the group in its current form.”

Irish media reported that Quanta Capital, a Dublin-based investment firm founded by former road race cyclist Mel Sutcliffe, was preparing a bid with a number of other investors. Sutcliffe sold Eurotrek Raleigh Ireland to Accell 10 years ago.

Pandemic buyout

Accell was bought by a consortium led by New York-based private equity firm KKR for €1.8 billon in 2022 following a surge in demand for bicycles during the coronavirus pandemic.

But the company struggled to produce bikes fast enough and its costs rose after it ordered too many components in anticipation of a sustained rise in sales that never materialised.

By the time supply chains recovered after lockdown, Accell was left with a mountain of unsold bikes that it had to sell at a discount to limit its losses. Revenues fell 22% in 2024 to just over €1 billion.

Accell closed the Netherlands’ last remaining bike factory, the Batavus plant in Heerenveen, last year, shifting production to Hungary and shedding 160 jobs.

Babboe recall

The company was also hit by the mass recall of 22,000 Babboe cargo bikes after it received hundreds of complaints about the frames breaking on the road, which cost it tens of millions of euros as well as severe reputational damage.

The consumer standards agency NVWA briefly banned Babboe from selling new bikes and launched a criminal investigation amid allegations that the company had tried to cover up the flaws.

The collapse of Accell leaves the Netherlands with only one major bike maker, Gazelle, based in Dieren, as well as a handful of smaller manufacturers such as Kruitbosch (whose brands include Cortina) and Azor.

The consumer protection agency Consumentenbond has advised owners of Accell-made bikes to check the status of their guarantee with the shop or retailer where they bought it. Some replacement parts are still available because they were made by other companies.

World.title: Fire station break-ins soar as criminals steal rescue gear
World.content:
Break-ins at Dutch fire stations, which have risen sharply this year, are threatening life-saving work, the police have said. Criminal gangs are stealing the cutting equipment crews use to free people trapped in crashed cars, which they can be used for robberies.

There were 17 break-ins or attempted break-ins at fire stations in 2024 and 18 in 2025, broadcaster NOS reported. So far this year there have been 50. Stations in Maassluis, Aalsmeer and Ten Boer were all targeted in the past week.

The police, the fire service and the public prosecution department have begun working together nationally to stop the thefts. “One way or another, we are going to put a stop to this,” Jos van der Stap of the national police told NOS.

Police believe experienced criminals have discovered a market for the specialist tools. Van der Stap said they are being used in raids on jewellers and, abroad, to break open cash machines, and have turned up in several places across Europe.

Steven van der Looij of Brandweer Nederland, the national fire service organisation, said staff who work day and night at stations find it terrible thatpeople are coming into the buildings. Both quiet rural stations and busy city ones staffed around the clock have been hit.

Locking the equipment away is not straightforward. Everything on a fire engine is laid out so it can be grabbed at speed, Van der Looij said, and every extra lock has to be undone again. “Every second counts.”

Security cameras are being installed at some stations and windows are being replaced with mirrored glass.

World.title: Mental health services lose track of 62,500 people, says report
World.content:
A quarter of adults with a severe mental illness in the Netherlands – an estimated 62,500 people – are receiving no or insufficient care and have dropped out of sight of mental health services altogether, according to a report from the sector body de Nederlandse GGZ.

The organisation puts the total number of adults with a severe mental illness at around 250,000. What goes wrong, it says, is rarely the treatment itself but the handover – the point at which someone leaves a clinic, moves house or finishes a prison sentence.

“A discharge from a clinic, a house move or the end of a period in detention must not become the moment at which someone loses their support,” GGZ chair Ruth Peetoom said in a statement on Tuesday. “A psychological vulnerability does not disappear when a care pathway or an assessment comes to an end.”

Nowhere to go

The housing crisis is one of the biggest obstacles in helping patients through the transition out of care. The report calculates that 3,980 social housing units are needed each year for people leaving sheltered accommodation, but only 1,320 came free in 2023.

Around 33,000 people aged between 18 and 65 were registered as homeless at the start of 2024.

The pattern is similar for people leaving prison. Of the roughly 5,000 people released each year after more than three months inside, 27% are homeless or have no known address immediately afterwards, and almost half reoffend within two years.

Outreach

The report calls for assertive outreach – teams that actively go looking for people who are not asking for help – to be made a statutory duty for councils again.

It has not been one since social care was devolved in 2015, and funding is now split between health insurers, councils and central government, on top of the pressure on waiting lists that has already prompted legal action against the state.

Debate about severe mental illness in the Netherlands is dominated by figures on nuisance and public safety, the report says. It puts the number of people who pose a safety risk to others at around 1,500, against 24,000 to 60,000 who are a risk to themselves, through self-neglect, homelessness or avoiding care.

If you are struggling with your mental health, support is available. The MIND Hulplijn offers free, anonymous advice on 0900-1450, on weekdays from 9am to 9pm, or via mindhulplijn.nl. In a crisis, contact your family doctor or call 113.

The Polish government has appealed to Starlink, the satellite internet service operated by Elon Musk’s SpaceX, to reverse its decision to exclude Poland from its European roaming area. It says that Polish users, who will now face greater costs when travelling, should not be treated as “second-tier customers”. Starlink, which provides users with portable terminals that act as receivers for internet connections from its network of satellites, offers a “Roam” service that lets customers continue using their connection outside their home country without extra charges as long as they remain within their designated region. One region is Europe, in which Starlink has included 36 countries and territories. However, the firm makes clear that “Poland is not included in the Europe region”, meaning users registered in that country are not included in the Roam system. The company offered no explanation for Poland’s exclusion from the system. Some media reports have suggested that it is because terminals registered in Poland are used in Ukraine. However, Ukraine is itself not included in Starlink’s European “Roam” region. The proportion of Poles who hold a negative view of Polish-Ukrainian relations has risen to 46%, the highest figure ever recorded by Polish state research agency CBOS. Only 12% think relations are good. By contrast, three years ago, in mid-2023, only 3% had a negative view and 64% a positive one. Meanwhile, CBOS also found that belief among Poles that reconciliation between the two neighbours, who share a difficult history, is possible is at its lowest level on record, 53%, down from 78% three years ago. The findings follow other polls showing worsening attitudes towards Ukraine and Ukrainians in Poland in recent years, and come amid an ongoing diplomatic crisis triggered by President Volodymyr Zelensky naming a military unit after a group that massacred Poles in World War Two. Przekonanie o możliwości pojednania między Polakami 🇵🇱 a Ukraińcami 🇺🇦 spadło do najniższego poziomu w historii naszych pomiarów. 📙 Więcej w komunikacie #CBOS "Stosunki polsko-ukraińskie" ⤵️ https://t.co/kw2o4upY3Q#Ukraina #Ukraińcy pic.twitter.com/LItCFC3f2m — CBOS (@CBOS_Info) August 11, 2026 Relations between Poland and Ukraine improved significantly in the wake of Russia’s full-scale invasion in February 2022, as Poland welcomed millions of Ukrainian refugees and provided Kyiv with extensive military, humanitarian and diplomatic support. However, since 2023, those relations have been hit by a series of controversies over Ukrainian agricultural exports, border blockades by Polish farmers and truckers, and, above all, over the two nations’ difficult World War Two history. Among Poles who now hold a negative view of relations, CBOS also asked them who was responsible for the situation. A large majority, 65%, primarily blamed Ukraine, while only 4% said it was Poland’s fault and 28% placed responsibility on both sides. In its regular surveys since 1997, the agency has also asked Poles if they believe that reconciliation between Poles and Ukrainians is possible or not. In the early 2000s, that figure rose to a record level of 81%, and in 2023 it still stood at 78%. Now, however, it has dropped to an all-time low of 53%. There have long been tensions between Poland and Ukraine over their difficult, intertwined histories, in particular during the first half of the 20th century. In World War Two, Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Polish civilians, mostly women and children, in an ethnic-cleansing operation known as the Volhynia massacres. Poland has officially recognised that episode as a genocide. However, Ukraine rejects that label and also points to the persecution of Ukrainians who lived in the interwar Polish state, as well as to massacres of Ukrainians by Polish groups during World War Two. Long-simmering tensions between Poland and Ukraine over WWII massacres have finally boiled over, prompting a diplomatic crisis.@danieltilles1 looks at how we got here and what it may mean for the two countries and Europe more broadly https://t.co/a8tiYJJHRr — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 22, 2026 Those tensions recently boiled over after Zelensky, in May this year, approved a request to rename a military unit after the “heroes of the Ukrainian Insurgent Army (UPA)”, the group that led the Volhynia massacres but is remembered positively in Ukraine for its role in fighting Moscow-imposed Soviet rule. Zelensky’s decision prompted his Polish counterpart, Karol Nawrocki, to strip the Ukrainian president of Poland’s highest honour. While tensions have since calmed somewhat, the dispute remains unresolved. However, even before that diplomatic crisis broke out, polling showed increasingly negative attitudes in Poland towards both Ukraine and Ukrainians, who are by far the country’s largest immigrant group. In its annual survey of attitudes towards various national and ethnic groups, published in February, CBOS found that the proportion of Poles who said they disliked Ukrainians had increased by five percentage points year-on-year, to 43%. Only 29% said they liked Ukrainians. In January, CBOS reported that opposition to accepting Ukrainian refugees in Poland had risen to its highest ever level. In December 2024, a poll in Ukraine found that positive sentiment towards Poles had fallen by half in the space of two years. The proportion of Poles opposed to accepting Ukrainian refugees has reached its highest ever level of 46%, up from 3% in the wake of Russia's full-scale invasion. Other recent surveys have also indicated declining sympathy towards Ukrainians among Poles https://t.co/DLPGY2ToZG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 7, 2026 Meanwhile, the number of reported hate crimes against Ukrainians in Poland rose by 30% in the first half of 2026, including a number of high-profile incidents. Poland’s government has blamed increasing anti-Ukrainian rhetoric from the right-wing and far-right opposition. Last month, Ukraine’s foreign minister, Andrii Sybiha, called on “Polish politicians to stop inciting hatred against Ukrainians”. CBOS’s new study shows that attitudes towards relations with Ukraine differ significantly depending on political affiliation. Whereas 35% of supporters of the centrist Civic Coalition (KO), Poland’s main ruling party, hold a negative view of relations, that rises to 52% among voters of the national-conservative opposition Law and Justice (PiS) party and 81% for the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). Among those with a negative view, 49% of KO voters blamed Poland and Ukraine equally for the situation while 10% blamed mainly Poland. By contrast, 86% of Confederation supporters and 82% of PiS supporters placed responsibility on the Ukrainian side. Demonstrations took place in 25 Polish cities on Sunday against the “growing wave of hate and violence” against Ukrainians, who are Poland’s largest immigrant group. The development marks a major milestone in a 15 billion zloty (€3.5 billion) programme to modernise the ageing Polish navy and strengthen NATO’s maritime defences. “Poland is becoming a maritime power in the Baltic Sea,” declared Prime Minister Donald Tusk at a ceremony to name the new ship, which he attended alongside opposition-aligned President Karol Nawrocki in a rare show of unity. Na terenie PGZ Stoczni Wojennej w Gdyni prezydent RP Karol Nawrocki, @PremierRP @donaldtusk oraz wiceministrowie @MON_GOV_PL @magdasobkowiak i @pawelbejda uczestniczą w uroczystości chrztu pierwszej jednostki programu „Miecznik”, fregaty wielozadaniowej – przyszłego ORP Wicher. pic.twitter.com/X2ftjoKTLZ — Ministerstwo Obrony Narodowej 🇵🇱 (@MON_GOV_PL) August 12, 2026 The ORP Wicher, a medium-sized warship designed for escort, air defence and other fleet protection duties, is the first of three multi-role frigates based on Britain’s Arrowhead 140 design being built under Poland’s Miecznik programme, the largest modernisation project in the history of the Polish Navy. It is due to be launched on Thursday in a complex manoeuvre involving its transfer and controlled launch from a semi-submersible barge. Shipyard officials have described the operation as one of the most demanding engineering projects undertaken by Poland’s shipbuilding industry. The three frigates are intended to form the core of Poland’s surface fleet and will replace Poland’s two current Oliver Hazard Perry-class frigates, which were constructed in the 1970s and transferred from the US Navy in the years 2000 and 2002. Ahead of Wicher’s launch, leading Polish officials attended the naming ceremony in Gdynia, including Tusk and Nawrocki, who are normally bitter rivals but have sought to present a more united front when it comes to national defence. “There can be no arguments or disputes when it comes to our country’s security,” said Tusk, who declared that Poland was seeking to play a role in “determining not only its own future, but also the entire region and Europe”. Nawrocki, meanwhile, said that the modernisation of the Polish navy “sends a clear message that we will develop our armed forces in every theatre – on water, on land, and in the air”. Both leaders also hailed the fact that the new frigates are being built in Poland itself, helping bolster the Polish shipbuilding industry. World.title: Negative views of Poland’s justice system have grown under Tusk government, finds state pollster
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. The proportion of Poles who negatively assess their country’s justice system has increased under the current government, despite its promises to restore the rule of law and ensure that courts function more effectively and independently. New polling by state research agency CBOS found that, in June this year, 61% of Poles had a negative view of the functioning of the justice system, up from 55% in 2022 and 51% in 2017, when the former Law and Justice (PiS) government was in power. Only 26% now positively assess the system, down from 28% in 2022 and 36% in 2017. The last time positive views were lower was in 2005 (22%). The findings come two and a half years after the current government, a coalition ranging from left to centre right led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power in December 2023, replacing the national-conservative PiS administration. One of Tusk’s main promises was to restore the rule of law after eight years in which PiS had implemented a series of contested judicial reforms that experts, European courts and many Polish judges had condemned as undermining the independence and functioning of the judiciary. However, Tusk’s government has struggled to implement its promised changes. In many cases, its efforts have been blocked by PiS-aligned Presidents Andrzej Duda and Karol Nawrocki or other officials appointed under the former government. But in other cases, such as with a pledge to separate the functions of justice minister and prosecutor general, which were fused by PiS in 2016, the current ruling coalition has simply not followed through on its promises. In its latest polling, CBOS found that supporters of the current opposition are most dissatisfied with the functioning of the justice system: 72% of PiS voters have a negative view, as do 71% of those who support the far-right Confederation (Konfederacja). However, even among voters of Tusk’s centrist Civic Coalition (KO) party, a majority, 53%, have a negative opinion, with only 38% holding a positive one. Interestingly, public attitudes towards judges themselves have hardly changed. Currently, 19% of Poles have a positive view towards them and 23% a negative one. That is similar to findings in 2017 (22% positive, 24% negative) and 2012 (19% positive, 23% negative). More Poles (35%) think that the rule of law has got worse under Tusk's government than believe it has improved (24%). A further 28% think there has been no change, finds a new poll https://t.co/KkiuY2vDSW — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) January 5, 2025 When asked to identify the greatest problems with the justice system, Poles instead often point to structural issues – that is, those that are under the control of politicians. The most commonly identified problem (chosen by 38% of respondents, who could select up to three main problems) was “prolonged proceedings” in court cases. The second biggest issue was “politicisation of courts” (18%). Only 4% said that “judges’ neglect of duty, incompetence and impunity” were among the biggest problems. However, 23% of respondents were unable to name a single major issue that the justice system faces. Fifteen months since the change of government, Poland's rule-of-law crisis continues – indeed, many Poles think the situation has got worse.@J_Jaraczewski explains the roots of the crisis, what its impact has been, and how it might be resolved https://t.co/7KOCURV3dU — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 17, 2025 CBOS’s findings echo a number of other polls. After the first year of Tusk’s government, a survey by SW Research for the Rzeczpospolita daily found that 35% of Poles thought the rule-of-law situation had got worse, compared to only 24% who thought it had improved. Another poll by the same agency for Onet, a news website, in January this year similarly found that 40% of Poles believe the justice system has not improved under the current government, while only 33% think it has got better. In response to the latter poll, justice minister Waldemar Żurek admitted to Onet that there had been problems in addressing the rule of law. But he blamed the “hurdles [put] in our path” by Presidents Duda and Nawrocki. Opposition-aligned President @NawrockiKn has vetoed a government bill intended to reform a judicial body at the heart of Poland’s rule-of-law crisis. He argued that the measures would simply create even greater “legal chaos” https://t.co/I7FHRKIoP1 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) February 19, 2026 In 2024, Duda refused to sign government bills overhauling the Constitutional Tribunal (TK), which still contains judges illegitimately appointed under the former PiS administration. As a result, Tusk’s government refuses to recognise rulings issued by the TK. In February this year, Duda’s successor, Nawrocki, vetoed a government bill intended to restore the legitimacy of the National Council of the Judiciary (KRS), the body responsible for nominating judges to positions on courts. In 2017, the KRS was overhauled under PiS in a manner that rendered it illegitimate, according to multiple Polish and European court rulings. That in turn has led to doubts over the legal status of around 3,000 judges appointed by the KRS since 2017 and all the rulings issued by them. Nawrocki has also refused to swear in four new TK judges nominated by parliament this year, despite an order by the European Court of Human Rights that they be allowed to take up their positions. The European Court of Human Rights has ordered Poland’s Constitutional Tribunal (TK) to accept four judges whom opposition-aligned President Nawrocki refused to swear in. The decision was welcomed by the government but rejected by the TK itself https://t.co/9NxInPdYk9 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) May 6, 2026 ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Indians and Colombians now third and fourth largest groups of foreign workers in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. Indians are now the third-largest group of foreign workers in Poland, followed by Colombians, according to new data from the country’s Social Insurance Institute (ZUS). Ukrainians remain by far the largest immigrant group, followed by Belarusians. The figures also show that the overall number of registered foreign workers has risen more than 8% over the last year, a faster rate of growth than in recent years. However, the government official responsible for migration strategy says this is because stricter government measures have pushed some employers to register previously uninsured workers. The ZUS data, reported by Dziennik Gazeta Prawna (DGP), a leading daily, show that there were 1.34 million foreign workers registered in ZUS at the end of June, up from 1.24 million at the same point last year. That 8.2% increase is larger than the growth rate of around 6% seen in each of the previous two years, notes the newspaper. Maciej Duszczyk, the deputy interior minister responsible for migration, commented that the rise actually reflects the government’s tougher migration strategy, which he said “forces employers to report for insurance those who arrived earlier” but were working unregistered The official pointed to recent data showing that, in fact, in the first half of this year, Poland issued 50% fewer work permits to foreigners than in the same period of 2025. Dane ZUS pokazują dokładnie to co zakładaliśmy w Strategi Migracyjnej. Radykalny spadek liczby wydawanych, nowych zezwoleń na pracę (ponad 50% rok do roku) wymusza na pracodawcach zgłaszanie do ubezpieczenia, tych którzy przyjechali wcześniej. Tylko w pełni legalne zatrudnienie! — Maciek Duszczyk (@MaciekDuszczyk) August 11, 2026 Ukrainians remain by far the largest group of registered foreign workers, with 901,000 now in the system, a 10.1% rise from a year earlier. Belarusians (144,000, up 4.9%) remain in second. But two non-European migrant groups whose numbers have been growing rapidly in recent years now occupy third and fourth place: Indians (25,500, up 4.9%) and Colombians (23,000, up 31%, which was the fastest growth of any national group). Georgians, who had previously been the third-largest group, saw their number fall by 17% to 22,000, meaning they are now in fifth, ahead of Filipinos (15,400, down 2%), Moldovans (14,200, down 1%), Nepalis (13,400, up 8.3%), Vietnamese (12,200, up 6.1%), and Russians (11,800, down 2.5%). Latin American migration to Poland is booming, with 45,000 work permits issued last year, five times more than in 2022@Gosia_Tomczak looks at what is driving this trend and what challenges and opportunities it has created for both the migrants and Poland https://t.co/tl1wUTCaC0 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) October 15, 2025 ZUS’s data also show that foreign workers are increasingly establishing their own businesses in Poland, which Dziennik Gazeta Prawna notes is a sign that they are establishing longer-term ties with the country but also a result of an easier online system for registering businesses. In 2021, only 22,700 foreigners had a registered business in Poland, a figure that now is now almost five times higher, at 102,000. The rise has been driven in particular by Ukrainians, many of whom are legally entitled to establish companies in Poland under the same terms as Polish citizens. As a result, 7.6% of foreign workers now run their own business, up from 6.7% a year ago and from 2.7% before Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine, which led to a wave of Ukrainian refugees settling in Poland. Ukrainian refugees boosted Poland’s GDP by 2.7% last year while not raising unemployment or lowering wages, finds a report by the UN @Refugees agency and @Deloitte "Whoever thinks refugees are a burden on the economy should think again," says @UNHCRPoland https://t.co/rOvtOvBNwG — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) June 12, 2025 Over the last decade, even before the war in Ukraine, Poland has experienced a wave of migration unprecedented in its history and among the largest anywhere in Europe. For six years running, between 2017 and 2022, it issued more first residence permits to immigrants from outside the European Union than did any other member state. Much of the surge in immigration came during the rule of the national-conservative Law and Justice (PiS) government from 2015 to 2023, despite its strong anti-migrant rhetoric. The current government, a more liberal coalition led by Prime Minister Donald Tusk, came to power pledging to reduce immigration, which it said had got out of control under PiS. Under Tusk’s government, in 2024, Poland issued the lowest number of residence permits to non-EU immigrants in a decade. In 2025, the government introduced tougher entry requirements for foreign workers and students. It has also stepped up deportations of foreigners who have broken the law. However, Duszczyk notes that the current government still sees “selective and responsible migration” as a way to “maintain the competitiveness of the economy without limiting wage growth”. ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. World.title: Mother bear and cubs spotted on busy hiking trail in Poland
World.content: Keep our news free from ads and paywalls by making a donation to support our work! Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and is published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers. We cannot do what we do without your support. A female brown bear and her three cubs have been spotted in Poland’s Tatra mountains crossing a popular trail filled with hikers, with the animals coming unusually close to people. According to an official from Tatra National Park, where the incident took place, the behaviour could be a survival strategy by the mother to protect her young from male bears, which can kill cubs but tend to avoid humans. In a video posted on Sunday, the mother and three cubs were seen crossing the Chochołowska Valley trail in broad daylight, as crowds of people looked on Videos of the bear family have appeared increasingly often on social media, prompting questions about whether the animals are becoming less wary of people. But park officials say the female’s behaviour may have a biological explanation. “As we know, male brown bears are infanticidal. They kill not only other bears’ cubs, but their own as well. So the females, to avoid contact with the males, tend to stay closer to people,” Tomasz Zwijacz-Kozica, a park official, told local newspaper Gazeta Krakowska. “Females sense this instinctively and generally use the presence of people as a sort of shield to defend themselves against these males,” he added. The park staff hope to gather more detailed data on the female bear’s movements and behaviour in the future by possibly fitting her with a telemetry collar. They note that similar behaviour has been seen before. Around 20 years ago, a female bear drew attention when hundreds of tourists photographed her. They advise visitors to remain calm if they encounter a bear and to follow several basic rules, including staying calm and not running or making sudden movements, which may trigger a pursuit; not approaching the animals; and not attempting to take close-up photographs or use a flash. If a bear is encountered, visitors should slowly retreat in the direction from which they came while maintaining eye contact with the animal. Particular caution is required when cubs are present. Visitors should also avoid feeding bears or leaving rubbish behind. The smell of food can attract animals to trails and encourage behaviour that brings them into dangerous contact with people. A woman has died after being attacked by a bear in a forest in southeastern Poland. Such incidents are extremely rare, with the last fatal bear attack in the country reported in 2014 https://t.co/sAC2MPAvfh — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) April 23, 2026 Estimates of Poland’s brown bear population vary between 120 and 400, with most found in the southeastern Bieszczady mountains as well as the Tatras and Beskids further west. The population is thought to be growing, with a rise in reports of encounters with humans. In April this year, a woman was killed in a bear attack, Poland’s first such fatality since 2014. Another bear attack earlier in the year in the same region left a man with head and limb injuries. In March, the government launched a new 16 million zloty (€3.7 million) scheme aimed at both protecting bears and ensuring the safety of their human neighbours. It includes the creation of a special force to monitor and respond to bear sightings, including fitting the animals with tracking collars. In 2022, the town of Zakopane, located at the foot of the Tatra mountains, installed bear-proof rubbish bins to prevent animals from foraging in them – and thereby coming closer to areas of human population Poland has launched a new programme to protect brown bears and ensure the safety of their human neighbours, amid growing reports of encounters. A special force will be set up to respond to bear sightings and fit the animals with tracking collars https://t.co/GEOCpnEj70 — Notes from Poland 🇵🇱 (@notesfrompoland) March 21, 2026 ​ Notes from Poland is run by a small editorial team and published by an independent, non-profit foundation that is funded through donations from our readers.
