World.title: Senior Iraqi security delegation heads to Saudi Arabia
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — A high-level Iraqi security delegation will travel to Riyadh on Thursday, August 13, 2026, to conduct talks regarding recent cross-border drone strikes targeting petroleum infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, according to a senior government source.

The delegation will be led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari, Director of the Office of the Commander-in-Chief of the Armed Forces, alongside Iraqi National Intelligence Service (INIS) Chief Hamid Al-Shatri. The trip follows a reciprocal visit to Baghdad days earlier by Saudi Intelligence Chief Khalid bin Ali Al-Humaidan.

Key Security & Diplomatic Developments

High-Level Delegation: Led by General Abdul-Amir Al-Shammari and Intelligence Chief Hamid Al-Shatri to establish joint intelligence-sharing protocols with Riyadh.

Incident Background: Late last month, the Saudi Ministry of Defense reported intercepting several drones originating from Iraqi territory targeting oil facilities in the Eastern Province and Riyadh.

Domestic Investigation: Prime Minister and Commander-in-Chief Ali Falih al-Zaidi ordered a formal military investigation into the launch origins following the Saudi allegations.

Diplomatic Mediation: The visit comes after international and regional mediation restored diplomatic channels following the cancellation of Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s planned trip to Riyadh late last month amid joint U.S.-Saudi strikes inside Iraq.

Regional Position: During a recent bilateral meeting in Amman between Saudi Foreign Minister Faisal bin Farhan and Iraqi Foreign Minister Fuad Hussein, Riyadh reaffirmed support for Iraq while stressing the necessity that Iraqi territory not be utilized as a platform for aggression against neighboring states.

The bilateral security summit aims to reinforce radar tracking, anti-drone intelligence sharing, and border surveillance between Baghdad and Riyadh.

While the “Islamic Resistance in Iraq” denied responsibility for the Saudi oil facility strikes, Prime Minister Al-Zaidi’s administration is taking direct steps to prevent unauthorized non-state launches, safeguard Iraqi sovereignty, and protect diplomatic and economic ties with Riyadh.

World.title: Supreme Judicial Council President Faiq Zidan to visit Syria
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — President of the Iraqi Supreme Judicial Council, Judge Faiq Zidan, is scheduled to conduct an official visit to Syria on Thursday, August 13, 2026, marking a landmark first-of-its-kind judicial mission to Damascus, according to a senior official source.

The high-level visit aims to hold structured talks with Syrian judicial authorities to address shared legal frameworks, cross-border judicial coordination, counter-terrorism extradition agreements, and legal mechanisms regulating bilateral trade corridors.

World.title: Iraq Transport Ministry reports 95% completion of Development Road designs
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Minister of Transport Wahab Al-Hasani met with the Parliamentary Transport and Communications Committee on Tuesday, August 11, 2026, to review execution milestones across strategic infrastructure projects, including the Development Road, the Grand Fao Port, and national rail modernization.

During the executive session, Al-Hasani presented technical updates on the 1,200-kilometer Development Road Project, confirming that primary design phases are near completion, with railway engineering blueprints reaching 95% and highway transit designs at 85%.

Key Operational Metrics & Project Milestones

Development Road Project: Designs for the 1,200 km transit corridor are nearly complete (95% for railway tracks, 85% for highways). The MOU executed with Turkey serves as a preliminary framework with no current financial or legal obligations.

Grand Fao Port: Submerged tunnel construction reached 86% completion, alongside advanced structural work across five main container berths.

Rail Network Modernization: Ministry teams are actively pursuing the rehabilitation of the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia railway corridor extending toward the Syrian border.

Maritime Fleet Mobilization: State maritime companies confirmed readiness to deploy Iraqi vessels to transport crude oil and refined petroleum products to support alternative national export strategies.

Administrative & Executive Actions: Al-Hasani confirmed the suspension of Iraqi Airways’ former Director-General and two deputies following an internal investigative audit.

Legislative Alignment: Agreement reached to draft amendments to Transport Law No. 80 of 1983 and establish a joint parliamentary-executive committee holding weekly meetings to update transport regulations.

The meeting highlights Iraq’s strategy to transform into a central logistics bridge connecting the Gulf to Europe, bypassing maritime transit chokepoints.

By pairing the Grand Fao Port’s advancing infrastructure with overland rail links extending north to Turkey and west through the Baghdad–Mosul–Rabia line toward Syria, the Ministry of Transport is laying the groundwork for integrated commercial supply chains across Eurasia.

World.title: MP Abdul Jabbar proposes 145 km pipeline to boost Basra crude to Ceyhan
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Independent MP and Secretary-General of the Fao–Zakho Coalition, Amer Abdul-Jabbar, proposed a plan on Wednesday, August 12, 2026, to construct a 145-kilometer oil pipeline link to transport Basra crude north toward Turkey’s Ceyhan terminal.

Abdul-Jabbar stated via social media that the proposed missing link would instantly increase Iraq’s northern export capacity by 150,000 to 300,000 barrels per day (bpd). To avoid drawing on the federal budget during the ongoing liquidity crisis, he advocated launching a “National Volunteer Effort,” utilizing surplus piping from state-owned enterprises alongside logistical backing from private contractors operating under Ministry of Oil contracts.

Key Technical & Strategy Highlights

Proposed Pipeline Link: A 145 km strategic bypass connecting southern oilfields in Basra directly to northern export routes toward the Turkish port of Ceyhan.

Capacity Increase: Designed to boost crude export flows by 150,000 to 300,000 bpd, mitigating bottlenecks caused by Persian Gulf shipping disruptions.

Zero-Cost Volunteer Framework: Proposed execution via a “National Volunteer Effort” using inventory audits of unused piping across state firms and private sector contractor support.

Existing Ministry Export Strategy: Complements Oil Minister Basim Mohammed Khudair’s August 9 plan to export 750,000 bpd to Ceyhan via: 450,000 bpd pumped through the Strategic Pipeline after rehabilitating the PS3 pump station in Najaf and K3 in Haditha. 300,000 bpd transported via road tankers (including 200,000 bpd through KAR Group and 100,000 bpd under a secondary contract).

Long-Term Iraqi-Turkish Energy Framework: Ministry of Oil is finalizing a 1-year interim agreement with Ankara, paving the way for a 10- to 20-year strategic partnership involving Turkish BOTAŞ and BP in developing Kirkuk oilfields.

Abdul-Jabbar’s proposal comes as the Ministry of Oil accelerates alternative land-based export channels to bypass the blocked Strait of Hormuz.

Minister Khudair previously confirmed that Iraq’s State Company for Oil Projects (SCOP) and Turkey’s BOTAŞ are actively inspecting and rehabilitating the northern export system to handle between 500,000 and 750,000 bpd. Implementing the 145 km bypass link could offer Baghdad an immediate, low-cost mechanism to restore crude cash flows while long-term pipeline infrastructure is constructed toward Syria and Jordan.

World.title: Meta meets its own ‘tobacco’ moment in court
World.content:
Oakland – With billions of users around the world, Meta will defend itself against allegations of harming children in a new trial in the United States this week, which experts describe as social media’s big tobacco moment.

After a coalition of states sued Meta in 2023 for allegedly designing addictive features for kids in its apps, four states were selected to represent their claims: California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey.

Top prosecutors of those states now aim to prove in federal court that Meta deliberately made Facebook and Instagram addictive for children.

Meta “strongly disagrees with these allegations” and is “confident the evidence will show our longstanding commitment to supporting young people,” a spokesperson told AFP, adding that the company has “listened to parents, worked with experts and law enforcement.”

Although it’s not the first lawsuit that seeks to hold a social media company accountable for its impact on mental health and safety, it could become one of the most consequential.

“It really feels like tobacco in the 1990s,” Vincent Joralemon, a director at Berkeley’s Life Sciences Law and Policy Center, told AFP.

While these cases about social media harms revolve around the intersection of technology and addiction, the legal argument in this case against Meta centers on its business practices, just like when the federal government sued tobacco companies around three decades ago, Joralemon said.

By the early 1990s, decades of research showed that tobacco use caused health problems such as cancer, and eventually additional investigations revealed how the industry deliberately downplayed, and even concealed, the harmful impacts of its products.

– ‘Protecting teens’ –

Dozens of US states sued four major tobacco companies, and by 1998, won a landmark settlement agreement which included financial penalties and changes to how products were marketed, particularly to children whom the industry targeted with s featuring cartoon characters, the most famous of which was known as “Joe Camel.”

Jury selection begins today in Oakland, a short drive from San Francisco and opening statements are expected to begin August 18.

Meta was convicted on similar grounds in separate trials held in Los Angeles and New Mexico, with combined damages that approach $1 billion.

In Oakland, the states are demanding a long list of changes to Meta’s apps, in addition to financial penalties as high as $1.4 trillion, close to Meta’s entire market value which hovers around $1.5 trillion.

Despite the eye-popping number, money isn’t Meta’s biggest problem, if it were to lose the case.

“The huge issue here is reputational harm” and being forced to make major changes, Joralemon said.

“Putting a CEO on the witness stand can be quite damning,” as well, he said.

Meta founder and chief Mark Zuckerberg is among the star witnesses expected to testify.

The case could be “the beginning of a broader reckoning” for Meta, Nora Freeman Engstrom told AFP via email. She is a law professor and associate dean at Stanford.

It will be important to see the “gap” between what Meta knew privately and what it disclosed publicly, Engstrom said.

Meta is “confident in our record of protecting teens online and will continue to defend ourselves against claims that misrepresent the facts,” Meta told AFP last week.

With so many plaintiffs suing Meta and other social media companies, these lawsuits could potentially “go on for decades,” Joralemon said.

In May, Snap, TikTok, YouTube and Meta settled with a school district in Kentucky for $27 million to avoid another trial that was expected to set a precedent for around 1,200 similar lawsuits.

On Monday, a federal appeals court ruled that more than 3,000 additional lawsuits filed against Meta, YouTube-parent Google, Snap and TikTok can proceed.

World.title: Colombia rescuers find woman alive as quake death toll passes 240
World.content:
Pereira – Colombian rescuers pulled a 32-year-old woman alive from the rubble of a collapsed building Tuesday, sparking cheers and applause as exhausted crews raced to find more survivors from the country’s strongest earthquake in a century.

Daniela Largo was carried from the wreckage wrapped in a blue blanket as rescuers embraced and relatives shouted out with joy.

The rescue came as soldiers, firefighters and volunteers searched collapsed buildings across western Colombia after a 7.4-magnitude quake killed at least 241 people and injured more than 1,600.

“We were losing hope and then we received a call,” said her mother Sandra Milena Perez in Pereira.

Perez said a local resident heard cries for help beneath the rubble and joined neighbors in removing debris before professional rescuers arrived.

“Thanks to him, today we’re happy,” she said. “At home her 12-year-old son is waiting for her.”

In Pereira and in Cali, emergency crews used cranes, dogs and heavy machinery to search ruined buildings while volunteers formed human chains to clear debris by hand, hoping to reach people still trapped beneath collapsed structures.

As darkness fell, families prepared to sleep in parks as aftershocks rattled damaged neighborhoods where entire blocks had been reduced to rubble.

The quake overwhelmed parts of the health system, turning the rescue effort into one of Colombia’s largest disaster responses in years.

“The house came down on top of us. I wasn’t able to get out,” said Beatriz Arcos, who was trapped with her husband and mother beneath their collapsed condominium.

“It took about an hour to get us out.” Arcos said she was hospitalized after a concrete block fell on her back. Her husband and mother were also injured.

In Cali, residents armed with picks, shovels and their bare hands joined firefighters in digging through collapsed buildings.

Rescuers stopped every few minutes to call into the rubble and listen for any response.

“We’re doing this with our hands, with gloves” said volunteer Pablo Cesar Ruiz “It’s sad to see time slipping away.”

In Pereira, army units and sniffer dogs combed through twisted concrete and exposed steel.

At one site, a rescue squad leader abruptly raised his fist, stopping workers so they could listen for signs of life.

Volunteers formed human chains, passing bricks and chunks of masonry hand-to-hand to clear paths into collapsed structures.

– ‘So much effort’ –

For many families, the desperate search was becoming a vigil.

“My aunt lived there. She’s under the rubble,” said Jorge Gonzalez, standing beside a collapsed building in Pereira.

“I arrived yesterday and I haven’t left, and until they find her body I don’t intend to leave here.”

While some families waited for news of missing relatives, others were grappling with the loss of homes, possessions and livelihoods.

“We lost everything,” said Stella Galvis, fighting back tears after escaping the collapse of her home.

“We survived by a miracle, since I managed to get my little boy out and my partner managed to get out too.”

From the air, neighborhoods in Cali appeared flattened, with piles of grey rubble replacing entire blocks of homes and apartment buildings.

Nearby, cars lay crushed beneath fallen walls and concrete slabs.

On one mound of debris, a young couple climbed over broken masonry searching for belongings.

They recovered a box from inside a child’s bright red bedside table.

Many survivors spent the night outdoors, either because their homes were damaged or because they feared aftershocks.

One park in Pereira was transformed into a makeshift shelter with tents and mattresses.

“We lost everything, but we’re alive,” said 23-year-old John Tabasco, who was camped there with his wife and seven-month-old son.

“We’ve never had to do this before, to depend on someone else to help us. It’s amazing how life can change.”

Others struggled to come to terms with losing homes built over decades.

“You buy a little house with so much effort, spending 40, 50 years struggling to get yourself that house, you finally get it and in just a few days it all goes down the drain,” said 79-year-old Jaime Alzate.

In Cali, part of the Hospital Universitario del Valle collapsed during the quake, forcing doctors to move patients into a parking lot and treat some in the open air.

Yet amid the destruction, many Colombians mobilized to help.

Thousands brought water, food and supplies to affected neighborhoods, while long lines formed outside blood donation centers.

“It’s about wanting to help your community, your city and your country,” said blood donor Ferney Cabrera.

President Abelardo de la Espriella declared a state of emergency and promised rent subsidies for affected families Tuesday during a visit to Pereira.

The United States announced $15.5 million in emergency aid, while messages of support and offers of assistance arrived from around the world.

As aftershocks continued to rattle damaged cities, rescue crews pressed on through the ruins, hoping more voices, taps or whistles might still emerge.

World.title: Passengers rescued as second ferry in days catches fire in Indonesia
World.content:
Mataram – A navy vessel and other ships rushed in Wednesday to rescue over 100 people from a ferry on fire off the tourist island of Bali, officials said, in the second such incident in days.

There were no immediate reports of casualties among the passengers and crew, with at least 114 people on board, according to the manifest.

The passenger ferry had been sailing from Bali to the next-door island of Lombok when it caught fire in the early morning hours.

Muhamad Hariyadi, head of the search and rescue agency at Mataram on Lombok island, said the total number of passengers on board was being verified.

He said passengers were evacuated on at least three different vessels, including a navy ship and another ferry.

Search and rescue vessels were at the scene and a helicopter was conducting surveillance from the air.

“As of now, we have not received any report of casualties,” Hariyadi told Metro TV.

“We have approached the ship and confirmed that all passengers are no longer on board,” he added. “We visually see no passengers on the ship.”

Last week, five people died when a ferry caught fire off Java island.

Marine accidents are a regular occurrence in Indonesia — an archipelago of more than 17,000 islands that rely heavily on boat connections.

Lax safety standards and unpredictable weather are the main reasons for the disasters.

A ferry transporting more than 70 people sank while sailing near Selayar, a small island south of Sulawesi, last month.

Four bodies were recovered, but the search operation ended with 14 others still officially missing.

World.title: Charges dropped against Bondi Beach attack hero
World.content:
Sydney – Australian police dropped assault charges on Wednesday against a man lauded for his bravery during last year’s mass shooting at Bondi Beach.

Fruit seller Ahmed al Ahmed was hailed as a hero after footage showed him disarming a gunman during the December 14 attack, which killed 15 people at a Jewish festival.

Ahmed was earlier this year accused of stalking and assaulting his father, charges he denied.

Both charges were withdrawn after a brief hearing on Wednesday, court documents showed.

Ahmed ducked between parked cars as the Bondi shooting unfolded, grabbing one of the two gunmen and wresting away his weapon in an effort to stop the killing.

He sustained gunshot wounds in the attack.

Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese would later meet Ahmed in person, describing him as a “true Australian hero” and an inspiration to all.

World.title: J&K SIA reopens probe into 1990 killings of Kashmiri Pandit poet, nurse
World.content:
On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat

SRINAGAR: Sarvanand Kaul Premi was a poet. Sarla Bhat was a nurse. Both were Kashmiri Pandits who stayed behind when militancy erupted and were killed in 1990. More than three decades later, J&K policeâs SIA revived unresolved cases from the Valleyâs darkest years. The agency searched Wednesday nine locations in its probe into the abduction-murder of Premi and his younger son, weeks after filing a chargesheet in Bhatâs killing.Premi, 66, a poet, teacher and Gandhian, and Verinder were abducted from their village, Soaf Shali near Kokernag, on Apr 30, 1990. They were shot dead the next day. Five days later, the grief-stricken Kaul family left Kashmir, never to return.State Investigation Agencyâs searches were linked to FIR No. 45/1990 registered at Dooru police station in Anantnag. SIA is pursuing militancy-era cases that had lain cold for decades.On June 29, SIA filed a chargesheet in the abduction, torture and killing of Bhat, 27, a staff nurse in the neonatology ward at Sher-i-Kashmir Institute of Medical Sciences in Srinagar. She was allegedly abducted by JKLF from SKIMS Habba Khatoon Hostel on Apr 18, 1990, and taken to Illahibagh-Lal Bazar, tortured and shot dead.Her bullet-riddled body was found the next day at Omer Colony Malabagh in downtown Srinagar.Born in Soaf Shali in 1924, Premi joined Khadi Bhandar after completing his education and became associated with Mahatma Gandhiâs Swadeshi movement. His association with Kashmiri poet Ghulam Ahmad Mahjoor inspired his literary career. He translated Rabindranath Tagoreâs âGitanjaliâ into Kashmiri and the Bhagavad Gita and Ramayana into Kashmiri and Urdu, and advocated secularism and interfaith harmony.J&K govt under then-CM Farooq Abdullah posthumously awarded Premi a gold medal in 1997 for his contribution to Kashmiri literature and communal harmony.The killings from Kashmirâs violent spring of 1990 were part of a wider wave of hostility against Kashmiri Pandits after militancy erupted, driving a mass exodus of the community from the Valley. In 2010, J&K govt under then-CM Omar Abdullah told the assembly that 209 Kashmiri Pandits had been murdered since 1990.

World.title: Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann meets Governor; seeks 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on "humanitarian grounds"
World.content:
Punjab CM Bhagwant Mann meets Governor; seeks 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on "humanitarian grounds"

Punjab chief minister Bhagwant Singh Mann on Wednesday met with the Governor to recommend a 10-day parole for Jagtar Singh Hawara on humanitarian grounds, citing the deteriorating health of the prisoner's mother.Jagtar Singh Hawara is currently serving a life sentence for his involvement in the 1995 assassination of the then Punjab chief minister Beant Singh.Speaking to the media after the meeting, the chief minister stated that the recommendation was made to allow Hawara to meet his mother, who has not seen him in over three decades."A recommendation was made recently regarding the matter of granting parole to Jagtar Singh Hawara so that, on humanitarian grounds, he could be given parole as his mother's health is not well. His mother has a desire to meet him after 31 years," CM Mann said.The chief minister explained that since the case is being heard in the Union Territory, the Governor's role is pivotal in forwarding the request to the Central Government."I met the Governor today because as the case is being heard in the UT, the Governor will have an important role and the matter will be sent to the Centre. The final decision rests with the Centre, but we have requested a 10-day parole," he added.Addressing potential concerns regarding security and public order, CM Mann informed that he has provided a formal assurance to the administration."In this regard, we have assured the Governor that we will not allow the atmosphere to be spoiled in any way and the situation will remain under control," the CM asserted.According to the chief minister, the Governor has responded positively to the request and promised to expedite the administrative formalities."The Governor has assured that he will speak with the Home Secretary of the Government of India today itself to complete the formalities, and Hawara will receive relief soon. The Punjab government will send whatever necessary documents are required from their side," Mann stated.Earlier on August 9, CM Mann wrote to Governor Gulab Chand Kataria regarding the same."It has been brought to my notice that Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara's mother is not in good health due to age-related health problems. Mr Jagtar Singh Hawara has also filed CRWP No. 3868/2026 in the Hon'ble Punjab and Haryana High Court, Chandigarh, seeking direction to release him on parole. The Hon'ble Court has also directed to consider his parole application. Therefore, on the basis of human compassion, I would like to request you to grant 10-day parole as soon as possible," the letter read.

World.title: China says India border 'generally stable' amid tensions in Arunachal
World.content:
China said Wednesday that the situation along the India-China border was âgenerally stable at the momentâ, while declining to confirm reports of increased Chinese military activity in disputed areas near Arunachal Pradesh.

Chinese foreign ministry spokesperson Guo Jiakun made the remarks at a regular press briefing in Beijing in response to questions about videos circulating on Indian social media that purportedly showed heightened Chinese military activity along the border.

Guo said China and India had held the 36th meeting of the Working Mechanism for Consultation and Coordination on Border Affairs the previous week. He said both sides had agreed to maintain communication through diplomatic and military channels and work together to preserve peace and tranquillity along the border.

The comments came a day after India reiterated that its border with China remained a matter of serious concern and that maintaining peace and tranquillity along the Line of Actual Control was essential to the broader relationship between the two countries.

The Chinese response also came amid reports of heightened military activity by Chinese troops in Arunachal Pradeshâs Upper Subansiri region. Beijing claims Arunachal Pradesh as part of what it calls âSouth Tibetâ, a claim consistently rejected by New Delhi.





India had separately pushed back against Chinaâs objections to New Delhi formally identifying 27 locations and geographical features in Arunachal Pradesh by their standard Indian names. The Ministry of External Affairs said the state was an âinalienable and integralâ part of India and that nothing could change that reality.

The two countries reached a disengagement agreement covering the remaining friction points at Depsang and Demchok in October 2024.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping subsequently held talks in Kazan, followed by further diplomatic efforts aimed at improving bilateral relations.

World.title: 'Has no shame': Kangana Ranaut attacks Rahul Gandhi over Amit Shah debate row, Parliament logjam
World.content:
NEW DELHI: BJP MP

on Wednesday launched a sharp attack on Lok Sabha leader of opposition

over the continuing stalemate in Parliament, accusing him of making a "mockery" of the House and the country while refusing the government's offer for a debate on the students' protest.

Ranaut alleged that Gandhi was demanding a statement from Union home minister

over the police action against protesters, while simultaneously saying the opposition would not listen to him.

"I feel he is making a mockery of the country. He constantly ridicules the nation; for him, everything is a joke. This is the first time I am seeing Parliament being made such a mockery of. In the same breath, he says, 'We want an answer from Amit Shah ji--asking whether or not he did such-and-such to the students--while simultaneously declaring, 'We are not here to listen to him'.

He has no sense of shame or propriety left," news agency ANI quoted Ranaut saying.

"The whole world is watching and wondering what kind of person this is. The way he is venting his frustration and insulting Parliament and, by extension, the entire nation and its citizens convinces me, as someone observing his role as leader of the opposition, that this will be his final term," she added.

Ranaut, who represents Mandi in the Lok Sabha, also attacked Gandhi over his political record, saying the Congress under his leadership had "lost a hundred elections" and claiming that he would not retain the leader of opposition post in the future.





"He is demanding the resignation of the Prime Minister--a democratically elected leader who has secured a massive mandate for a third consecutive term. He seems to think that no one else in this country should even exist but him. Then there are his other actions--colluding with figures like Soros or international forces to tear the country apart and leave it in ruins. Ultimately, it doesn't matter whose resignation he demands or what he wants, because the public simply doesn't care about him," she said.

World.title: 'Acting like goondas': CJP’s Saurav Das claims Pondicherry Police ‘harassed’ kin, claims Centre link

on Wednesday alleged that Puducherry Police officials visited his family home and subjected his family members to questioning, claiming that the action was aimed at intimidating him into silence.

World.title: ‘Delete posts, apologise’: Bengal CM Adhikari orders action over derogatory posts about Netaji
World.content:
NEW DELHI: West Bengal chief minister Suvendu Adhikari on Wednesday ordered action against social media posts making unsavoury comment against

.

While talking to reporters, Suvendu said, "Those making derogatory remarks against Netaji on social media should immediately delete posts and issue apology,"

"I have asked police to arrest those making unsavoury comments on Netaji.

Law will be equal for MLAs, MPs, and government officials," he added.

Adhikari also directed all MLAs to set up public service centres in their respective constituencies and name them after Netaji Subhas Chandra Bose.

The chief minister's direction to the police came days after BJP MP Nagendranath Roy, popularly known as Ananta Maharaj, described Netaji as a âwar criminalâ and questioned his leadership and the role of the Azad Hind Fauj in Indiaâs freedom struggle.

World.title: Delhi Police’s ‘Kuchu Puchu’ Gen-Z twist to warn Delhiites about Chinese manjha
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

has found a rather unusual way to join the viral âkuchu-puchuâ Gen Z trend, using internet humour to deliver a serious warning about kite-flying strings.

In a recent social media post, the police urged residents to enjoy kite flying but stay away from banned Chinese manjha and plastic-coated strings, which can cause serious injuries to people and animals.

âDear Kuchu Puchu, Patang Udao but Say NO to Chinese Manjha, Samjhe?â the police wrote, giving its usual safety messaging a more playful, social media-friendly tone.

The message comes as authorities step up action against the banned string in Delhi. The Crime Branch recently seized more than 1,300 rolls of Chinese manjha during an enforcement operation. In a separate action, Central Delhi Police recovered around 120 rolls.

The post quickly drew reactions online, with some users poking fun at the police for adopting the language of Gen Z.

âGen-Z mode of Delhi Policeâ, âThey are updatingâ, some comments read. Behind the light-hearted presentation, however, is a serious safety concern.

Chinese manjha is generally made using synthetic or plastic material and can be coated with abrasive substances. Because of its sharpness, it can cause deep cuts and injuries.





It can also become particularly dangerous for birds, which can get caught in the string while flying. There have already been fatal consequences in Delhi.

Recently, a 32-year-old man travelling to Mundka for business suffered a cut to his neck after coming into contact with Chinese manjha in southwest Delhi's Uttam Nagar.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

In another tragic incident in 2023, a seven-year-old girl died after being injured by Chinese manjha while travelling with her father on a scooter in west Delhi's Paschim Vihar.

The police's latest post therefore carries a straightforward message beneath all the social media humour. People can continue flying kites and enjoying the activity, but using banned synthetic strings can put lives at risk.

The campaign also reflects a broader change in the way police departments communicate with the public, with serious safety warnings increasingly being delivered through the language, trends and humour that dominate social media.

World.title: Cybersecurity at nuclear installations accorded highest priority; AERB, external govt agencies assess security at plants: Centre
World.content:
Chennai: The Union govt on Wednesday informed Lok Sabha that security assessments are conducted periodically at all nuclear power plant sites by the Atomic Energy Regulatory Board (AERB) and âexternal govt agencies.

â

In a written reply to Congress MP Manickam Tagore, minister of state in the Prime Ministerâs Office Jitendra Singh said the plants also conduct internal security assessments. âThe observations made are reviewed, monitored and necessary upgrades are carried out for compliance,â he said.

Tagore had sought details of third-party security audits at nuclear plants, including Kudankulam, and measures to counter threats from drones, cyberattacks and sabotage.

He asked whether any foreign or suspected state-sponsored cyberattack attempts had been detected during the past three years.

The National Alliance of Anti-nuclear Movements urged the Union govt recently to constitute a commission of inquiry to investigate the alleged leak of files related to the Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant. The statement comes in the wake of a ransomware group reportedly publishing hundreds of files linked to the Kudankulam plant which are said to be highly sensitive.





The govt did not directly disclose whether any such foreign or state-sponsored attempts had been detected. It said cybersecurity at nuclear installations was accorded the âhighest priorityâ, with continuous monitoring and surveillance mechanisms in place. Preventive measures include access controls, regular security audits, vulnerability assessments, incident-response mechanisms and capacity-building programmes.

It cited CERT-inâs (Indian Computer Emergency Response Team) role in issuing alerts and advisories, coordinating responses to cyber incidents and operating the National Cyber Coordination Centre.

On physical security, Singh said nuclear power plants were equipped with perimeter intrusion-detection systems, access controls, CCTV surveillance and X-ray baggage inspection facilities. The AERB conducts regulatory inspections covering nuclear security.

Singh said regulatory-approved emergency preparedness plans were in place at every nuclear power plant, including Kudankulam. Exercises involving local administration, security agencies and plant authorities are conducted periodically, and feedback is used to revise and strengthen preparedness plans.

An ICCR exercise was conducted at the Kudankulam nuclear power plant on April 15, 2025.

The govt said all other nuclear power plant sites had conducted their latest ICCR exercises since Sept 2024. At Kalpakkam, an off-site emergency exercise involving the district administration, was conducted on July 17, 2026, with an initiating event from the Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor.

World.title: Singappen Special Force helps 11-year-old boy from Coimbatore continue schooling
World.content:
The Singappen Special Force (SSF) attached to the Coimbatore District (Rural) Police helped a Class 6 student continue his schooling after his mother was unable to support his studies.

The force extended a helping hand to the boy who was left helpless and unable to continue his school education due to family circumstances.

According to the police, the boy from Kuniyamuthur area of Coimbatore was living with his parents and studying in Class 6 at a government school. The boy’s father forced his wife and son out of the house, allegedly due to a family dispute. The mother faced hardship as she could not take proper care his son and send him to school while she went out to work.

The mother approached SSF, seeking help for her son’s education and safety. Upon receiving her request, the SSF team inquired about the boy’s situation. The team helped the woman enrol her son in a residential school at Valparai. The mother expressed her gratitude to the force.

In July, the SSF team enrolled two children in the tribal residential school at Valparai on July 20 after their mother struggled to support their studies following the death of her husband. The force also arranged clothes and study materials for the siblings.

World.title: Research under way at TNAU to refine glycerol obtained from leftover cooking oil
World.content:
Refining of glycerol, a by-product obtained after conversion of leftover cooking oil into biodiesel, for cosmetic applications is on the agenda of researchers in the Department of Renewable Energy Engineering (DREE), Agricultural Engineering College and Research Institute, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU), Coimbatore.

Through transesterification process, leftover cooking oil is being converted into biodiesel with over 90% viscosity vis-a-vis petroleum diesel, but the value of glycerol derived in the crude form has not been tapped.

The glycerol has to be refined for removal of residues. The process warrants extensive research. “We will be working on the processes for purification of glycerol,” D. Ramesh, Head, DREE, said.

Availability of leftover cooking oil for biofuel conversion, though meagre, has improved in the wake of the Food Safety Department keeping a close watch on the inventories of major restaurants to prevent re-use, he said.

The quality of biodiesel derived from leftover cooking oil is superior compared with the product sourced from non-edible oil.

Flanked by P. Rajkumar, Institute Dean, students of the department, on Tuesday, he demonstrated the utility of the biodiesel for lighting lamps, during the course of celebration of World Biofuel Day.

World.title: 1,000 college students form human chain against drug abuse in Coimbatore
World.content:
About 1,000 college students participated in a human chain awareness programme on Race Course road in Coimbatore city on Wednesday to spread awareness on the dangers of drug abuse and to promote the goal of a “Drug-Free Tamil Nadu”.

The students formed the human chain along with Coimbatore District Collector Pavankumar G. Giriyappanavar.

Students from Government Arts and Science College for Women, Puliyakulam; Government Arts and Science College; and Bishop Appasamy College of Arts and Science, Race Course Road, participated in the programme.

Speaking to reporters, Mr. Giriyappanavar said a series of awareness programmes against drug abuse would be conducted across Coimbatore district for a week. The programmes followed the State-wide mass pledge-taking event held on Tuesday in Chennai as part of efforts to achieve a drug-free Tamil Nadu.

World.title: AAP rattled by BJP govt.’s welfare schemes: Sood
World.content:
Delhi Education Minister Ashish Sood on Wednesday dismissed as “baseless” the Aam Aadmi Party’s (AAP) allegations of irregularities in various welfare schemes of the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) government. The Minister said AAP is rattled by the launch of a number of welfare schemes.

This comes amidst allegations by the AAP of scams in the BJP government in procurement of medicines, rice, and bicycles. Meanwhile, the AAP on Wednesday continued to attack the government over the alleged scam in procurement of cycles for a government scheme. The Minister said that there was a narrative by the AAP that if the BJP comes to power then slums will be demolished, but the BJP has actually allowed lakhs of more slum dwellers to be eligible for rehabilitation by amending the DUSIB Act. The Delhi Assembly on Tuesday passed a Bill extending the cut-off date for slum dwellers eligible for rehabilitation to January 1, 2025, from the existing date of January 1, 2006. Mr. Sood also attacked senior AAP leader and Leader of Opposition (LoP) Atishi for not attending the monsoon session of the Assembly. “AAP is completely flustered and trembling with panic after seeing the joyful faces of over 3,000 young girls receiving brand-new bicycles. They are not just scammers, they are daily fabricators of fake percentages. One day they claim (there is a corruption of) Rs. 90 crore, then 75% (commission), then 70%, and then 43%. Their changing figures expose their political desperation,” Mr. Sood said while addressing a press conference. The Minister said that the entire bicycle procurement scheme was executed with complete transparency through the government e-Marketplace (GeM) portal. Mr. Sood said that the AAP had been relentlessly attacking the BJP for not implementing the election promise of ₹2,500 per month for women, but they fled the Assembly session during discussions on the ‘Delhi Lakshmi Yojana’ under which the government is giving the financial aid. He said that in just 16 to 17 months, the BJP government has implemented over 157 major policy interventions. “AAP has failed in its duty as an opposition, fleeing even from discussions on the North-East Delhi riots conviction. Our government operates with zero tolerance to corruption and remains dedicated to serving the citizens of Delhi.” The AAP has been claiming that they bought the same bicycle that the government purchased for ₹6,957 each at each at ₹4,200 each. The government has bought 1.4 lakh bicycles to be distributed to grade 9 girl students of Delhi government schools under the ‘Vidya Vahini Yojana’. “I hope CM Rekha Gupta takes action. Otherwise, all of us will now file a complaint with the ACB (Anti-Corruption Bureau) as well as the CBI (Central Bureau of Investigation). We will not allow Delhi’s children to be looted through their bicycles. We hope that when we file the complaint, the Anti-Corruption Bureau will properly investigate it and take action,” said AAP MLA Sanjeev Jha. AAP Delhi president Saurabh Bharadwaj alleged that the genuine Skyler bicycle they were supposed to purchase for around ₹7,000 has seven gears, suspension and disc brakes. ‘”The bicycle they have supplied under the name Skyler has none of these. It has no gears, no disc brakes and no suspension. They have simply put a fake Skyler sticker on it,” he said.

World.title: Engineering student’s murder in Coimbatore: six arrested, search on for 11
World.content:
Police on Wednesday (August 12) arrested six persons and continued searches for at least 11 others, most of them students of a private college at Othakalmandapam near Coimbatore, in connection with the murder of a student of the institution near the campus on Monday (August 10).

Police said that B. Aaramudhan (20) of Panruti in Cuddalore district, M. Aravind (21) of Manamadurai in Sivaganga district, S. Siva Rohith (20) of Needamangalam in Tiruvarur district, V. Mani Balu (20) of Sathanatham near Kunnam in Perambalur district, a 17-year-old boy from Tiruvallur district, and one Santhosh were arrested in connection with the murder of K. Amuthan (19) of Kallakurichi, a third-year undergraduate student of Hindusthan College of Engineering and Technology. The first four accused are students of the same college, police said.

Police were on the lookout for at least 11 others, including fourth-year student Deepak, who is suspected to have taken the lead in the murder.

As per the statement given by Santhosh to police after his arrest, he was part of a team led by Deepak that assaulted Vanchit and Haridas, second-year students of the college, at a ground near the campus, on the night of August 9. Amudhan and his friend Sriman (19) came to know about the assault on their friends.

To avenge the assault, Amuthan, Vanchit, Haridas and others went to the accommodation of Deepak and others at Othakalmandapam around 5.30 a.m. on Monday and assaulted them. Vanchit and Haridas went to Goa for an industrial visit after the incident, said the police.

The Chettipalayam police registered a case in connection with the incident based on a complaint from a civil engineering student of the college.

According to the police, Deepak and his friends planned to take revenge for the assault. They intercepted Amuthan and Sriman at Malumichampatti around 8.30 a.m. on Monday. They took the duo to the ground behind the campus and assaulted them. Amuthan returned to his accommodation around 10 a.m. and he developed breathing difficulty by 3 p.m. He was rushed to a hospital and died without responding to treatment.

The Chettipalayam police registered a case based on the complaint of Sriman and arrested the six accused.

Faculty from Hindusthan College of Engineering and Technology told media persons on Wednesday that the institution had placed Amuthan and another student, Ajis, under suspension on July 24 for assaulting a cook of their hostel on the campus on July 21. The institution did not have knowledge that Amuthan stayed back in Coimbatore after the suspension. They said the police sought a list of 15 students from the college in connection with the incidents.

World.title: DDA clears Master Plan for Delhi-2047
World.content:
The Delhi Development Authority (DDA) on Wednesday approved the Master Plan for Delhi-2047, extending the target year from 2041 to 2047 after the earlier plan remained pending with the Centre for more than three years.

The plan, approved at a DDA meeting chaired by Lieutenant-Governor Taranjit Singh Sandhu, will now be sent to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs?? for final approval and notification, according to an official statement.

The L-G, who is also the chairperson of the DDA, in a social media post, said the plan would align Delhi’s long-term development with the Centre’s “Viksit Bharat@2047” vision.

A road map for sustainable and inclusive urban growth and improving ease of doing business and ease of living were also discussed in the meeting, the L-G added.

The approval comes after the earlier Master Plan for Delhi-2041 was cleared by the DDA on February 28, 2023, and sent to the Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs (MoHUA) in April that year for notification. It has since missed several deadlines, including a 100-day deadline set by the Centre after the Narendra Modi government took office for a third term.

The latest plan is expected to shape Delhi’s expansion, housing, mobility and environmental management over the next two decades, with the DDA saying it takes an integrated approach to housing, economic growth, transport, infrastructure, environmental sustainability, heritage conservation and urban regeneration.

Delhi’s previous master plan, MPD-2021, had also faced a prolonged delay and was finally notified in 2007, seven years after the intended planning horizon began.

Policies rolled out

Several components linked to Delhi’s long-term development have already been taken up separately while the full master plan remained pending. The Centre notified a new transit-oriented development policy in April, paving the way for higher-density construction around metro corridors. The government has also decided to regularise 1,511 unauthorised colonies on an “as-is-where-is” basis.

The 2047 plan will also address some of the city’s long-standing planning challenges, including the proposed land pooling policy in outer Delhi, the Green Development Area policy, and the future of unauthorised colonies in the Yamuna O-Zone, officials said.

The O-Zone, an ecologically sensitive floodplain, has more than five lakh residents living in unauthorised colonies.

In May, the Delhi High Court held that residential colonies could not legally exist in the area, adding another layer to the question of how these settlements will be dealt with under the city’s long-term planning framework.

The DDA said the Master Plan 2047 takes into account the projected growth in Delhi’s population and seeks to provide a framework for housing, infrastructure, mobility and environmental management as the capital expands towards 2047.

Approvals eased

The DDA also approved amendments to the Unified Building Bye-Laws (UBBL), 2016, aimed at reducing the number of prior clearances required for building permits in the authority meeting, for “ease of doing business”.

Under the changes, applicants will no longer have to obtain separate no-objection certificates from the Delhi Pollution Control Committee, Chief Inspector of Factories, Delhi Jal Board and Forest Department as a precondition for obtaining building permits. The move is intended to reduce compliance requirements and simplify the building-plan approval process.

A senior official said, “The applicant will need to self-certify through the portal and the independent third-party auditor will approve the proposal. The third-party auditor in this case, the official added, will be the government authority’s empanelled architect who will approve that the building plan complies with rules like floor area ratio and other criteria.”

It also approved a policy allowing reconstruction and redevelopment of DDA-built two-storey dwelling units on individual plots in older housing schemes, including at Naraina Vihar. The policy will apply to similarly placed DDA housing schemes across Delhi.

World.title: Agricultural scientists of KVKs across T.N., Puducherry study carbon credit models at ‘green sites’ in Tiruppur
World.content:
A delegation of agricultural scientists representing KVKs (Krishi Vigyan Kendra) across Tamil Nadu and Puducherry on Wednesday (August 12) studied the carbon credit models at the ‘green sites’ developed under Vanathukkul Tiruppur agroforestry initiative by Vetry environmental organisation.

The 35 participating scientists taking part in the two-day capacity-building programme on Carbon Farming encompassed experts from key domains, such as soil science, agronomy, and horticulture.

The programme organised by the Indian Council of Agricultural Research - Agricultural Technology Application Research Institute (ICAR-ATARI) Zone X, Hyderabad; Tamil Nadu Agricultural University (TNAU) Directorate of Extension Education; and the university’s Forest College and Research Institute (FC&RI), Mettupalayam, envisaged brainstorming sessions on analysing soil-moisture retention, crop combinations, biomass generation, and pest resilience.

The main interaction took place at Glenmorgan Farm in Chengapalli, Natraj Muthusamy, CEO of VETRY NGO, said.

Farm owners Kumarasamy and Soundarya Vadivel, showcased the agroforestry interventions. The scientists were shown teak farm developed with precision farming technique developed by the FC&RI for maximum volume growth.

Dedicated trial plots nurtured by the Institute of Forest Genetics and Tree Breeding (IFGTB) enabled evaluation of the field adaptation of Punnai (Calophyllum inophyllum) and newly developed, elite Neem varieties.

The scientists learnt about the project undertaken by the Vetri organisation for planning 25 lakh trees over 11 years, involving local communities in rural parts of Tiruppur district with the promise of economic uplift and financial security through initiation into silvopasture models, combining timber growth with livestock grazing.

The scientists explored practical frameworks for integrating scattered agroforestry plots into international carbon credit markets, and appreciated the high survival rates, and robust data tracking.

World.title: Ahead of I-Day, DMRC issues advisory against kite flying near elevated corridors
World.content:
Ahead of Independence Day, the Delhi Metro Rail Corporation (DMRC) on Wednesday issued an advisory urging the public against flying kites near elevated metro lines to avoid entanglement of kite strings with Over Head Equipment (OHE) wires, which might prove fatal. “Delhi Metro has around 25,000 Volts of live wires along its 416 km long elevated stretch as Over Head Equipment (OHE). These live wires run parallel to the tracks for powering the trains for daily passenger services. Kite strings getting entangled in these OHE wires can not only disrupt train services but also can be fatal for those flying kites with metallic manjhas,” said a DMRC official. The advisory comes ahead of the Independence Day on August 15, when kite flying increases significantly in Delhi and the National Capital Region. The official further added that DMRC has dedicated teams deployed near kite prone stations to swiftly remove the kite strings as and when spotted besides advising the train operators and station staff to be more cautious.

Chinese manjha seized

Delhi Police recovered around 1,398 reels of banned Chinese kite string reels from a car in west Delhi, officials said on Wednesday. Police arrested three people identified as Rajesh (33), Asad (23) and Sohail (19), seized the vehicle used for transporting the reels and registered a case.

World.title: 'We aspire for it to grow': Turkiye's Erdogan eyes expansion of Makkah Joint Defence Agreement
World.content:
Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan said on Wednesday that he hoped more countries would join a defence agreement signed last week between Turkiye, Saudi Arabia and Pakistan, aimed at stabilising a region wracked by conflict.

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement was signed on Friday as the Middle East grapples with fallout from the US-Iran war, which has dragged in regional players and disrupted shipping through the Strait of Hormuz and the Red Sea.

“Our vision for it is not limited to the three countries,” the Turkish leader told the London-based Asharq Al-Awsat daily. “Rather we aspire for it to grow, and perhaps appropriate conditions will emerge one day for all countries of the region to gather under its umbrella.”

Turkish Foreign Minister Hakan Fidan on Saturday said Turkiye expected Egypt to join the pact “in the next stage”, telling the Anadolu state news agency only “a few technical issues” stood in the way.

Egypt has not commented on the agreement nor on the remarks by Fidan, who will visit Cairo on Thursday and Friday.

Cairo has robust military cooperation with Ankara, but has given no indication it intends to sign up to the new security alliance, which contains a Nato-style clause saying any attack on one would be seen as an attack on all.

The five-month US-Iran war has upended the security architecture in the region and forced a rethink of decades of conventional wisdom rooted in US military supremacy.

Erdogan said the pact emerged out of the “new circumstances” in the Middle East with regional players seeking to assume greater responsibility for their own security and stability.

“Regional issues should be resolved by regional actors, and with this action, we consider that we have taken a first step toward achieving that goal,” he told the Saudi-owned newspaper.

“Resolving regional issues must be carried out away from formulas imposed from the outside. We know very well that solutions imported from abroad only bring disasters.”

The Makkah Joint Defence Agreement has been hailed by the 57-member Organisation of Islamic Cooperation (OIC) as an “important strategic step”.

Kuwait , Bahrain and Somalia are among the countries that have welcomed it. Iran’s comments also took a rather positive tone, stressing its stance of pursuing “security mechanisms based on cooperation between regional countries”.

On Monday, Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif affirmed that the defence pact was “entirely for defensive purposes”, and not for any aggression.

Addressing the federal cabinet on Monday, PM Shehbaz stressed that the objective of the pact is to “promote peace, progress, and prosperity in the region”.

While the pact comes in the backdrop of the US-Israel war on Iran, Bloomberg had reported in January — before the conflict began — that Ankara was seeking to join a separate mutual defence pact between Islamabad and Riyadh.

Pakistan and Saudi Arabia had already signed the “ Strategic Mutual Defence Agreement ” in Riyadh last September, pledging that any attack on either nation would be treated as an act of aggression against both.

In January, Reuters quoted Defence Production Minister Raza Hayat Harraj as saying that a draft had been prepared after 10 months of talks. Turkish FM Hakan Fidan had said Ankara favoured an “inclusive platform that creates wider, bigger cooperation and stability”.

Pakistan has also sought to mediate efforts to end the US-Iran war, while Turkiye has played a diplomatic role in negotiations aimed at ending the war in Gaza.

Israel ‘removing Palestine’ from world agenda

Erdogan also accused the Israeli government of Benjamin Netanyahu of seeking to “remove Palestine” from the world’s agenda.

“The aim of the Netanyahu government is to remove Palestine from the common agenda of humanity by profiting from chaos and new conflicts in the region,” Erdogan said at a joint news conference with his Palestinian counterpart, Mahmoud Abbas.

“No matter what they do, they will not succeed. The Palestinian cause will continue to grow in people’s hearts as they try to destroy it,” he stressed, vowing Turkiye would fight for the establishment of a Palestinian state.

A strong advocate of the Palestinian cause, Erdogan has repeatedly lambasted Netanyahu’s government, accusing the Israeli prime minister of committing “genocide” in Gaza and of pursuing expansionist policies in the West Bank, Lebanon, Syria and beyond.

Abbas arrived in Ankara on Tuesday accompanied by his diplomatic adviser Majdi Khalidi, intelligence chief Majed Faraj and senior Palestinian official Ziad Abu Amr.

He met Erdogan on Wednesday with the pair discussing developments in the region in talks the Palestinian leader described as “important and fruitful”.

“I hope the decision to hold legislative and presidential elections in Palestine after a long time will bring good fortune … [and] will advance the reconciliation process,” Erdogan said, in a nod to the historic rivalry between Abbas’ Fatah movement and Gaza’s Hamas rulers.

Abbas also hailed the defence pact between Ankara, Riyadh and Islamabad, saying it was “of utmost importance” and expressing hope it would help enhance security and stability in the region.

World.title: Govt cuts petrol price by Re0.94, raises high-speed diesel by Re0.54
World.content:
The government on Wednesday reduced the price of petrol by Re0.94 and increased the price of high-speed diesel (HSD) by Re0.54 per litre.

Following the revision, petrol will retail at Rs324.98 per litre while HSD will cost Rs382.79 per litre. The government continues to levy Rs114 per litre in taxes and duties on petrol and Rs100 per litre on HSD.

According to the Petroleum Division’s notification, the new prices will be applicable for August 13 (Thursday).

The price of HSD has come down from a peak of Rs520.35 recorded on April 3. Its price had started rising from Rs281 per litre after the US-Iran war broke out on February 28.

The petrol price had peaked at Rs458.41 on April 3 after beginning its upward trajectory from Rs266 in the first week of March.

Earlier, Petroleum Minister Ali Pervaiz Malik announced that fuel prices would now be fixed on a daily basis due to fluctuations in international market prices following renewed hostilities between Iran and the US.

The government had been announcing weekly revisions to fuel prices since early March, alongside measures for the conservation of fuel amid possible oil supply disruptions due to the ongoing conflict in the Middle East. The federal government in April also announced targeted relief measures to provide subsidised fuel.

The petroleum minister stated that the cabinet and the prime minister had decided to give the Oil and Gas Regulatory Authority (Ogra) the responsibility of deciding fuel prices on a daily basis based on international market trends.

The daily pricing decision was rejected by the All Pakistan Dealers Association, which said it would consider a protest plan.

Petrol is mainly used in private transport, small vehicles, rickshaws and two-wheelers, and changes in its price affect the middle and lower-middle classes.

Similarly, changes in diesel prices also impact the public at large, as it is mainly used in the heavy transport sector, power plants and large generators.

Petrol and high-speed diesel (HSD) are the major revenue earners, with monthly sales of about 700,000 to 800,000 tonnes, compared to just 10,000 tonnes of monthly demand for kerosene.

World.title: After death of 3 Pakistani sailors, FO says Islamabad will implement maritime coalition 'in full earnest'
World.content:
The Foreign Office (FO) said on Wednesday that Pakistan, as a signatory to the recently announced multinational maritime defence coalition, would implement its commitments “in full earnest”.

The statement comes following the deaths of three Pakistani sailors in Houthi strikes on a Saudi cargo ship on Tuesday.

Last month, Riyadh unveiled plans for a multinational maritime defence coalition to protect shipping and energy supply routes in the Red Sea region. Fourteen countries, including Pakistan, Turkiye and Egypt, backed the coalition in a joint statement.

Answering questions at a weekly press briefing, FO spokesperson Tahir Andrabi elaborated that Pakistan was a signatory of the recent joint statement supporting a multinational maritime defence coalition, led by Saudi Arabia, to protect shipping and energy supply routes.

“Pakistan is a signatory to this maritime coalition communique and we will implement it with full earnest,” Andrabi said, adding that the country was engaged with the Saudi authorities in this regard.

Andrabi further said that on the directions of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar, Pakistan was ascertaining the details of the agreement.

In his opening statement, the FO also said that Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi’s visit to Iran was aimed at discussing bilateral relations, security-related matters and regional developments, particularly peace and stability in the region.

He said Naqvi — who arrived in Tehran on Tuesday — was holding meetings with senior Iranian officials.

He added that the visit provides the two countries the opportunity to discuss “bilateral relations, security-related matters, and regional development, with a particular focus on efforts to promote peace, stability, and constructive engagement amongst the parties in the region and regional developments”.

Naqvi was received in Tehran by his Iranian counterpart, Eskandar Momeni, and later held talks with Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi and Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkian, Iranian media reported.

A diplomatic source had told Dawn from Tehran that the principal objective of Naqvi’s visit was to follow up on the Islamabad Memorandum of Understanding and Pakistan’s mediation bet­­w­een Iran and the US.

Speaking further on Pakistan’s mediation efforts between the US and Iran, Andrabi reiterated that Pakistan remained engaged alongside “brotherly states” in “sincere efforts” to work towards a resolution to the crisis.

“Pakistan is making all-out efforts to bring the two parties to the negotiating table and the Islamabad MoU and pave the way for peace and stability in the region,” he said.

He also warned that Pakistan would continue to “offset spoilers using direct and indirect channels” and ensure the continuation of constructive dialogue to resolve outstanding issues.

During the Q&A session, responding to a question regarding the status of the Islamabad MoU, the spokesperson said, “Whenever the rationality for dialogue will overcome the logic of escalation, the template for peace is provided in the Islamabad MoU and Pakistan-Qatar joint statement.”

The current deadline for the 60-day period for US-Iran negotiations under the Islamabad MoU is Aug 17. Andrabi, however, noted that this deadline “can always be extended” if there is the intention to hold dialogue.

“Even then, five days still remain, so we are not closing the chapter,” he added. “But we hope that even if the deadline is not implemented, the extension will take place eventually and the parties will revert to dialogue.”

Asked about the basis for Pakistan’s continued optimism amid the US-Iran conflict, the spokesperson said, “As a mediator and facilitator of talks, we remain optimistic that a solution is in sight.”

He pointed out that during the conflict, the countries had cycled through periods of heightened escalation followed by relative calm and eventual dialogue. He termed this “the natural progression of any armed conflict of international significance”.

“We are not discouraged by escalations, as much as we do not get overly optimistic when there is a period of calm,” he said, while highlighting Pakistan’s sustained engagement with the parties to resolve the conflict.

The country would continue its engagement with optimism “that ought to be there in any credible facilitator and mediator”, he added.

Makkah pact reflects ‘resolve for sharing burden of regional peace’

The FO spokesperson also spoke of the defence pact signed last week between Pakistan, Saudi Arabia and Turkiye, which he said was “highlight of the week”.

The joint defence agreement, signed in Makkah on Friday, aims to strengthen collective deterrence and empowers its signatory states to treat an attack against one of them as an attack against all of them.

He said the agreement reflected the three nations’ “commitment to further strengthen their collective security, promoting peace security and promoting peace security and stability in the region and beyond”.

He said the agreement reflected the “long-standing brotherly relations” among the three countries and “displays our resolve for sharing the burden of regional peace and security”.

“The agreement is purely defensive in nature and allows unified efforts to confront threats and security challenges to the member states,” Andrabi added, recalling Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar’s statement congratulating the nation on the agreement on August 10, wherein he held the agreement was defensive in nature and not against any country.

Responding to a question, he noted that while the agreement was open to other countries, he was not “particularly aware” of which specific countries may join it in the future. He also said that he was not aware of any consultations with the US and China regarding the agreement, calling this “a matter of diplomatic exchange”, but noted that channels of communication with both countries remained open.

FO rejects Indian MEA’s ‘baseless’ remarks on AJK

When asked about the Indian Ministry of External Affairs’ recent remarks regarding alleged human rights abuses in Azad Jammu and Kashmir (AJK), the FO spokesperson rejected the “baseless” statement. The region has been gripped by unrest since early June as elections are also being held.

“India’s professed concerns for human rights in AJK are disingenuous given its own well-documented record for repression in Indian Illegally Occupied Jammu and Kashmir, including excessive use of force, arbitrary detention, suppression of political freedom and sweeping powers under the draconian laws enacted there.”

He added that India’s “politicisation” of developments in AJK was “misleading and cannot divert attention from the stark realities in Indian illegally occupied Kashmir”.

“Pakistan remains fully committed to the protection of fundamental rights and the democratic freedom of AJK,” he said.

He added that rather than making such statements over AJK, India would be “well advised to honour commitments made by its founding fathers and uphold the right of the people of Indian illegally occupied Jammu and Kashmir to freely determine their future through a United Nations plebiscite in accordance with relevant UN Security Council resolutions”.

World.title: Met Office forecasts fresh rain spell for upper, central parts of country from Aug 13-15
World.content:
The upper and central parts of the country are set to receive a fresh spell of monsoon rains from August 13 to 15, the Pakistan Meteorological Department (PMD) said on Wednesday.

In an advisory, the Met Office said monsoon currents were penetrating the upper parts of the country along with a westerly wave.

In Kashmir, it forecast rain accompanied by wind and thundershowers in Neelum Valley, Muzaffarabad, Rawalakot, Poonch, Hattian, Bagh, Haveli, Sudhanoti, Kotli, Bhimber and Mirpur. In Gilgit-Baltistan, the Met Office predicted rain in Diamir, Astore, Ghizer, Skardu, Hunza, Gilgit, Ghanche and Shigar.

In upper Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP), Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Malakand, Shangla, Battagram, Mansehra, Abbottabad, Galiyat, Buner, Bajaur, Mohmand, Peshawar, Nowshera, Mardan, Swabi, Haripur, Kurram and Khyber are expected to receive rain.

In northeast Punjab, rainfall was predicted in Murree, Sialkot, Narowal, Mandi Bahauddin, Gujrat, Gujranwala, Hafizabad, Wazirabad, Lahore, Kasur, Sheikhupura and Nankana Sahib from the night of August 12 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

Rain-wind and thundershowers, with a few heavy falls, are also expected in Islamabad, Rawalpindi and the Pothohar region from the night of August 13 to August 15, with occasional gaps.

In Sargodha, Faisalabad, Jhang, Toba Tek Singh, Khushab, Layyah, Bhakkar, Noorpur Thal, Sahiwal, Pakpattan, Bahawalnagar, Bahawalpur, Dera Ghazi Khan, Zhob, Barkhan and Musakhel, the Met Office predicted rainfall from August 12 to 15.

Meanwhile, in Sindh, partly cloudy to cloudy weather is expected in the southeastern and coastal areas, with chances of rain-wind/thundershowers in Tharparkar, Umerkot and Sanghar districts on August 12 and 13.

Elsewhere in Sindh, hot and humid weather is expected to persist.

The Met Office warned of urban flooding in low-lying areas of Islamabad, Rawalpindi, Mardan, Swabi, Gujranwala, Gujrat, Sialkot and Lahore during the forecast period.

It also indicated the possibility of landslides in vulnerable areas of upper KP, including Dir, Chitral, Swat, Kohistan, Buner, Battagram, Mansehra, Haripur and Abbottabad, as well as in GB, Murree, Galiyat and Kashmir.

The Met Office advised tourists to exercise caution, while farmers were urged to manage crop activities in accordance with weather conditions.

According to the National Disaster Management Authority (NDMA), 155 people have lost their lives and 460 have been injured in rain-related incidents in the current monsoon season.

Monsoon rains fall across the region from June to September, offering respite from the summer heat and are crucial to replenishing water supplies.

However, heavy downpours also trigger deadly floods, landslides and displacement, particularly in vulnerable, poorly drained, or densely populated areas.

World.title: AJK polls: Rathore’s LA-17 Haveli victory disputed, local PML-N announces indefinite strike
World.content:
MUZAFFARABAD: A controversy emerged on Wednesday after the returning officer (RO) issued Form 27 declaring PPP’s Faisal Mumtaz Rathore, the sitting AJK prime minister, the winner from LA-17 (Haveli), despite rival PML-N candidate Engineer Mohsin Aziz being assured that the form would not be issued until the Election Commission took up his complaint.

The development triggered fresh tensions in Haveli district, where PML-N workers announced a complete shutter-down strike and protest from Thursday (August 13) for an indefinite period.

At a meeting in Forward Kahuta, chaired by PML-N Haveli president Syed Abid Bukhari, participants demanded that the Election Commission open all polling bags from LA-17, order a recount and determine the result on the basis of the original results issued by presiding officers at the polling stations.

They warned that the scope of the protest would be expanded if the demand was not accepted.

Polling in the constituency had been held on Monday amid serious allegations and counter-allegations of rigging by all three major contestants — PM Rathore of PPP, PML-N’s Aziz and independent candidate Khawaja Tariq Saeed.

Late on Monday evening, thousands of Aziz’s supporters gathered at the district courts, claiming that the results provided to polling agents by presiding officers on Form 24 showed their candidate leading Rathore by more than 8,000 votes, but that the RO was subsequently preparing the result in favour of the prime minister.

There were also reports of some people being injured during the demonstration.

The protest ended on Tuesday after Aziz said in a video message that the RO had given him a written undertaking that Form 27 would not be issued until the Election Commission in Muzaffarabad decided his claim.

On Tuesday, Chief Election Commissioner Justice (retd) Ghulam Mustafa Mughal had told Dawn that the Commission would take a decision after the polling bags and relevant election records reached its office. He had reportedly given a similar assurance to Aziz over the phone.

The DRO, Waheed Mughal, and RO, Asheer Chughtai, both members of the subordinate judiciary, were evacuated from their offices in Forward Kahuta along with the polling bags with the help of the army’s Quick Response Force (QRF). They reached Muzaffarabad by midnight.

However, the RO subsequently issued Form 27 after midnight, dated August 11, declaring Rathore the winner with 33,872 votes. Aziz secured 32,354 votes, followed by Saeed with 12,538 and IPP candidate Amir Nazir Chaudhry with 5,405.

Hours later, PM Rathore said on X that his “remarkable victory had been officially notified”.

“LA-17 has spoken. I thank the people of Haveli and again pledge to serve them now and forever. I’m grateful to my party leadership, specially, Chairman Bilawal Bhutto Zardari and Adi Faryal Talpur, for their trust, guidance and unending support amid every challenge we have faced,” he wrote.

The issuance of Form 27, however, failed to settle the dispute, with reports from Haveli suggesting that tensions were rising again.

In a video message recorded in Muzaffarabad, Aziz reiterated his allegation that the Form 24s handed to polling agents of all nine participating candidates contained the genuine results, while different figures were subsequently taken into consideration by the RO.

He offered to have just two polling bags, rather than all of them, opened from areas where he alleged the results had been changed. If his allegation proved to be wrong, he said, he would apologise and congratulate Rathore.

“If Faisal Rathore has won, why is he afraid of opening of polling bags and a subsequent recount?” he asked.

Aziz also claimed that the Election Act, 2020, made it obligatory for the RO to open polling bags following a complaint by any candidate. He said that when they asked Chughtai to take the step, the RO maintained that he was unaware of the provision and did not have a copy of the Act with him.

On Wednesday, senior lawyers Raja Sajjad Ahmed and Chaudhry Ghulam Nabi submitted an application to the chief election commissioner, seeking a recount of votes polled in LA-17 over alleged tampering with the results.

The Election Commission announced that it would take up the matter at 10am on Thursday.

In a post on X, PML-N leader and federal Minister for Parliamentary Affairs Tariq Fazal Chaudhry called for a transparent investigation into the rigging complaint filed by Aziz, saying he hoped the Election Commission would address the allegations regarding the Haveli constituency on merit.

Aziz, however, said he had little hope from the commission after what he described as its failure to prevent the issuance of the “unlawful Form 27”.

“I will take my case to the people’s court apart from the superior judiciary,” he said.

Meanwhile, Saeed also alleged tampering with his results and called for a recount. He claimed that he had won at nine polling stations, but the votes secured by him there had not been included in his tally and had instead been added to that of Rathore.

PPP calls polls ‘rigged and violent’

Against this backdrop, the PPP also criticised the conduct of the AJK elections, with a high-level meeting of the party in Islamabad describing the polls as “rigged and violent” and expressing serious concern over the role of the AJK Election Commission.

The meeting, chaired by PPP Women’s Wing president and AJK affairs in-charge Faryal Talpur, also criticised the phase-wise conduct of the elections and demanded the immediate completion of polling in the remaining two districts of the third phase and seven constituencies of Poonch so that the Legislative Assembly could be fully constituted.

The participants raised questions over the suspension of internet services, shortages of polling material and staff at some polling stations, and alleged inadequate security arrangements.

Talpur said the PPP was the representative party of the people of AJK and had continued to enjoy strong public support despite challenging circumstances.

On the other hand, Tariq Fazal Chaudhry said the PML-N had secured a clear lead in the elections and would have 24 general seats, with another six reserved seats, taking its strength to 30.

In his post on X, he said the AJK Assembly session would be convened next week for the swearing-in of members and election of reserved seats, followed by elections for the speaker and prime minister.

Chaudhry described the elections as free, fair and credible, saying there had been “zero tolerance” for misconduct or rigging. He cited the arrest of a candidate in LA-6 (Mirpur) for taking away a ballot box from a polling station as an example of action against electoral misconduct.

World.title: Awaam Pakistan calls ECP delisting ‘unwarranted’, seeks urgent hearing
World.content:
ISLAMABAD: Headed by former prime minister Shahid Khaqan Abbasi, Awaam Pakistan has challenged the Election Commission of Pakistan’s (ECP) decision to delist the party over its alleged failure to hold intra-party elections, calling the move “arbitrary, unwarranted and unprecedented”.

In a letter to Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja dated August 12, 2026, Abbasi, who is also the party’s president, said Awaam Pakistan had been “taken by surprise” by an ECP notification issued on August 7. The notification cited an ECP order dated Aug 3, 2026, in a case titled “Non-Conduct of intra-party election by Awaam Pakistan”.

Abbasi said the party had conducted intra-party elections for both the National General Council and national office-bearers between March 26 and April 2, 2026. He said the polls were held within the extension granted by the ECP in its decision of January 2026.

“The results of the intra-party election and detailed documentation were submitted to the ECP on April 6, 2026,” the letter said.

He added that 12,846 party members participated in the exercise, which was “democratic, transparent, and in full compliance with the Elections Act, 2017.”

Terming the delisting “in contradiction of the record available with the ECP”, Abbasi said the action was taken “without an opportunity to be heard by the Election Commission”.

“We request an urgent hearing by the commission so that we can clarify our position,” he wrote.

While Article 17 of the Constitution guarantees the right to form political parties, enlistment with the ECP is a legal requirement for obtaining an election symbol to contest polls.

Under Section 202 of the Elections Act, 2017, a party must apply for enlistment within 30 days of formation.
